A tool result whose `details` carry `keep: false` (web search, §21.6) is held in memory only and never written to the app's own storage.

### 7.7 Sessions and the record

A Harness run is a recURd run, recorded natively rather than through hooks (DESIGN §16.7's table gains a row, Appendix D):

- Each Pi session entry (`message`, `model_change`, `usage`, `compaction`, `branch_summary`, `custom`) is a record entry in the author's vault, sealed per DESIGN §16.8, its `id` and `parentId` kept, so the tree branches as Pi's file does. Coverage is complete by construction: no transcript to tail, no hook to miss. Since CO-25 nothing a model read or wrote is left out: each entry is a `session_entry`, its large parts `session_blob` entries, and each call's context rebuilds exactly (§24).
- Model calls are `model_call` entries with attestation (§6.8); tool calls are `tool_call` entries naming the message that holds the result and its `details` whole (§24.4); approvals are I-8's entries.
- **Resume** reads the run's entries back from the vault; **fork** and **clone** start a new run whose first entry names the old one's entry; a run continues on another of the member's devices from the vault, their agents' enclaves among them (§24.7). `ur harness export <run>` writes Pi's JSONL v3, which Pi and PiG can open.
- Redaction before seal (DESIGN §16.7) applies to every entry, as to any run.
- A web search's entry is a stub: the call, the number of results and a hash of the answer, not the results, which are not stored (CO-26; §21.6, Q-SRCH-9); CO-25 leaves it a stub (§24.9).
- An enclave's runs are its sponsor's: an agents' enclave, one of their devices, writes them into the member's vault as any of their devices does, each call's entries as the call is made (§11.4, §24.5).

### 7.8 Approvals and taint

- **O tools** (`enclave_create`; any DESIGN §16.5 O tool the profile includes) call `Sidecar.Authorize` (DESIGN §5.4) from the tool's before-hook; the agent waits on `approval_pending` until a person decides on an approval-capable device, as any O call does.
- **Untrusted input** taints the run (I-9) and the Harness marks it between untrusted-data markers in the model's context: inbox messages per §20.7; a remote agent's answers, from a tainted run there or from an enclave that is not the member's own (Q-HARN-8), and commands on the attach link whose origin is not trusted (7.10); launch instructions, prompts, steers and follow-ups from a tainted run, and a tainted local child's answers (7.9); a record entry a tagged sidecar other than the member's own enclave wrote (IC-12); `evs_read` of versions whose provenance is untrusted (DESIGN §16.6), and the bundled `git`'s `clone`, `fetch` and `pull`, or any of its commands that fetches an object lazily, when a push it takes objects from shows a tainted run, a tagged sidecar other than the member's own enclave or another member, or no provenance it can read, the run tainted before the worktree is written or the command answers (§13.6), so what it brought in is read only in a tainted run; `ssh_exec` and `bash` output, since an enclave reaches the internet, and in the enclave profile every tool that reads or runs in the agents' container, the file tools and `git` included, from the moment it starts, so that whatever the call pushes carries the bit, since what they read comes from a container whose agents reach the internet (§11.10); `web_fetch`; `web_search` results; outside mail (`mail_list`, `mail_read`), calendar events (`calendar_list`, §23.9) and connected services' results (`service_call`, §25.10); any result whose tool says `Trust: untrusted`. A tainted run loses send, forward and publish until a person approves on another approval-capable device or with a presence key (I-9; [owner decision 142](DESIGN.md#od-142)). For this document's kinds 23-26, the device's safety classifier may approve first in auto mode (CO-40, §27).
- **Sending out of a tainted run.** A tainted run may not move what it read past the device by another door: `ssh_exec` and `enclave_exec` to an enclave whose egress is not `none` become O, since the command and its stdin can carry anything to the internet, and to another member's enclave whatever its egress, since the text leaves the member; `agent_launch`, `agent_prompt` and `agent_send` to an agent in such an enclave, and an `agent_broadcast` that reaches one, become O for the same reason, since there a receiver's taint stops nothing its `bash` sends (7.10); `agent_send`, `agent_prompt` and `agent_broadcast` to another member's agent become O, since the text leaves the member; all as DESIGN makes `mail_send` W only for an untainted run, and all as one outward kind, 24 `tainted_send` (§16.3), at every entry point, the `ur` commands of §16.3's row included; so is `harness_continue` into such an enclave when the calling run is tainted or a node it continues is flagged or untrusted (7.10), and no evs or git write reaches an inbox (§20.4). So no tool or command that messages, runs a command or moves a context leaves a tainted run a door. An `agent_send` that lands in the agents repo, a reply in a `*` thread, reaches every enclave the member sponsors, as a broadcast does. Wherever kind 24 turns on an enclave's egress, an enclave whose egress is `none` counts as one whose egress is not `none` when a rule lets it dial another device's services: a `listener:` grant, the listeners rule's default for tagged sources among them, or a `dial` rule to a member's device (§26.7), since a listed service, a container runtime's or a notebook's API among them, can act on the internet for it.
- **The EVS door** (Q-HARN-10). What a tainted run writes into EVS otherwise, a summary, a status line or a file in a repo an enclave syncs, is an in-network write that every reader takes as untrusted; but there too a receiver's taint stops nothing its `bash` sends, so an enclave whose egress is not `none` holds such a version back. Its daemon, outside the agents' container, holds from the container, and from every run there without the `private` mark (below), every version whose push's provenance shows a tainted run, or none it can read, other than pushes from the agents' containers of the member's enclaves that reach out, by runs without that mark, which carry nothing such a container could not send already: its agents' files, their `git` and `evs_*` reads, their `agent_*` answers and their context see the path as of its last version not held, marked `held`. A release is kind 24 (§16.3), its sender the run that wrote the version: an agent that meets `held` may ask for it, its request naming only the versions' refs, and the sponsor may release from the enclave's card (`ur enclave release <name>`); the sponsor's device builds the action from the versions it reads itself, its card showing each whole as untrusted text, and its effect is a version of the enclave's settings in the vault naming them, which only a device of the sponsor that is no enclave writes (§11.4). An enclave whose egress is `none`, and that no rule lets dial another device's services, takes them unheld, as untrusted input (7.10). What remains is §2.7's residual: what an untainted run writes, or the person releases, an enclave's agent may still send out.
- **Private data in an enclave** (CO-43, Q-HARN-11). An agents' enclave is one of its sponsor's devices, so its Harness's tools reach what their devices hold; but in an enclave that reaches out (its egress not `none`, or a rule letting it dial another device's services, as above), an agent's `bash` sends whatever its run holds to the internet outside every gate. So there a run holds the sponsor's private data or the agents' container, not both. A run that, anywhere, reads mail, calendar events or a connected service (`mail_list`, `mail_read`, `calendar_list` and the calendar writes, `connections_list`, `service_call` and the typed tools), or, through `evs_*`, `search` or `record_query`, the mailbox, a file of the vault or a recorded node that carries the mark, takes the mark `private`, which, like taint, it never loses, which follows the work as taint does (7.9), and which its session entries carry, so a continuation or fork that takes a marked node has it (`marks`, §24.5); on a device the mark restricts nothing and only travels with the run. A marked run calls no tool that runs in or reads the agents' container (`bash`, the file tools, `git`, `ssh_exec`, a `pig` session), and a run that has called one makes no such read and takes in no marked run's answer or node, each refused with `private_container`, unless the person approves the crossing: kind 24, its card showing what the run holds (`ContextFields`, §16.3), which the safety classifier never decides (§27.7). A marked run works as a local run does: the gates above and §22.5's fetch rule bind it, and what it writes into EVS, tainted where mail or a service tainted it, waits behind the hold above before the container reads it. Other repos, the agents repo and the agent repos among them, are no private data here: the container's runs read every repo the sponsor reads but the vault and the mailbox, which the enclave's disclosure says (§2.8). In an enclave that does not reach out, the mark restricts nothing.
- **Searching** is not an outward action, even in a tainted run: a query goes to Parallel's gateway, not to a host an injected instruction chose. What it could leak is text into Parallel's logs and training data, so the tool refuses a query that matches the record's redaction patterns (§21.6, §21.9); but a tainted run's queries also choose which pages become listed, which widens §22.5's residual, and if the gateway fetches on demand a URL a query names, a search would reach the host the run chose: until G-SRCH-parallel settles that (§21.5), a tainted run's search whose objective or queries name a URL or host it may not fetch is refused (§22.5).
- **Fetching** a listed URL is R; in the local profile, a URL the agent composed is R in an untainted run and outward action 23 in a tainted one, since it could carry what the run read to the host it names, and a tainted run's other fetches without approval stop at 10 a turn its person drives; in an enclave, whose agents reach the internet anyway, the egress mode governs (§22.5).
- **Calendar writes** are W in an untainted run and outward action 25 in a tainted one, and for any event with attendees, whose invitations, updates and cancellations are mail to other people; one approval covers a call's batch, each event shown and switchable (§23.9).
- **Connected services** (§25.10): reads are R and taint; once the person has connected the service, every other call is W in an untainted run, sends included (CO-40), and outward action 26 in a tainted one, where a send and any call other than `GET` and `HEAD` that the service's definition does not classify always go to a person (§27.4); `service_call` refuses the paths a typed tool owns, so the calendar's writes keep kind 25's cards.
- **Spending** is not an outward action per call: a remote call spends within the agent's budget (§16.4), and a budget raise is (`compute_budget_raise`, §16.3).
- **Automatic approvals** (CO-40, §27): where a bullet above makes an action outward only because its run is tainted, kinds 23, 24, 25 and 26 in their tainted cases, the device's safety classifier decides first in the person's auto mode, the default: when it finds nothing injected in what tainted the run or in what the action would send, and none of §27.7's rules holds, the action goes ahead, signed by the device as an automatic decision and recorded; otherwise, and for every approval that exists for another reason, a person decides as above (§27.4).

### 7.9 Agents launching agents

`agent_launch(name, model, instructions, tools?, where?, budget?)` starts a child agent: `where` is `local` (in this Harness) or `enclave:<name>` (in that enclave's Harness, over the attach link's management mode, 7.10, through which `agent_prompt`, `agent_wait` and `agent_stop` also reach the other agents there the person may reach). The model is any catalog id the policy allows the child (R-HARN-3), from `models_list` (7.5), and the launch checks it as the router will (§6.4) before the child starts, by the rules of the Harness that will run it (an enclave's are its sponsor's, §11.4): a model the floor, the provider list or the person's `allow` refuses fails the launch with `model_refused`, and one labeled `none` whose provider's disclosure the person has not acknowledged raises the `disclosure` request in the launching run when the person is attached to it, and otherwise fails the launch with `disclosure_required`, so the launching agent can pick another model or tell the person (§2.8); the child's own calls pass the router again. The child registers its name (§20.5), starts with the recURd skill, and runs its own loop; `agent_prompt` sends it a prompt or steers it, `agent_wait` blocks the parent until the child settles and returns its last message, and `agent_stop` aborts it. A child's events stream to the parent's subscribers nested under `agent_spawned`, so an app shows the tree. Limits: 8 concurrent agents in a local Harness, 4 levels deep; a child's budget comes out of its parent's. **Taint follows the work:** a child launched by a tainted run starts tainted, its instructions being that run's text; a prompt, steer or follow-up from a tainted run taints its receiver, local or remote; and a child's answer (`agent_wait`'s result, its thread reply) taints the parent that reads it when the child's run is tainted, as its Harness keeps it, the member's own enclave's included (CO-43), and always when the agent runs in another member's enclave (Q-HARN-8); the `private` mark follows the work the same way (7.8). DESIGN §16.6's rule that binds every run of one harness process does not apply here: the Harness tells its runs apart, so a tainted agent taints only the runs its text reaches.

### 7.10 Attaching to an enclave's Harness

```text
transport  the bundled SSH (§12) to the enclave's overlay address, exec "ur harness rpc --session <id>|--new
           [--harness ur|pig]"; the remote side speaks Pi 1.5.0's RPC protocol on the channel: JSON lines,
           commands on stdin with an id, responses with that id, and events, on stdout
commands   prompt, steer, follow_up, abort, get_state, set_model, compact, get_messages, get_tree, switch_session,
           fork, clone (Pi's); list_sessions, subscribe {from_seq}, ui_response (sidecar's)
events     7.6's, as the remote Harness emits them
who        the person's devices, and the person's own agents, as the ssh rule allows (§16.2); the remote side checks
           the caller's sidecar from the SSH session (§12.5) and refuses a caller the rule does not name
several    many attachers may read one session; commands are applied in arrival order, and each attacher sees the
           others' prompts as events
reconnect  each event has its seq; a client that reconnects sends subscribe {from_seq} and the remote replays from
           the incarnation's own journal of the run; entries from before this incarnation the local side
           reads from the vault (§7.7)
harness    "ur" (default): the Harness in the enclave profile; "pig": PiG's `pig --mode rpc`, pinned in the image,
           its provider set to the enclave's own gateway (§8) so it uses the same catalog
endpoint   the enclave's SSH server, outside the agents' container, verifies the session's origin (§12.5)
           and joins an exec of ur harness rpc to the Harness, which runs in the daemon's namespaces
           (§11.10), never starting it in the container; a pig session runs pig --mode rpc in the
           container as a program, its gateway on the container's loopback, and since PiG marks no
           untrusted text, only the person's origin drives it
```

Approvals an enclave's agent needs reach the person's approval-capable devices through DESIGN §16.6's channel, never through the attach link, so an attacher cannot approve by sending an RPC line. A Claude Code or Codex session in an enclave has no RPC mode: the person reaches it through a terminal (`ur enclave ssh`), and its runs are recorded by `ur install-harness` inside the enclave, as on any machine.

**Managing remote Harnesses** (CO-23). A person asks the local Harness to run the remote ones, and its agent does it with 7.9's tools over a management mode of the same link, which reaches every agent of the remote Harness rather than one session:

```text
mode       exec "ur harness rpc --manage", as agent (§12.5): the whole Harness; the ur Harness only, since PiG
           runs one session (--harness pig refuses it); the SSH server joins it to the Harness, outside the
           agents' container, as for a session
commands   Pi's prompt, steer, follow_up, abort, get_state and get_messages, each naming its "agent" (a command
           without one is refused; Pi's other commands stay in the session mode); and the Harness's own:
           ur_list_agents {}               every agent: name, id, model, run, parent, status and newest
                                           summary (§20.6)
           ur_launch_agent {name, model, instructions, tools?, budget?, parent}
                                           7.9's launch in that Harness, refused from any origin but the
                                           sponsor's (its person, its devices' runs, its own enclaves'); its
                                           parent the calling run's agent, from the verified origin, its
                                           depth counted along the cards' parent chain, and tainted from
                                           the start when the origin is; answers the registered name (§20.5)
                                           and the agent id
           ur_subscribe {from?: {<agent>: seq}, agents?, level?}
                                           the events of every agent, or of those named, each carrying its
                                           "agent", replayed from the incarnation's journal of each run past
                                           the seq given for it; level status sends state changes only, so
                                           a phone watching several enclaves takes no deltas
           ui_response {agent, request_id, …}
                                           the person's answer to a remote agent's dialog (7.6), from the
                                           person's origin only
           ur_continue {run, at, act, agent?, model?}
                                           continue or fork a run of the sponsor's here, which the enclave
                                           reads from the vault as one of the sponsor's devices (§24.7),
                                           from the person's origin only: the app's UI, ur harness, or the
                                           person's confirmation or kind 24 approval of harness_continue,
                                           whose id the caller's daemon stamps on it
origin     every command, in either mode, carries its origin: the person (the app's UI, or ur harness reading
           the person's input from its controlling terminal, /dev/tty, with no harness process among its
           ancestors, as DESIGN §5.8's confirmed commands require) or a run, with its agent and taint bit (a
           tool call, or a ur process whose ancestry binds a run, DESIGN §16.7); any other caller is an
           unknown run's. The caller's sidecar sets it, never a line's writer, and signs it before the exec
           in an origin@ur.io request (§12.4, §12.5): with its identity key, over the session's exchange hash,
           either one origin for a session whose bytes it only carries (ur ssh), which the daemon ends when
           that run is tainted, or that its own Harness stamps each line. The enclave's SSH server verifies
           it outside the agents' container; a session without it, such as OpenSSH's through ur ssh agent
           (§12.9), is an unknown run's
trust      as 20.7 reads a push's provenance: a command's text is trusted only when its origin is the person,
           signed by an untagged device of the enclave's sponsor, or an untainted run on such a device or in
           another of the sponsor's enclaves (CO-43); anything else (a tainted run, a cloud agent, another
           member or another member's enclave, no signature) reaches the agent
           between untrusted-data markers, with its verified sender, and taints its run (I-9, IC-12)
threads    every prompt is also a 20.7 thread message, which the command names by its path and the text's
           SHA-256: an agent's written by its tool (agent_prompt, below), the person's by the device's input
           path as 20.7's kind (a) (the sdk's Prompt, Steer and FollowUp on a managed agent, ur harness);
           the remote Harness delivers the text once, by the command or the message, whichever it takes
           first, a refused command (Pi's prompt while the agent streams, without streamingBehavior)
           delivering nothing; where text or trust disagree it takes the lower trust and alarms; the agent
           reports back in that thread, to its reply_to where the prompt set one (Both sides, below)
events     the local Harness relays each with the enclave's name beside its agent, so the agent tree (7.6) and
           the recURd graph (§20.8) nest it under the enclave; events reach the person's view, never a model's
           context, which takes a remote agent's words only through a tool, as untrusted input (7.8); the
           person's view renders their text as untrusted (7.11), an approval_pending only from the approval
           log, and a ui_request only as 7.6 allows
who        as for attach: the ssh rule (§16.2), checked from the SSH session (§12.5); one link per device and
           enclave, shared by the device's agents and views, so §12.4's session limits hold; another
           member's link needs the sponsor's consent, and its prompts, steers and stops spend the sponsor's
           budget (Q-HARN-9)
never      approvals (above); ui_response from any origin but the person's, so no agent answers another's
           dialog; and any answer to a `disclosure` (7.6): only the sponsor's acknowledgment answers it,
           reaching the enclave in its settings (§11.4)
record     each command enters the receiving run's record with its origin, and each tool call the caller's
```

**The tools.** 7.9's tools reach any agent of a remote Harness that the `ssh` rule lets the person reach, not only the caller's children; an agent is named `<name>`, its card saying where it runs (§20.5), or `enclave:<e>/<name>`:

| Tool | Tier | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `harness_list(enclave?, live?, untrusted?)` | R | the person's enclaves, each with its state, label and egress mode, its Harness (`ur`, its version, whether a link is up, and any PiG sessions attached) and its agents: name, host, model, state and its age, run, parent, and what reaches each (the ur Harness's agents by link and thread; Claude Code, Codex and other external harnesses by thread only, read at their next turn; PiG sessions, which hold no card, by `list_sessions` and a session attach); read from `enclave_list` (in an enclave, which has none, from the cards' `host` and the config) and the agents repo's cards and status, synced already, or, with `live`, from each Harness's `ur_list_agents`; with `enclave` naming one, also another member's that a rule lets the person reach, live. Identifier fields reach the model between untrusted-data markers, labeled with their writer, each held to its grammar and the whole capped (§20.6), and do not taint; status text and each agent's newest summary go to the model as §20.6 lets them, trusted where an untainted run of the member's wrote them, in the member's own enclave too (CO-43), and otherwise to the person's view, and to the model only with `untrusted: include`, which taints the run first (DESIGN §16.11's stub rule; 20.6). An enclave that runs no Harness, such as the network's indexer (§11.10), is listed alone |
| `agent_launch(…, where: enclave:<name>)` | W; O (kind 24) in a tainted run when the enclave's egress is not `none`; refused into another member's enclave | `ur_launch_agent`: the child is the caller's, which its card names as `parent`, and starts tainted when the caller's run is (7.9); it spends from the enclave's budget, which the broker bounds per tagged subject (§16.4), since the broker cannot see the caller's, and it counts against the limits of the Harness that runs it |
| `agent_prompt(agent, text, mode?, thread?)` | W; O (kind 24) in a tainted run when the agent runs in an enclave whose egress is not `none`, or is another member's | `mode` is `prompt`, `steer` or `follow_up`; for a remote agent it writes the text into a 20.7 thread with that agent (`thread` if given, else the caller's open thread with it, else a new one), then sends the command naming that message; with no link the thread alone carries it, and the agent's lease wakes it, though only the link can steer mid-turn; the message sets `reply_to` to the person's `me` when the calling run is one the person started, so the report goes to the person (Both sides, below); to an agent no link drives (an external harness, by its card's `harness`), the result says the prompt waits for that harness's next turn |
| `agent_wait(agent, timeout?)` | R; the answer of a remote agent, or of a tainted local child, is untrusted and taints the run | returns when the agent settles, with its last message, or when it replies in the thread, whichever comes first |
| `agent_stop(agent)` | W; from a tainted run, only for agents it launched, any other waiting for the person's confirmation, so an injected run cannot stop every agent the person runs | `abort`, over the link, which it opens if none is up |
| `harness_continue(run, at?, enclave)` | W, after the person's confirmation in the app or on `/dev/tty`, never an RPC `ui_response`; O (kind 24) when the enclave reaches out (7.8) and the calling run is tainted or a node it continues is flagged or untrusted | sends `ur_continue` naming the run and `at` (its tip by default), with the person's origin, stamped with the confirmation's or approval's id; the enclave reads the run from the vault (§24.7) |

**Both sides.** The link carries control and the live view: prompts, steering, aborts, state, and every event, which the person's devices show under the enclave. Threads carry the work: the agent reports back in the prompt's thread with `agent_send` when it is done, blocked or unsure, and the report reaches its addressee whether the link is up or the phone asleep (CF-10). A prompt that carried the person's request (`reply_to`, the member's `me`) is answered to the person's side of the thread (§20.7), so the report shows on each of the person's devices without waking the asking bot, which learns that the work ended from the agent's stub (state, exit), which does not taint, and reads the report only when the person asks; any other report wakes its asker. A remote child given no thread reports to its parent, opening one in the parent's inbox, and an agent prompted with no thread and no parent reports to its member's `me`. The recURd skill teaches each side its part (§20.9): the local profile to manage, the enclave profile to be managed. A prompt from a run counts toward its receiver's wakes (§20.7), so two agents cannot drive each other without end. Nothing here adds to what a server sees: the link is connect's Required-mode ciphertext over the overlay (§12), and threads are EVS ciphertext (IC-2).

**Another member's enclave.** Its agents' status, summaries and conversations are its sponsor's owner-bound record (owner decision 126), so another member manages it only with the sponsor's consent: a requested `ssh` grant naming that member, which the sponsor's consented device approves (`autogroup:dst-owner`, DESIGN §8.8) and the enclave's SSH server checks (§12.5); an admin's rule alone admits no one. Since CO-43 the enclave also holds everything its sponsor's devices hold, so such a grant never reaches `root` (§12.5), and what another member's command has a run read of the sponsor's goes back to that member only by the sponsor's kind 24 (7.8). With it, the other member lists, prompts, steers, waits on and stops the enclave's agents but never launches one, and its prompts, steers and stops spend the sponsor's budget, since the enclave's agents run on it; their reports back to that member's agents are kind 24 from the enclave's runs (7.8) (Q-HARN-9).

**What a tainted run pays.** A managing agent that has read a remote answer is tainted, so its next prompt into an enclave that reaches the internet waits for approval (kind 24), which the device's safety classifier gives first in auto mode for the member's own enclave (§27.4): in such an enclave the receiver's taint stops nothing its `bash` sends. The design spends that wait only where the bot has read: `harness_list`'s stubs and the person's view of events do not taint; reports on the person's requests go to the person's side of the thread, not into the bot's context (Both sides, above); the person's own prompts, typed in the app or `ur harness`, never wait; and an enclave whose egress is `none`, and that no rule lets dial another device's services (7.8, §26.7), takes a tainted run's prompt without approval, as untrusted input. A bot that reads remote answers for the person still asks at its next such prompt, which 7.15 counts as a risk. An enclave whose egress is `none` sends nothing to the internet itself, but it writes into the network; its runs that took the prompt are tainted, so their own sends onward pass kind 24 in a Harness that sits outside its agents' container (§11.10), and the daemon marks the enclave, so an `egress_change` (DESIGN kind 5) that later moves it off `none` shows that it took tainted input there (§16.3's field 49). What its runs write waits behind 7.8's hold before an enclave that reaches the internet reads it.

### 7.11 The terminal renderer

`ur harness [--agent <name>] [--model <name>] [--enclave <name>]` runs a Harness in the terminal: markdown rendered with ANSI styles, thinking dimmed and folded, tool cards with one-line summaries and the last lines of output, diffs colored, the cost meter and TEE badge in the status line with the provider's disclosure line, approval and disclosure prompts on the terminal (§2.8). It is a renderer over 7.6's events with no terminal-UI framework, so it adds little to `ur`; with `--enclave` it renders an attached remote session. Untrusted text (results, pages, inbox messages, tool output, and all text relayed from a remote Harness) is printed with ESC, C0 and C1 control characters removed, so none of it can write the clipboard (OSC 52) or plant a link (OSC 8); the renderer's own OSC 8 links carry only URLs it has checked.

### 7.12 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Embed PiG (`coding` SDK) | full features at once | 7.3's table: size, wasm, globals, shell-outs, churn | rejected for the local Harness; shipped in enclaves |
| Embed only PiG's `agent` + `ai` | Pi's loop exactly | still no wasm; the TLS `init()`; providers we would bypass | rejected; the design is copied, the code is not imported |
| A Harness of sidecar's own design | free shape | loses Pi's formats, tooling and UI renderers | rejected: Pi's formats kept |
| Attach over a new subprotocol stream instead of SSH | one less layer | CO-5 names SSH; PiG's RPC runs over any byte stream | SSH |

### 7.13 Decisions proposed

**D-HARN-1 (proposed).** The Harness is sidecar's own Go code modeled on Pi's agent core, reusing Pi's event JSON, RPC protocol and session entries. *Why:* 7.3.

**D-HARN-2 (proposed).** Two tool profiles, local and enclave, with 7.5's table. *Why:* CO-5 and CO-6.

**D-HARN-3 (proposed).** Runs are recorded natively as Pi-shaped entries in the vault. *Why:* complete coverage without hooks; Pi's export works.

**D-HARN-4 (proposed).** Attach is Pi's RPC over the bundled SSH; enclaves run the Harness or PiG behind the same protocol. *Why:* CO-5; one client for both.

**D-HARN-5 (proposed).** The attach link gains a management mode, `ur harness rpc --manage`: one SSH session per device and enclave carries Pi's prompt, steer, follow_up, abort, get_state and get_messages, each naming its agent, and the Harness-wide `ur_list_agents`, `ur_launch_agent` and `ur_subscribe`, whose events nest under the enclave, with `ui_response` and `ur_continue` from the person's origin only; 7.9's tools reach any agent there the `ssh` rule lets the person reach, `harness_list` shows them all, each remote prompt is also a message in a 20.7 thread where the agent reports back by `agent_send`, and approvals never cross the link. *Why:* CO-23; Q-HARN-5; I-8.

**D-HARN-6 (proposed).** Every command on an attach link carries an origin the caller's sidecar signs over the session, the person or a run with its taint bit, which the enclave's SSH server verifies outside the agents' container; the receiver trusts its text only as the person's, from an untagged device of the enclave's sponsor, or as an untainted run's there or in another of the sponsor's enclaves, and otherwise shows it as untrusted and taints its run; a remote agent's answer taints its local reader when its run is tainted, as the member's own enclave's Harness keeps it, and always from another member's enclave, and `harness_list`'s identifier stubs never do. *Why:* I-9; IC-12; CO-43; Q-HARN-6, Q-HARN-8.

**D-HARN-7 (proposed).** A tainted run's command, prompt or message into an enclave whose egress is not `none`, an enclave a rule lets dial another device's services counting as such, or to another member's agent, is outward kind 24, `tainted_send`, whichever tool or `ur` command carries it, as is `harness_continue` into such an enclave when the calling run is tainted or a node it continues is flagged or untrusted; no evs or git write reaches an inbox. *Why:* I-8, I-9; Q-HARN-7.

**D-HARN-8 (proposed).** Taint follows the work between agents: a child launched or prompted by a tainted run is tainted, and a child's answer taints the parent that reads it when the child's run is tainted, in the member's own enclave as on a device (CO-43), and always from another member's enclave. *Why:* I-9; CO-43; otherwise a tainted run launders what it read through a fresh child.

**D-HARN-9 (proposed).** An enclave's Harness and the receiving end of every attach link run in the daemon's namespaces, outside the agents' container, which runs only the agents' tool processes; the enclave's SSH server verifies each link's signed origin, and the Harness keeps each run's taint bit. *Why:* I-9; agents have root in their container, so whatever is kept beside them, a taint bit, a trust mark or an origin check, is theirs to rewrite.

**D-HARN-10 (proposed).** `ui_request` gains the kind `disclosure`, naming an id and version only: the renderer shows the signed policy's text, only the person's acknowledgment answers it, never a `ui_response`, and one from a remote Harness is relayed by id and version, the enclave reading the sponsor's acknowledgment from the vault. *Why:* the person's act, not a run's (I-8's line); no agent, run or remote Harness may supply a disclosure's text or its answer.

**D-HARN-11 (proposed).** The bundled `git`'s `clone`, `fetch` and `pull`, and any command that fetches an object lazily, taint the run before the worktree is written or the command answers when a push they take objects from shows a tainted run, a tagged sidecar other than the member's own enclave or another member, or no provenance they can read; in the enclave profile every tool that reads or runs in the agents' container taints its run as it starts, the file tools included, so every push from the container is a tainted run's. *Why:* I-9; CO-43, which trusts an enclave's untainted runs; otherwise an untainted run reads injected text through `git pull` and `read`, and its calendar, service and enclave writes then pass at W.

**D-HARN-12 (proposed).** An enclave whose egress is not `none` keeps from its agents' container, and from every run there without the `private` mark, every EVS version whose provenance shows a tainted run, or none its daemon can read, other than pushes from the containers of the member's enclaves that reach out by runs without that mark, until its sponsor releases it by kind 24, built on the sponsor's device from the versions it reads; an enclave whose egress is `none` counts as reaching out where a rule lets it dial another device's services. *Why:* Q-HARN-10; kind 24's reason, that a receiver's taint stops nothing in such an enclave, holds for what it reads from EVS, and a listed service can act on the internet for an enclave with no egress of its own.

**D-HARN-13 (proposed).** In the local profile the file tools refuse every `.git` path component, in every spelling git itself refuses, and the bundled git writes a worktree's config with no command, alias, include, filter or hook. *Why:* IC-7; a `core.fsmonitor` an agent wrote would run on the person's computer once their shell prompt or editor opened the worktree.

**D-HARN-14 (proposed).** In an enclave that reaches out, a run holds the sponsor's private data or the agents' container, not both: reading mail, calendars, connected services, the mailbox, a vault file or a marked node gives a run the `private` mark, which it never loses, which follows the work as taint does and which its session entries carry; a marked run calls no tool that runs in or reads the container, and a run that has called one makes no such read and takes in no marked run's work, each crossing waiting for the person's kind 24, never the classifier's; a marked run works under the local profile's rules. *Why:* CO-43 puts the sponsor's data in the enclave while its agents' `bash` reaches the internet outside every gate; Q-HARN-11; I-9.

### 7.14 Questions

**Q-HARN-1.** Fork PiG or reimplement? *Options:* (a) vendor PiG; (b) reimplement on Pi's formats; (c) import `agent` + `ai`. *Answer:* (b), for 7.3's reasons. *Decider:* owner.

**Q-HARN-2.** Does the local Harness get web access? *Options:* (a) no; (b) a `web_fetch` tool. *Answer:* (b): CO-17 asks for a core fetch tool and CO-16 for search, so the local profile gets both (§21, §22), through URnetwork's network, under the listed-URL rule and taint. *Decider:* owner.

**Q-HARN-3.** May a local Harness run on the page Worker or the extension? *Answer:* not at launch: the extension's Worker is Later in DESIGN, and the page Worker has no compute surface; remote-only Harness in the browser follows the Worker. *Decider:* owner.

**Q-HARN-4.** What runs by default in an enclave? *Options:* (a) the Harness; (b) PiG. *Answer:* (a): it records natively and its tool and approval rules are sidecar's; PiG is one flag away for people who want Pi's extensions and TUI. *Decider:* owner.

**Q-HARN-5.** How does a local Harness reach several agents in one enclave? *Options:* (a) a session attach for each agent; (b) one management link per device and enclave, reaching every agent of that Harness; (c) inbox threads alone. *Answer:* (b), with threads beside it for work that outlives the link. (a) spends an SSH session per agent against §12.4's 16 a client, and can neither list agents nor launch one; (c) cannot steer, abort or show a run as it happens. One link carries control and the live view, and each prompt's thread carries the answer, which survives a dropped link or a sleeping phone. *Decider:* owner.

**Q-HARN-6.** How does the remote side know whether a command on the link is trusted? *Options:* (a) by the caller's sidecar alone, every command from a device the `ssh` rule admits trusted; (b) by an origin the caller's sidecar signs over the session, the person or a run with its taint bit, trusted only from an untagged device of the enclave's sponsor; (c) never: every command untrusted. *Answer:* (b). (a) lets a tainted run on the person's own device carry injected text into an enclave agent's trusted context, past I-9; (c) taints every run the person drives by hand and costs it its outward actions, though the person typed the prompt. (b) is D-SKILL-4's rule for messages applied to the link, so since CO-43 an untainted run in another of the sponsor's enclaves counts as one on their device (IC-12). Signing over the exchange hash keeps an origin from moving to another session or being chosen by a line's writer, and keeps OpenSSH sessions, which `ur ssh agent` lets any same-user process open, from carrying one; a same-user process that detaches from its harness and drives a pty can still pass as the person, DESIGN's TB1 residual (owner decision 47), which §2.7 discloses. *Decider:* peer review.

**Q-HARN-7.** Is a tainted run's prompt into an enclave an outward action? *Options:* (a) no: the receiver marks it untrusted; (b) yes when the enclave's egress is not `none`, as `ssh_exec` is (7.8); (c) always. *Answer:* (b), as kind 24, `tainted_send`, for every tool that carries text there, `agent_send` and `agent_broadcast` included. A receiver's taint stops nothing in an enclave, whose `bash` reaches the internet outside the gate (DESIGN §16.6), so the gate must be the sender's. An enclave whose egress is `none` sends nothing to the internet itself, unless a rule lets it dial another device's services, which can act on the internet for it, so such an enclave counts as reaching out (7.8, §26.7); and it writes into the network (deposits, the agents repo, the repos it syncs): its runs that took the prompt are tainted, so their sends onward pass the same gate, kept by a Harness outside its agents' container (§11.10), and what they write waits behind 7.8's hold before an enclave that reaches the internet reads it, so (c) would cost approvals for nothing the hold does not already cover. One kind for every tool and command that messages, runs a command or moves a context, and no evs or git write into an inbox, leaves a tainted run no messaging door. *Decider:* owner.

**Q-HARN-8.** Does a remote agent's answer taint the local run that reads it, even from an untainted run in an enclave whose egress is `none`? *Options:* (a) always; (b) only when the remote run says it is tainted. *Answer:* (b) for the member's own enclave, as CO-43 has it, and (a) for another member's. The member's enclave is one of their devices, whose Harness keeps each run's taint in the daemon's namespaces, outside the agents' container, where no agent can clear it (§11.10), so its untainted runs are trusted as a desktop's are; most of its runs are tainted anyway, since every tool that touches the container taints its run (7.8), and their answers taint the reader. Another member's enclave is another member's device, whose runs taint as any other member's (IC-12). A managing agent stays useful because it need not read: `harness_list`'s stubs do not taint, events go to the person's view rather than its context, threads bring the answer when it is needed, and the person's own prompts never wait for approval. *Decider:* owner.

**Q-HARN-9.** May an enclave's agent manage another enclave's Harness, and a member another member's? *Options:* (a) never; (b) as the `ssh` rule allows, every such command untrusted to its receiver; (c) by default. *Answer:* (b) within a member, and another member's enclave only with its sponsor's consent. Within a member, managing is the `ssh` action (§16.2): the default rule reaches a member's enclaves from that member's untagged devices and the agents on them (§16.5), so one enclave reaches another only by a rule naming both (`tag:enclave-<a>` to `tag:enclave-<b>`). Another member's enclave holds its sponsor's owner-bound agent record, its agents' status, summaries and conversations (owner decision 126), so a rule an admin writes is not enough: the sponsor's consented device approves a requested `ssh` grant naming the other member (`autogroup:dst-owner`, DESIGN §8.8), which the enclave's SSH server checks; with it the other member may list, prompt, steer, wait on and stop the enclave's agents but never launch one, since `ur_launch_agent` takes only the sponsor's origins, and its prompts, steers and stops spend the sponsor's budget. Either way its commands arrive untrusted (Q-HARN-6), from a tainted run into an enclave that reaches the internet they wait for approval (Q-HARN-7), and a report back to another member's agent is kind 24 from the enclave's run, so the skill has such agents report once, at the end. Since CO-43 the enclave holds what its sponsor's devices hold, so such a grant never reaches `root` (§12.5), and what another member's command has a run there read of the sponsor's reaches that member only by the sponsor's kind 24, which the classifier never decides for another member (7.8, §27.7). *Decider:* owner.

**Q-HARN-10.** May a tainted run's EVS writes reach an enclave that reaches the internet with no person's act, and should an enclave's agents read every summary of their member's agents? *Options:* (a) yes to both: every reader takes such text as untrusted, §2.7's residual; (b) no to both: the enclave's daemon holds a tainted run's versions until the sponsor releases them by kind 24, and its agents read cards and status stubs, their own agents' files and their threads, other agents' summaries only by the sponsor's grant (§20.4); (c) no enclave reads its member's repos. *Answer:* (b) for the first; for the second, since CO-43 makes the enclave one of its sponsor's devices, its agents read the agents repo, summaries included, as the member's other agents do (§20.4), a summary a tainted run wrote waiting behind the hold like any other version. Kind 24 exists because a receiver's taint stops nothing in an enclave that reaches the internet, and the same holds for what it reads from EVS; the local Harness keeps everything in EVS (CO-6), so a summary a mail-reading run wrote is the common path, not a corner. Holding only tainted runs' versions leaves untainted work flowing, while (c) would break the agent graph and the management of CO-19 and CO-23. *Decider:* owner.

**Q-HARN-11.** Once an enclave holds its sponsor's data (CO-43), may one run there both read it and use the agents' container, whose `bash` reaches the internet? *Options:* (a) yes: the enclave is the person's device, and its agents act as an external harness's do on a desktop, its disclosure saying so; (b) only in an enclave that does not reach out, a run in one that does holding the sponsor's private data (mail, calendars, connected services, the vault, the mailbox) or the container, the crossing being the person's kind 24; (c) no mail, calendar or connection tools in an enclave that reaches out. *Answer:* (b). In an enclave that reaches out, a prompt-injected agent's `bash` sends whatever its run holds outside every gate, so under (a) one injected message could send the person's mail, accounts and record anywhere, past every approval; (c) would take from such an enclave the mail, calendars and connections CO-42 shares with it. (b) keeps both: mail and accounts work in runs that never touch the container, under the local profile's gates (7.8), and builds, root and the internet in runs that never read them, as before CO-43; a run that needs both asks the person once, and a crossing's card shows what the run holds. Repos other than the vault and the mailbox stay readable by the container's runs, as CO-43's full access has it for the initial version, which the enclave's disclosure says (§2.8). *Decider:* owner.

### 7.15 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pi's formats change after 1.5.0 | medium | attach to newer PiG breaks | pin PiG in the image; the RPC handshake carries the protocol version |
| A local agent's workspace fills a phone | medium | app storage pressure | 7.5's caps; cleanup at run end |
| Event floods on phones | medium | UI lag | 30 updates a second, authoritative `message_end` |
| A managing agent, tainted by a remote answer, asks approval at each prompt into an enclave | high | people approve without reading | stubs and the person's view do not taint; reports on the person's requests go to the person's side of the thread, not the bot's context; the person's own prompts never wait; egress `none`, and no rule letting it dial another device's services, where an enclave needs neither the internet nor the network's services (7.8, 7.10); the safety classifier first in auto mode (§27) |
| Agents driving one another without end, over the link or by thread | medium | spend and noise | prompts from runs count toward §20.7's wakes; budgets; 7.9's depth limit |
| An enclave's agents tamper with what runs beside them in their container | medium | forged events or dialogs in the person's view; a cleared taint bit | the Harness, the receiving end of the link and the origin check outside the container; `ur` there read-only; its one socket's calls tainted; relayed dialogs limited (7.6) |
| Held versions stall an enclave's work | medium | an agent waits, or works on a file older than the person expects | only a tainted run's versions wait; the agent sees `held` and asks; the person releases from the enclave's card, and kind 24's card shows each version whole (7.8) |
| A run in an enclave needs both the sponsor's data and the container | medium | the person asked to approve a crossing, or the work split across two runs | a marked run keeps the local profile's tools; a second run or a child takes the container's part, their exchange gated as any tainted send (7.8); the crossing's card shows what the run holds |

### 7.16 Phasing

M11: the loop, local profile, events, sdk and CLI hosts, the record, the skill, taint between parent and child (7.9); the local profile's `git` comes with §13 in M13, its agents keeping work with `evs_*` until then. M14: the enclave profile, RPC mode and attach, with attach's management mode, `harness_list`, `harness_continue` and the remote reach of 7.9's tools (7.10), and the Harness outside the agents' container (§11.10), with 7.8's hold on tainted versions, its `private` mark, and the enclave as its sponsor's device (§11.4). §19.

## 8. The local gateway

### 8.1 Purpose and scope

This section designs the gateway: the daemon's loopback endpoint through which Codex, Claude Code and other harnesses use every catalog model (local and remote, in a TEE or not) and the compute balance, configured once. The catalog and router behind it are §6; the charges are §9; recording a call is §6.8.

### 8.2 Requirements

| Id | Requirement | Source |
|---|---|---|
| R-GW-1 | One endpoint exposes every catalog model the grant's policy allows, local and remote, in a TEE or not, by its canonical name, and the compute balance | CO-4, CO-11, CO-18 |
| R-GW-2 | Codex and Claude Code use it with no change to their code, through settings `ur install-harness` writes | CO-4 |
| R-GW-3 | The same models, prices and attestation as the Harness: the gateway is a second front on §6's router, not a second router | CO-11 |
| R-GW-4 | Local servers bind loopback, authenticate callers and check Host | I-17 |
| R-GW-5 | A call to a TEE-labeled model that cannot be verified fails; the gateway never falls back to another model, provider or label | R-CCTX-2 |
| R-GW-6 | Each call is a `model_call` entry in the caller's run, with its attestation evidence, and its request and response are session entries of that run (§24.8) | DESIGN §16.7, RECORD.md section 12; CO-25 |

### 8.3 What harnesses need (2026-11-23)

From [Rpt:bb] (gateway_harness_compat.md, which read openai/codex at 5f645d73 and Claude Code's gateway pages):

| Harness | API it speaks | What the gateway must do |
|---|---|---|
| Codex | OpenAI Responses only (`wire_api = "chat"` removed in February 2026) | one streaming `POST /responses`; stateless full-history requests with `store: false` and `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`; item ids it never issued; complete items in `response.output_item.done`; a terminal `response.completed` with `id` and integer `usage.input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `total_tokens`; `insufficient_quota` ends a turn without retry; its hosted `web_search` tool, which `ur install-harness` turns off and the gateway drops (§21.7) |
| Claude Code | Anthropic Messages | `POST /v1/messages` (inference posts to `?beta=true`), SSE through `message_delta` and `message_stop`, `ping` during pauses, no empty thinking blocks; accept and ignore the fields it sends for unknown model ids (`thinking.type=adaptive`, `output_config`, `context_management`, `cache_control`, `defer_loading`, `strict`, `role: "system"` mid-conversation); `count_tokens` optional; WebSearch's side request with the server tool `web_search_20250305`, which the gateway answers `unavailable` (§21.7) |
| OpenCode, Goose, Aider, Cline, Roo, Continue, Zed, Copilot CLI, pi | Chat Completions by default; some also Responses or Messages | `POST /v1/chat/completions` with streaming tool calls |
| Gemini CLI | the Gemini API only (`GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL`) | a fourth API; Later (Q-GW-3) |
| Cursor | sends custom-endpoint requests from Cursor's cloud | cannot reach a loopback gateway; unsupported (Q-GW-2) |

Anthropic states that it does not support routing Claude Code to non-Claude models through any gateway, so Claude Code's compatibility is the gateway's to test each release, and the docs say so (§18).

### 8.4 Endpoints

```text
listener   127.0.0.1:<port> and [::1]:<port>, the port chosen at install and kept in the daemon's settings;
           never another address, whatever a flag says (R-GW-4); held while any grant exists:
           `ur install-harness --gateway` installs the daemon's unit if it is absent, as `ur indexer add`
           does (DESIGN §5.8), a daemon that holds a grant never idles out, and where the OS holds a socket
           for a unit (launchd's Sockets, a systemd socket unit) the unit holds the port across the daemon's
           restarts, so no other user's process can take it while a harness may call
POST /v1/responses                 Open Responses (openresponses.org, 2026-04-24 revision) as the conformance target,
                                   stateless: store true or previous_response_id answer 400 unsupported_parameter
POST /v1/chat/completions          OpenAI Chat Completions, streaming and not
POST /v1/messages                  Anthropic Messages, ?beta=true accepted
POST /v1/messages/count_tokens     counts with the model's tokenizer where the catalog carries one, else
                                   ceil(bytes / 3.5), labeled an estimate
GET  /v1/models                    the catalog (§6.3) by canonical name, in OpenAI's shape, or Anthropic's when anthropic-version is set
GET  /v1/ur/balance                this grant's budget left and whether the network can pay (9.9's state); never the
                                   network's balance, which only §9.10's roles see
GET  /v1/ur/catalog                §6.3's full entries: prices, context, label, efforts, attestation status
GET  /v1/ur/listener               a nonce's MAC under a key the daemon gives `ur gateway token` over its control
                                   socket, so the command can tell that the daemon holds the port
```

**Is the listener the daemon?** Harnesses do not authenticate the gateway, so a token goes only to a port the daemon is shown to hold: `ur gateway token` and `ur gateway run` ask the daemon, over its control socket, which checks the caller's uid (DESIGN §5.8), for a fresh key, send a nonce to `/v1/ur/listener` on the port, and give out a token only if the answer is the nonce's MAC under that key. Otherwise they print nothing and exit non-zero, so a process that took the port gets no token and the harness's call fails closed, and `ur status` names the port's holder where the OS shows it.

Every request passes, in order: the listener check (8.7), the token (8.6), the token's model list and budget (§16.4), the router (§6.4), which verifies or refuses (§5), and the hold (§9.7). The gateway adds no plaintext path: a remote call goes out through §6.6's TEE or direct path, a local one to the device's engine (§6.5). A call whose model needs a disclosure the person has not acknowledged, one labeled `none` (§2.8), answers 403 with the code `disclosure_required` in each API's error shape (a `permission_error` in Messages) before any provider is called, its message naming the disclosure, its summary line and the fix, `ur disclosures ack <id>` or the app's settings, which Codex and Claude Code show the person; their web search goes through MCP's `web_search` (§21.7), which answers the same way until search's disclosure is acknowledged. The gateway never prompts, since no person is attached to a harness's call. `ur install-harness <h> --gateway` asks on /dev/tty, once, for the disclosures of the models it writes into the harness's settings, and for `search:parallel`, since the harness searches through MCP's `web_search` (§21.7), so neither a first call nor a first search fails. On a tagged or cloud sidecar, a CI runner say, the gateway takes the network's acknowledgments (§2.8, CO-41), its `disclosure_required` naming `ur disclosures ack <id> --network` for an Owner or Admin, and `ur install-harness --gateway` asks no one: it names each disclosure of the models it writes that the network has not acknowledged, for an Owner or Admin to acknowledge.

### 8.5 Translation

All three APIs map to one internal request, `InferRequest` (§6.4): messages with roles, content parts (text, image), tool definitions and `tool_choice`, a JSON schema for structured output, a reasoning effort, the token maxima, sampling and stops. The router answers one internal event stream, mapped back to the caller's API:

| Internal event (§6.4) | Responses | Chat Completions | Messages |
|---|---|---|---|
| start | `response.created`, `response.in_progress` | first chunk with role | `message_start` |
| text delta | `response.output_text.delta` in a `message` item | `delta.content` | `content_block_delta` `text_delta` |
| reasoning delta | `response.reasoning_summary_text.delta` in a `reasoning` item | `delta.reasoning_content` | `content_block_delta` `thinking_delta` |
| tool call | `response.output_item.added`, `function_call_arguments.delta`, `output_item.done` with `call_id` | `delta.tool_calls` | `content_block_start` `tool_use`, `input_json_delta` |
| usage, end | `response.completed` with `usage` | final chunk with `usage`, `[DONE]` | `message_delta` with `usage` and `stop_reason`, `message_stop` |
| error | `response.failed` with `error.code` | an error body, or an `error` chunk mid-stream | an `error` event |
| keepalive | `: ping` comment every 15 s | `: ping` comment every 15 s | `ping` event every 15 s |

**Reasoning across turns.** Codex sends back each turn's reasoning items with `encrypted_content`; Claude Code sends thinking blocks with a `signature`. Neither is readable by an open model, and the gateway is stateless to its callers (D-GW-2), so it fills both with its own sealed blob: the reasoning text under XChaCha20-Poly1305 with a key in the daemon's keychain, so a later turn can give the model its earlier reasoning where the model's template wants it, and a blob from anywhere else is ignored. The blob also names the session entry that recorded the reasoning, so a replayed blob matches it (§24.8). **Custom tools.** Codex's freeform `apply_patch` is sent only when the model catalog file enables it; the gateway's generated catalog (8.8) does not, so Codex edits through its shell tool, which needs no grammar translation. **Unknown fields** are accepted and ignored, never rejected, since a rejection makes Claude Code retry without each field one by one. **Overflow in each API's words.** A request past its model's window, or one the direct path cannot upload in time (§6.6), is answered in the words each harness acts on, since Codex and Claude Code compact only on their own API's overflow error and stop compacting when a gateway rewords it: Messages' 400 `invalid_request_error` "prompt is too long: <n> tokens > <max> maximum", and Responses' and Chat Completions' `context_length_exceeded`. **Images** larger than the model's input size are re-encoded to it before a call, deterministically, so a session's screenshots stay small and the session entries record what was sent and dedupe it across turns (§24.8). **Claude Code's attribution block**, which it puts first in the system text with its version and a conversation fingerprint, is turned off by the settings `ur install-harness` writes (8.8) and, from a Claude Code that still sends it, dropped by the gateway by its place and form, as Anthropic's API drops it, so no provider receives the fingerprint.

**Hosted web search.** The gateway serves none (CO-26): a Responses request's hosted `web_search` tool is dropped from the model's tools, and a Messages request whose only tool is a `web_search_*` server tool is answered at once with an `unavailable` result, with no model call and no charge; harnesses search through the MCP `web_search`, whose results the gateway's session entries record only as stubs (§21.7, §24.9).

**Retries never bill twice.** Codex re-runs a whole turn when a stream ends before its terminal event ([Rpt:bb]), and a remote call that ran is charged whether or not its stream reached the harness. So the gateway (a) always ends a stream with a terminal event, `response.failed` with a non-retryable code when the upstream failed after it began, and (b) keeps each response from its first byte, keyed by the grant and a SHA-256 of the request body (with Codex's `x-client-request-id` where sent): an identical request that arrives while the call is in flight joins it, replaying what has streamed and then following it live, the call running on to its end though its first caller left; one that arrives within 10 minutes of its end is answered from the kept response; neither makes a new provider call or a new charge. The kept responses are sealed to a key in the daemon's keychain, as the reasoning blob is, and kept in its state, so a restart keeps them; a planned restart (an upgrade, `ur daemon restart`) waits up to 10 minutes for calls in flight, so only a crash cuts one, its retry then a new call and the cut call billed as its provider bills a closed stream (§6.6). Each is dropped 10 minutes after its end.

### 8.6 Tokens

The gateway takes a bearer token in `Authorization` or `x-api-key`.

```text
mint     ur gateway token --harness <h> [--agent <label>] prints a token for one harness install: ur_gw_ and 32
         random bytes in base64url, valid 1 h; Codex's [model_providers.ur.auth] command and Claude Code's
         apiKeyHelper run it, so a token on disk lives at most an hour (Claude Code caches a helper's output 5 min)
binds    the token's grant: harness, agent label, model list (§16.4), budget per day and month, expiry; grants are
         made by ur install-harness and listed and revoked by ur gateway grants; a grant's budget never passes the
         server's default for its agent (§16.4), and a grant or raise above it is compute_budget_raise (§16.3),
         approved on an approval-capable device, since a same-user process can run ur install-harness too
keep     the daemon stores each grant and a hash of each live token in its sealed store; nothing reaches a server
I-7      the token administers nothing, reads nothing and signs nothing; it spends within its grant's budget on this
         loopback listener, as the telemetry token only adds reports (owner decision 463); §2.4's IC-11 states it
```

A same-user process can read the token and spend within the budget; it can also run `ur gateway token` or `ur install-harness` itself, so the token adds attribution and a budget, not isolation from processes of the same user, as DESIGN §2.4's TB1 already says of that user's agents. What bounds such a process is server-side: every gateway call carries its agent's id, and the broker enforces the default budgets per device and per agent, and $50 a day across all of a device's agents (§16.4), whatever grants exist locally.

### 8.7 Local security

- **Listener:** loopback only; IPv4 and IPv6. No Unix socket: none of the harnesses' base-URL settings accepts one ([Rpt:bb]). In an enclave the daemon also opens one itself on the agents' container's own loopback, in the container's network namespace (§11.10), rather than a socket and a relay inside the container, so nothing the agents control carries the gateway; PiG, Codex and Claude Code there take an ordinary base URL under this section's Host, Origin and token checks, and get their tokens, for the container's grants, only through the container socket, every call of which is a tainted run's. Those hour-long tokens are the only credential the container holds (IC-11, I-7). The container's grants are the enclave's: `ur install-harness <h> --gateway` run there (§7.10) writes the harness's settings in the container and asks for the grant through the container socket, and the daemon makes it from the sponsor's `models` key and acknowledged disclosures in the enclave's settings (§11.4), within the enclave's budget as a tagged subject (§16.4), as it makes PiG's when a session attach starts PiG; nothing there asks the person, and a model whose disclosure the sponsor has not acknowledged answers `disclosure_required`, which the sponsor answers on their own device.
- **Host:** the request's `Host` must be `127.0.0.1:<port>`, `localhost:<port>` or `[::1]:<port>`, else 421, which stops DNS rebinding (the Ollama CVE-2024-28224 class).
- **Browsers:** a request with an `Origin` header, or with `Sec-Fetch-Site` other than `none`, is refused 403, and no CORS header is ever sent, so no web page reads an answer.
- **Limits:** 32 MiB request body, since Codex and Claude Code resend the whole history, its images included, at every turn; 32 concurrent requests; a token's own rate (§16.4).

### 8.8 One config

The person sets models once, in the vault's harness config (`harness/config.json`, DESIGN §16.7), whose `models` key this document designs (§16.4): the default model, a per-harness mapping of the harness's tiers onto catalog ids, and the models allowed. `ur install-harness <h> --gateway` renders that into each harness's own settings and keeps them in step when the config changes. Where the person has mapped no tier, it asks on /dev/tty, offering each tier the models the catalog holds at the person's floor and list, and writes the answer into `models.harness` as `ur models set` does (§15.1), so no setting names a model the catalog lacks, such as Chutes' before G-PROV-chutes passes (CO-32); the examples show the shape:

```toml
# Codex: ~/.codex/ur.config.toml, used as `codex --profile ur`, so the person's own OpenAI setup is untouched
model_provider = "ur"
model = "chutes-<model>-tee-high"               # §6.3's canonical name
model_catalog_json = "~/.codex/ur-models.json"  # generated from the catalog: context, tools, reasoning
web_search = "disabled"                         # the gateway serves no hosted search (§21.7, CO-26);
                                                # agents search through MCP's web_search
[model_providers.ur]
name = "URnetwork compute"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1"
wire_api = "responses"
stream_idle_timeout_ms = 300000
[model_providers.ur.capabilities]
external_web_access = false                     # no hosted search or page opening, even under --yolo (§21.7)
[model_providers.ur.auth]
command = "/absolute/path/to/ur"
args = ["gateway", "token", "--harness", "codex"]
```

```json
// Claude Code: ~/.claude/ur-settings.json, which `ur claude` passes with `claude --settings`; with --default,
// these keys are merged into ~/.claude/settings.json instead, the person's own values kept to restore
{"apiKeyHelper": "/absolute/path/to/ur gateway token --harness claude-code",
 "permissions": {"deny": ["WebSearch"]},   // no hosted search: the MCP web_search instead (§21.7, CO-26)
 "env": {"ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>",
         "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL": "<provider>-<model>-high", "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL": "<provider>-<model>-medium",
         "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL": "local-<model>-off",
         "CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS": "<the smaller window of the opus and sonnet models>",
         "CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER": "0",     // no attribution block and its fingerprint (8.5)
         "CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC": "1",
         "CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS": "1"}}
```

Neither harness's own default changes unless the person asks: Codex gets the `ur` profile (`codex --profile ur`) and Claude Code a separate settings file that `ur claude` passes with `--settings`, so the person's own Anthropic or OpenAI setup keeps working beside the gateway; `ur install-harness <h> --default` makes the gateway that harness's default, keeping the values it replaced so `ur uninstall-harness` restores them. Codex's provider table must live in the user-level file, since a project's `.codex/config.toml` ignores providers ([Rpt:bb]). A canonical name carries its effort, so Codex's `model_reasoning_effort` and Claude Code's effort settings change nothing for it; `ur install-harness` writes one name per tier. `ur gateway config <h>` prints the same for any Chat Completions harness (OpenCode, Goose, Aider, Zed, Continue, Cline, Roo, pi); one that takes its key from a file or its environment, with no credential command to renew it, runs under `ur gateway run <h> -- <command>`, so no token outlives its hour (Q-GW-6). The install seals a hash of what it wrote, as DESIGN §16.7's config hash does, so an edit that widens a harness's settings shows as a changed config. A harness set to the gateway still runs its own hooks and MCP entry (DESIGN §16.7); the gateway adds the model calls. Claude Code takes one context window for all three of its slots, so the install writes the smaller window of the models in its opus and sonnet slots, and a background request past its haiku model's window gets Messages' own overflow error (8.5).

### 8.9 Recording

The gateway sees each call, so it writes the `model_call` entry itself (RECORD.md section 12's `ModelCallBody`) with the provider's request id, token counts and the charge, and, for a TEE call whose evidence the device verified, the attestation evidence of §6.8. It binds the call to a run by the harness's session headers where the harness sends them (Codex's `x-codex-window-id` and `x-client-request-id`; Claude Code's session in its hook events), else by harness, agent and time, labeled as an inference, as RECORD.md section 12's join already is. A hook's `model_call` for the same request id (DESIGN §16.7) merges with the gateway's, keeping the gateway's counts. Since CO-25 the gateway also records each call's whole request and response as session entries of that run, deduplicated against the run's earlier calls, so the run keeps what the model received and returned (§24.8); a call bound by harness, agent and time alone records its entries with the OR of the taint bits of every live run of the grant, failing closed (D-CTXH-9).

### 8.10 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Responses only, as CO-4 names | one API | Claude Code needs Messages; most others need Chat Completions | rejected: three fronts, one router |
| A hosted gateway at URnetwork | no daemon needed | URnetwork would see prompts, breaking the directive; or carry ciphertext only with the client's key on the server, which is the daemon | rejected |
| Expose the gateway beyond loopback for Cursor | Cursor works | a public, token-protected model endpoint billed to the person, with prompts in the clear to Cursor's cloud | rejected |
| Reuse LiteLLM as the gateway | mature translation | Python, a second router, its own key handling; no attestation | rejected |
| Store responses for `previous_response_id` | serves Agents-SDK clients | state on disk per conversation; Codex does not need it | Later |
| Serve Codex's and Claude Code's own hosted search on §21's tool | their built-in search works behind the gateway | it makes Parallel's Services available inside another vendor's tool, which Parallel's §2(c)(iv) bars (CO-26) | rejected: the gateway serves none, and they search through MCP (§21.7) |

### 8.11 Decisions proposed

**D-GW-1 (proposed).** Three API fronts (Responses, Chat Completions, Messages) over one router; Gemini later. *Why:* 8.3: no one API reaches the harnesses CO-4 names.

**D-GW-2 (proposed).** Stateless to its callers: no response is served from storage beyond D-GW-5's ten minutes, `store: true` and `previous_response_id` stay refused, and reasoning round-trips in a sealed blob the gateway alone opens; each call's request and response are recorded in the caller's run, sealed and deduplicated, and never read back to answer a call (§24.8). *Why:* Codex and Claude Code send full history; serving from state would be another plaintext store on disk and a dependency of every call; CO-25 asks for the history to be kept, not for calls to be served from it.

**D-GW-3 (proposed).** Per-harness grants, hour-long tokens minted by the harness's own credential command, budgets per grant under server-enforced defaults per device and agent; while a grant exists the daemon's unit holds the port, and a token goes only to a port whose listener proves it is the daemon (8.4). *Why:* attribution and a spend bound a local process cannot raise alone; I-7 is kept because the token neither administers, reads nor signs; harnesses do not authenticate the gateway, so no other user's process may take its port.

**D-GW-4 (proposed).** An empty balance is `insufficient_quota` (Responses, Chat Completions) and a 402 `billing_error` (Messages); a TEE that cannot be verified is a 503 `tee_unverified` naming the model, and nothing is retried elsewhere. *Why:* Codex does not retry `insufficient_quota`; R-GW-5.

**D-GW-5 (proposed).** Every stream ends with a terminal event; an identical request joins the call in flight or, within 10 minutes of its end, is answered from its kept response, which is sealed in the daemon's state and outlives a restart, and a planned restart waits for calls in flight; requests take 32 MiB, overflow errors keep each API's words, and Claude Code's attribution block reaches no provider. *Why:* a harness's automatic retry, mid-stream or after a restart, must not charge the person twice; harnesses resend whole histories with their images, and compact only on their own API's overflow error.

**D-GW-6 (proposed).** A gateway call that needs a disclosure the person has not acknowledged answers 403 `disclosure_required` before any provider is called, naming the id, its summary line and the fix, which the harness shows; the gateway never prompts, and `ur install-harness --gateway` asks on /dev/tty for the disclosures of the models it writes, or, on a tagged or cloud sidecar, names those the network has not acknowledged, an Owner's or Admin's acknowledgment for the network standing for the person's there. *Why:* CO-34, CO-41; no person is attached to a harness's call, so the fix must be findable from the error.

### 8.12 Questions

**Q-GW-1.** CO-4 says "responses api"; is that the only API? *Options:* (a) Responses only; (b) Responses plus Messages and Chat Completions. *Answer:* (b), as 8.3 shows: Claude Code speaks only Messages, and most open harnesses speak Chat Completions. *Decider:* owner.

**Q-GW-2.** Cursor? *Options:* (a) unsupported; (b) publish the gateway. *Answer:* (a): Cursor's custom endpoints are called from Cursor's servers, which would see every prompt, and the gateway would have to be public. *Decider:* owner.

**Q-GW-3.** Gemini CLI? *Options:* (a) Later; (b) at launch. *Answer:* (a); a fourth translation for one harness waits for demand. *Decider:* owner.

**Q-GW-4.** May the gateway forward to the person's own API keys for OpenAI, Anthropic or Google? *Options:* (a) never; (b) as an option. *Answer:* (a). CO-18 brings every provider URnetwork can reach into its catalog, paid from the compute balance under one namespace; a person's own keys are a separate matter, and a harness that wants them keeps its own provider settings beside the gateway's profile. *Decider:* owner.

**Q-GW-5.** Does the gateway run in the apps? *Options:* (a) desktop daemons and enclaves only; (b) everywhere. *Answer:* (a): phones run no external harness, and the apps' Harness calls the router in-process. An enclave runs it so Codex, Claude Code or PiG inside the enclave use the catalog (§11.10). *Decider:* owner.

**Q-GW-6.** How does a harness that takes its API key from a file or its environment, with no credential command to renew it (most Chat Completions harnesses, [Rpt:bb] gateway_harness_compat.md), keep working past a token's hour? *Options:* (a) a token that lives as long as its grant, written into the harness's own settings; (b) `ur gateway run <h> -- <command>`, which starts the harness with its base URL on a loopback port of its own and a session key that lives only in that process's environment and the runner's memory, and relays each call to the gateway under an hour-long token it renews; (c) restart such a harness each hour. *Answer:* (b). (a) leaves a long-lived credential on disk, past IC-11's hour; (c) breaks every session at the hour. Under (b) no credential reaches a file, the runner keeps §8.7's loopback, Host and Origin checks, its key ends with the process, and the grant, budget and recording are the harness's own, as for Codex and Claude Code; `ur gateway config <h>` prints this form for such a harness. *Decider:* owner.

### 8.13 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| A harness release changes its protocol use | high | that harness breaks | §18's gateway conformance suite per harness release; `ur status` names a harness version not yet tested |
| A same-user process spends the balance | medium | money | budgets per grant, hour-long tokens, `ur gateway grants` |
| Another user's process takes the gateway's port while the daemon is down | low | a harness sends a prompt and a live token to that process | the daemon's unit holds the port while a grant exists; a token only once the listener proves it is the daemon (8.4); a token lives an hour |
| Claude Code with non-Claude models misbehaves | medium | poor results | tested model list per release; the Haiku slot on a local model |

### 8.14 Phasing

M12: Responses and Chat Completions with Codex; M13: Messages with Claude Code, and the refusal of hosted web search for both (§21.7); Later: Gemini, stored responses.

## 9. The compute balance

### 9.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns the compute balance: its ledger, credits and how they are bought, auto-renew, the charges for inference, enclaves and web searches, holds and settlement, low-balance behavior, budgets' enforcement, refunds, statements, the spend view and fraud limits. How URnetwork pays providers is §10; who may spend is §16; the routes and tables are listed again in §14.

### 9.2 Requirements

| Id | Requirement | Source |
|---|---|---|
| R-BAL-1 | One compute balance per network, shared by inference, enclaves and web searches | CO-3, CO-16 |
| R-BAL-2 | Separate from the transfer balance: no conversion between them, and neither draws on the other | CO-3 |
| R-BAL-3 | Funded with credits bought in fiat and with auto-renew | CO-3, CO-10 |
