| R-BAL-4 | Each inference request, each enclave and each search has its own charges | CO-3, CO-16 |
| R-BAL-5 | Local inference is never charged | CO-9 |
| R-BAL-6 | No charge reveals content: a charge names a model, units and times, never a prompt, an output, a file or a query | directive; I-13 |
| R-BAL-7 | A network's owner, or its billing admins in a Team, see every charge and who caused it | derived; DESIGN §7.5 roles |
| R-BAL-8 | Spending stops before a network owes more than a bounded amount | derived |
| R-BAL-9 | Each service shows where its credits went: its total since the network's first charge, by provider and model, enclave and member, and its last 7 days, by those and by agent, to each of 9.10's roles as far as it sees, the person's own bot included | CO-22 |

### 9.3 What exists today

| Fact | Citation |
|---|---|
| Money is `model.NanoCents`, int64 USD × 10^9 | server/model/subscription_model.go:167-175 |
| The transfer balance is a byte ledger debited by contract settlement; Pro is an in-window `transfer_balance.pro` row | DESIGN §20.3; server/model/pro.go:429 |
| Payment markets: Stripe, App Store, Google Play, Gamma, Solana, Monero, Zcash, TAO, Bitcoin, ETH, x402, manual | server/PRO-GRANT-CYCLE.md:23-36 |
| Store purchases bind and reverse through existing models (`play_purchase_binding_model.go`, `apple_refund_reversal_model.go`, `store_notification_flow_model.go`), Stripe through `stripe_customer_model.go` and `stripe_invoice_payment_failure_model.go` | server/model/ |
| Escrow admission already uses Redis reservations that over-admit on loss and lease 24 h | server/model/subscription_redis_admission.go:19-24, :38 |
| Team billing runs on a `team_subscription` row and Stripe meters with a credit line drawn last | owner decisions [92](DESIGN.md#od-92), [199](DESIGN.md#od-199) |

Missing: any balance in dollars, any charge per request or per VM-minute, any off-session top-up.

### 9.4 The ledger

The compute balance is a set of **lots** per network, each a credit with what is left of it, and **charges** drawn from them. Postgres is the system of record; Redis holds the hot projection and the holds (9.7), as escrow admission does.

```sql
-- sidecar/model (owner decision 594); one migration group, MG-C1 (§14.4)
CREATE TABLE compute_account (
  network_id             uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  settled_nano_usd       bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,  -- sum of lots' remaining, less settled charges' overrun
  state                  smallint NOT NULL,          -- 1 active, 2 low, 3 grace, 4 suspended, 5 closed (9.9)
  negative_floor_nano_usd bigint NOT NULL,           -- how far below zero settlement may go (9.9)
  first_charge_day       date,                       -- the UTC day of its first charge: the spend view's "since" (9.13)
  version                bigint NOT NULL,
  update_time            timestamptz NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE compute_lot (
  lot_id            uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  network_id        uuid NOT NULL,
  kind              smallint NOT NULL,   -- 1 purchase, 2 subscription grant, 3 promotion, 4 adjustment
  market            smallint NOT NULL,   -- 1 stripe, 2 app_store, 3 google_play, 4 manual, 5 promotion (9.11)
  market_ref        text NOT NULL,       -- the PaymentIntent's id; the App Store's transaction id; Play's order id (9.5); a redemption's id (9.11)
  amount_nano_usd   bigint NOT NULL,
  remaining_nano_usd bigint NOT NULL,
  create_time       timestamptz NOT NULL,
  expire_time       timestamptz,         -- promotions only (9.11)
  reversed_time     timestamptz,         -- a refund or chargeback (9.12)
  lapsed_nano_usd   bigint,              -- what of a promotion was left at its expire_time (9.11)
  UNIQUE (market, market_ref)
);
CREATE TABLE compute_charge (            -- partitioned by day on start_time
  charge_id        uuid NOT NULL,
  network_id       uuid NOT NULL,
  kind             smallint NOT NULL,    -- 9.6's kinds
  subject_ref      uuid NOT NULL,        -- the request id (inference, search), the enclave id, the charge a refund returns (9.6), or a support case's id (kind 5)
  sidecar_id       uuid NOT NULL,        -- who caused it (I-13: an opaque id)
  agent_id         uuid,                 -- the agent, where the caller named one (§5.5's agent_id)
  member_id        uuid,                 -- whom it counts to (9.13): the sidecar's member, or a tagged sidecar's or enclave's sponsor, from the projection at the hold; empty for the network's own line
  enclave_id       uuid,                 -- enclave kinds, and a refund of one (9.6)
  catalog_id       text,                 -- the model or shape id (§6.3, §11.5)
  provider         smallint NOT NULL,    -- §4.6's provider id
  units            jsonb NOT NULL,       -- inference: input, output, cached tokens; enclave: seconds, GiB-hours; search: 1
  amount_nano_usd  bigint NOT NULL,      -- what the network pays
  cost_nano_usd    bigint NOT NULL,      -- what URnetwork pays the provider: in gamma (§10), or for a search in USDC (§21.8)
  start_time       timestamptz NOT NULL,
  end_time         timestamptz NOT NULL,
  settle_time      timestamptz NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (start_time, charge_id)
) PARTITION BY RANGE (start_time);
CREATE TABLE compute_charge_day (        -- the statement and spend rollup, kept 400 days (9.13)
  network_id uuid NOT NULL, day date NOT NULL, kind smallint NOT NULL, sidecar_id uuid NOT NULL, agent_id uuid,
  catalog_id text, member_id uuid, provider smallint NOT NULL, enclave_id uuid,  -- member: whom it counts to (9.13)
  input_tokens bigint NOT NULL, output_tokens bigint NOT NULL, cached_tokens bigint NOT NULL,  -- typed units, so
  seconds bigint NOT NULL, egress_bytes bigint NOT NULL, searches bigint NOT NULL,             -- an upsert adds them
  amount_nano_usd bigint NOT NULL, refunded_nano_usd bigint NOT NULL,  -- net of refunds; the refunds, positive (9.6)
  count bigint NOT NULL,                                               -- charges; a refund adds none
  UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (network_id, day, kind, sidecar_id, agent_id, catalog_id, member_id, provider, enclave_id)
);
CREATE TABLE compute_charge_total (      -- the spend view's totals, kept for the account's life (9.13)
  network_id uuid NOT NULL, kind smallint NOT NULL, member_id uuid, catalog_id text, provider smallint NOT NULL,
  enclave_id uuid,                                                     -- no day, no sidecar, no agent (Q-BAL-10)
  input_tokens bigint NOT NULL, output_tokens bigint NOT NULL, cached_tokens bigint NOT NULL,
  seconds bigint NOT NULL, egress_bytes bigint NOT NULL, searches bigint NOT NULL,
  amount_nano_usd bigint NOT NULL, refunded_nano_usd bigint NOT NULL, count bigint NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (network_id, kind, member_id, catalog_id, provider, enclave_id)
);
CREATE TABLE compute_charge_pruned (     -- the day rows dropped past 400 days, summed, for the totals' check (9.13)
  network_id uuid NOT NULL, kind smallint NOT NULL, amount_nano_usd bigint NOT NULL, count bigint NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (network_id, kind)
);
```

A charge draws lots in this order: unexpired promotions by nearest expiry, then subscription grants, then purchases, oldest first, a web search's charge passing over promotions (9.11). The draw is recorded in `compute_charge_lot (charge_id, lot_id, amount_nano_usd)` so a refund (9.12) knows what a lot paid for. Per-request rows live 90 days, a web search's 72 hours (§21.5), and roll into `compute_charge_day`, which lives 400 days: long enough for a year's statements and disputes, and no longer, since each row says when a sidecar used which model (§14.6's compute-3). `compute_charge_total` keeps the same sums with no day, sidecar or agent, for the account's life, and is deleted with the network: the spend view's totals (9.13) outlive the day rows without keeping when, or on which device, anything was used, since an agent's id would name one device's agent (DESIGN §5.5; Q-BAL-10). `compute_charge_pruned` keeps, per kind, the sums of the day rows dropped past 400 days, so the totals can be checked against the day rows (9.13). Both rollups' units are typed columns, which an upsert adds exactly; their `UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT` needs PostgreSQL 15 or later (§14.4).

### 9.5 Credits and how they are bought

A **credit** is one US dollar of compute balance. The balance shows in dollars; "credits" name what is bought.

| Market | What is sold | Auto-renew | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stripe (web, desktop app, `ur compute buy`) | packs of 10, 25, 50, 100, 250 and 500 credits at that many dollars, tax added by Stripe Tax; none of 5, on which Stripe's fees take 9% (§10.6) | threshold top-up (9.8) on a card its payer saved for it, and a monthly plan | Checkout saves a card for off-session use (`setup_future_usage=off_session`) only when the person paying turns on threshold top-up or the monthly plan in that act, to a Stripe customer for that network and that payer, its mandate naming both; auto-renew charges only a card its own holder saved for it, so no one's change of the settings charges another person's card, and a payer who leaves the network or loses the role that let them buy detaches it, which stops threshold top-ups until another is saved |
| App Store | consumables of 10, 25, 50 and 100 credits; auto-renewing subscriptions granting 10, 25, 50 or 100 credits a month, in one subscription group | the subscription | priced at the store's tier that nets at least the web price after the commission URnetwork pays there (Q-BAL-3): 15% in the small-business program and for a subscription past its first year, else 30% |
| Google Play | the same as the App Store | the subscription | as above |

The credit is applied only when the market says the money is final: Stripe's `payment_intent.succeeded`, the App Store's signed transaction (and `DID_RENEW` for a renewal), Play's verified purchase (and `SUBSCRIPTION_RENEWED`). Each lot's `(market, market_ref)` is unique, so a webhook replayed twice credits once; the reference is Stripe's PaymentIntent, the App Store's transaction id or Play's order id, each new at every purchase and renewal, since a Play subscription keeps one purchase token across its renewals, and a key on the token would credit it once ever. Store renewals reuse the existing notification paths (server/model/store_notification_flow_model.go) with a new product family, `compute.*`, so a compute subscription never grants Pro and a Pro subscription never grants credits.

**Store products** (D-BAL-8). A plan change that takes effect at once, an App Store upgrade with its prorated refund or a Play replacement that gives back the old plan's unused time, grants the new plan's credits less the old plan's for the part of its period the store gives back, so stepping through the plans in one sitting grants about the largest plan's credits, not their sum; a downgrade takes effect at the next renewal. A consumable is credited from the app's report or the store's notification, whichever comes first, and only then finished: the app calls `finish()` on the App Store's transaction when the server's answer arrives, and the server consumes a Play purchase (`purchases.products.consume`) at once, well within the three days after which Play refunds a purchase never acknowledged; a transaction left unfinished is reported again at the app's next launch and credits nothing twice. A purchase that names no network, such as a promotion code redeemed in the store, binds as Pro's do (`play_purchase_binding_model.go`, `apple_offer_code_binding_model.go`): to the network whose app reports it, its renewals and plan changes following the chain. One naming a deleted network credits none and is refunded through Play, or answered by support on the App Store, where only Apple refunds. A store build offers web checkout only in the storefronts whose rules allow a link to it (the US App Store's since the 2025 ruling), and counsel reads the stores' rules before the products are submitted (§19.2): Play's payments policy says in-app virtual currency "must only be used within the app or game title for which they were purchased", and compute credit is spent by the CLI, the gateway and enclaves too.

Purchase limits (9.11) apply before checkout opens, a network's from its own purchases and a payer's once its card is known: Checkout captures a card payment only after its fingerprint passes the payer's limits, and cancels it uncaptured otherwise; a store purchase, whose payer URnetwork learns only after the store took the money, is credited, and one past its payer's limits flagged for review. A balance is capped at $10,000 a network; a purchase that would pass it is refused before payment.

### 9.6 Charges

Every charge is one row with one kind; nothing is netted or bundled, so each inference and each enclave has its own lines (CO-3).

| Kind | Charged for | Units | Rate | When written |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 `inference` | one remote inference request | input tokens, output tokens (reasoning included), cached-input tokens | the catalog model's three per-million-token prices (§6.3) | when the request ends, from the usage the provider reports (9.7) |
| 2 `enclave_run` | one enclave's running time | seconds in `running` (§11.6) | the shape's price per hour (§11.5), per second | every 10 minutes while running, and at stop |
| 3 `enclave_disk` | reserved for persistent enclave volumes, which are Later (§11.9): no disk outlives a VM | — | — | never, at launch |
| 4 `enclave_host_egress` | bytes an enclave sends out through its provider's network under default egress off (§11.8) | GiB | the provider's egress price, where it bills one; else none | hourly |
| 5 `adjustment` | a support credit or debit, naming no charge; a refund is a charge of the kind it returns (below) | — | — | by `sidecarctl compute adjust`, with a reason |
| 6 `web_search` | one web search (§21) | searches: one per authorization Base shows used | the catalog price per search (§21.8) | when Base shows its payment settled; its times kept to the minute (§21.5) |

**Refunds.** A charge is refunded by a negative charge of its own kind, whose `subject_ref` names it and which carries its member, agent, model, provider and enclave, so the refund nets into that charge's service (9.13, Q-BAL-12). It is written by `sidecarctl compute adjust --refund <charge>`, with a reason, and when a dispute is upheld (§6.7); an unanswered direct call is never charged, so none is refunded for that (§6.6). Its `charge_id` is the UUIDv5, in a fixed namespace, of the charge it names, so a charge is refunded at most once and a retry adds nothing; its `start_time` is when it is written, so it counts to that UTC day and never reopens a closed one; it returns its amount to the lots the refunded charge drew, in reverse draw order, as negative draws in `compute_charge_lot`, a promotion past its expiry forfeiting its part as expiry does (Q-BAL-4); and its `cost_nano_usd` moves URnetwork's cost only as far as the provider's bill moved, zero for a refund at URnetwork's cost, so reconciliation (§10.7) still matches what providers billed. A refund wanted after its charge's row is gone (90 days, a search's 72 hours) is a support credit. A support credit or debit (kind 5) names no charge: its `subject_ref` is its support case's id, its `sidecar_id` the nil UUID and its `provider` 0, and it counts to the network's own line.

Local inference writes no charge (R-BAL-5): the device runs it, and nothing reaches the broker (§6.5). A web search is charged as kind 6 whichever model asked for it, local ones included (CO-16). A web fetch is no charge: its bytes are transfer (§22.7). Nor is a calendar call (§23.7). A search's own bytes, through the egress, are transfer too. An enclave's traffic through URnetwork (its overlay traffic and its default egress under `auto` or `exits`) is transfer, counted toward the transfer balance as all traffic is ([owner decision 10](DESIGN.md#od-10)); kind 4 covers only the provider's own bandwidth, which no URnetwork contract carries.

**Prices.** A price is the provider's price for the same unit, in gamma, times the compute markup, rounded up: per-million-token prices to $0.001, hourly prices to $0.001, per-search prices to $0.0001. The markup is 1.20 on every model and shape, whichever market bought the credits (Q-BAL-2, CO-35); a store's commission is carried in the price of its credit packs, never in the markup (Q-BAL-3, 9.5). The catalog (§6.3) carries the network's price for each model and shape; the broker re-reads a provider's prices hourly and the catalog's every 24 h, so a provider's price rise reaches users within a day, and a charge always uses the price in the catalog version the request named (9.7), so a user is never charged a price they were not shown; the broker takes a version only while it is current, or for 24 hours after a newer one, so no client keeps an old price, and a provider whose price varies by request is listed at the most it charges (§6.3).

### 9.7 Holds and settlement

The broker (`computeservice`, §14) is the only place a charge is made.

```text
inference   1 the device sends the request's clear header (§6.6): catalog version, model, max_input_tokens,
              max_output_tokens; the body is ciphertext the broker cannot read
            2 hold = the model's worst case: its context window × in_price + its maximum output × out_price,
              in a Redis script on {cmp_<network_id>} that refuses when settled - unsettled - open holds - hold
              would fall below zero, the floor (9.9) being kept for enclave intervals, when a budget (§16.4)
              would be passed, or when the provider's account could not cover it (§10.4: capacity)
            3 the broker forwards; the provider's TEE answers ciphertext and a clear usage trailer
              (input, output, cached tokens), or the provider's own usage record names the request
            4 settle: charge = usage × prices of the named catalog version; the hold is released and the charge
              appended to the settlement stream; usage above the declared maxima is still charged (below)
            5 the device compares the charge with its own count (§6.7) and raises charge_mismatch beyond 2%
direct      at authorization, a hold of the declared model's worst case, against the balance and budgets as
            above, one hold per authorization (§6.6); the exposure rule: since the broker cannot read the
            body's model, URnetwork carries the gap to the provider's costliest model, and the script also
            refuses while the network's open direct calls, each charged at its provider's costliest worst case,
            would leave it more than $5 below its floor; settle from the provider's signed receipt, else its
            usage record for the nonce or the body hash (N2), at the catalog prices of the model the provider
            reports (outside the catalog, its own charge × the markup); the lookup answers unknown (the hold
            released at no charge), in progress (kept) or finished (settled); while it fails the hold stays
            pending, never charged, and is released at no charge after 24 hours (§6.6)
search      at authorization, hold one search's price (the same script, balance and budgets, and 9.11's
            search cap; refused in grace or suspended, and where available less the network's unexpired
            promotional credit, which pays no search, would fall below zero, 9.11); settle when Base shows
            the authorization used, drawing no promotional lot; a lapsed one releases its hold (§21.8)
enclave     every 10 minutes the orchestrator writes the interval's enclave_run charge and holds the next
            10 minutes, against the balance and the floor alone: budgets (§16.4) bound calls and
            searches, never an enclave's running time; a hold the floor refuses is cut to what is left
            above -floor, the network's indexer enclave drawing its reserve and then 72 hours past it (9.9),
            and the enclave's stop is scheduled for when that runs out at its rate; a new enclave's first
            10 minutes are held from `requested`, released if it never runs (§11.6)
settlement  a taskworker job, compute_settle, every 2 s or 500 charges, moves the stream into Postgres in one
            transaction a batch: charges, lot draws, compute_account, and the day and lifetime rollups of
            the charges it inserts (9.13); idempotent: each producer derives a charge's charge_id and
            start_time from its subject (an inference's or search's request id and the time of its hold; an
            enclave interval's enclave id, incarnation and number on a fixed 10-minute grid, start_time the
            grid's start; a refund's from the charge it names, 9.6), so a charge sent twice meets the
            (start_time, charge_id) key; it inserts with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING and rolls up only
            the rows returned
projection  {cmp_<network_id>} holds available = settled - unsettled charges - open holds, and promo, the
            unexpired promotional credit left (9.11), both rebuilt from Postgres when absent; a lost Redis
            shard over-admits at most the holds then open, as escrow admission does;
            admission alone reads available, while the balance, settled - unsettled charges - the running
            enclaves' time accrued in their current interval, holds left out, drives auto-renew (9.8) and the
            states (9.9), since a hold is a worst case, not spend
```

The hold is the worst case because the broker cannot see the request: the true `max_tokens` is inside the ciphertext, and compressed ciphertext bounds no token count. A request can never use more than its model's context and maximum output, so it is never charged more than its hold, and every open request's worst case is already counted against the balance; calls and searches hold only down to zero, the floor being kept for enclave intervals, so a network can owe at most the floor, whatever its devices declare or however many requests run at once. A direct call is held at its declared model's worst case, since that is what an honest device sends; the broker cannot read which model the body names, so URnetwork carries the gap to the provider's costliest model, up to $5 a network, under the exposure rule above: a device that lies on every open call leaves its network at most $5 below its floor, is charged in full and flagged (§6.6, 9.11). Holds release at settlement, a second or so after a call ends. At catalog prices, the 1.20 markup included, the costliest model in §4.4 (a 1M-token context at $1.85 per million in and 32K out at $9.50, provider prices) holds about $2.58, and a small model, a 256K context at $0.12 per million in and 32K out at $0.48, about $0.05: a $10 balance runs a hundred such TEE calls at once. Direct calls run as many at once as the exposure rule admits: where the provider's costliest worst case is $3, five on a $10 balance, three on $5, and one at a time down to the last cent, so nothing is stranded. A call refused while open holds, not the balance, stand in the way answers `held` with a retry time (§6.6), so no one is asked for credit they have. The provider's usage is the source of truth for the charge because it is also what URnetwork pays (§10): the device's own count is a check, not a bill.

### 9.8 Auto-renew

Auto-renew has two modes per network, set by its owner or a billing admin (`ur compute auto-renew`, the apps):

```text
threshold   when the balance (9.7), holds left out, falls below T (default $5), charge the card its payer
            saved for it (9.5) for pack P (default $20),
            at most 3 times a day and up to a monthly limit L (default $200); Stripe only, since the stores
            sell no off-session consumable; the charge is an off-session PaymentIntent with confirm=true;
            an authentication_required answer emails a link and turns threshold off until the owner returns
monthly     on the same day each month, add M credits (10, 25, 50, 100 or 250): a Stripe subscription, or a
            store subscription from 9.5's table; unused credits carry over and do not expire
```

A failed threshold charge retries after 1 h and 6 h, emails the billing contacts each time, and after the third failure turns threshold off and says so in `ur compute status` and the apps. A store subscription's failure follows the store's billing retry; the credits of a period are granted only on its renewal. Both modes can be on at once: the monthly grant arrives on its day, and the threshold covers the rest of the month. Turning a mode off cancels only charges not yet sent to Stripe, as Pay with Gamma's switches do (mmm/BTCPAY.md §18.5).

### 9.9 Low balance, grace and suspension

```text
state      enters when                                   effect
active     balance >= 24 h of the network's burn          none
low        balance < 24 h of burn, or < T                SidecarEvent compute_low on every member device
                                                         and an email to billing contacts; threshold
                                                         auto-renew fires once the balance < T (9.8)
grace      balance <= 0                                  new remote inference and searches refused (402 COMPUTE_BALANCE);
                                                         running enclaves keep running down to the floor
suspended  balance <= -floor, or grace older than 1 h    enclaves stopped (11.6), keeping nothing but what is
                                                         in EVS; remote inference refused
closed     the network is deleted                        enclaves removed; lots refunded where 9.12 allows
```

Local inference runs in every state, since it writes no charge and asks no server (CO-9, IC-5). The states read the balance (9.7), which leaves open holds out, so a call that costs a cent neither fires a top-up nor moves a state. The floor is the smaller of $5 and one hour of the network's running enclaves' rates, and only enclave intervals reach into it, each cut to what is left above it and stopped when that runs out (9.7), so a network owes at most the floor, which is never more than $5, plus up to 72 hours of its indexer enclave's price in that enclave's grace (below), and up to $5 more only where a device of its lied about a direct call's model, which URnetwork carries (§6.6). Burn is the trailing 24 h of charges, or the running enclaves' hourly rates × 24 if larger. A top-up that lifts the balance above zero returns the account to `active` or `low` at once and restarts the enclaves suspension stopped, as new incarnations (§11.4) that re-sync their work from EVS (§11.9): each by its keeper under §11.7's rule, else once its sponsor starts it, the apps prompting; an enclave a person or a run stopped stays stopped (§11.11). Each state change raises `compute_low` with the new state on every member device, and grace and suspension email the billing contacts again; from `low` on, the notice names the enclaves a suspension would stop, and the days the network's indexer enclave's reserve and grace leave before its mail waits on senders' retries (DESIGN §15.6; below), and each stopped enclave's card says the balance stopped it (§7.6).

**The network's indexer enclave** (§11.10, Q-ENC-11) keeps its own reserve: at setup, 7 days of its price move into `compute_account`'s `indexer_reserve`, which neither `available` nor the balance the states read counts (9.7), and which only the indexer's `enclave_run` charges draw, once the rest can no longer pay them; it is refilled while the account is `active`. At suspension every other enclave stops as above, while the indexer runs on its reserve, then on 72 hours of grace, its intervals held past the floor by up to 72 hours of its price, as the bound above allows; each notice from `low` on counts its days down. A chargeback's suspension (9.11) stops it only once what of its reserve no reversed lot funded, and its grace, are spent. A top-up refills the reserve first, and the keeper restarts the indexer if it stopped.

### 9.10 Who buys, who spends, who sees

| Role (DESIGN §7.5) | Buy credits, redeem a promotion code, set auto-renew | Spend | See charges and the spend view |
|---|---|---|---|
| Owner | yes | per policy (§16) | all |
| Billing admin (Team) | yes | per policy | all |
| Admin | no | per policy | all |
| Network admin | no | per policy | all |
| IT admin | no | per policy | all |
| Auditor | no | no | all |
| Member | no, unless the policy names `compute:buy` (§16.2) | per policy and budget | their own and their agents' |
| Agent, tagged sidecar, enclave | never | per policy and budget | none, but its own run's cost in the record; an agent on its person's consented device (untagged, neither ephemeral nor Delegation-admitted, DESIGN §7.9) sees that person's spend view (9.13), never charges, through `compute_spend` |

Charges and the spend view are visible through `GET api/compute/charges` and `GET api/compute/spend` (§14.3) to the roles above, filtered server-side, for a Member, to the charges whose stored member (9.4) is theirs, so a SponsorSet moves no earlier charge; the record also carries each run's cost (RECORD.md section 13.1's `RunCostBody`), which §6.8 fills from the charges.

### 9.11 Limits and fraud

| Limit | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| balance cap | $10,000 a network | bounds the liability of unspent credit and a stolen card's reach |
| new account purchase | $100 a day and $200 in its first 7 days, for each network and for each payer (below), a payer's 7 days counted from its first purchase anywhere | card testing and stolen cards, keyed to the payer too, since networks are free and a fraudster can make one for each purchase |
| daily load | at most $1,500 a UTC day for each network and for each payer, across markets (Q-BAL-15) | the closed-loop exclusion's $2,000 a device a day (§10.8); without it, after day 7 only the balance cap bounds a day |
| the payer | a keyed hash of a Stripe card's `fingerprint`, one card across customers and networks, or of an App Store purchase's `appTransactionId`, one Apple Account in the app; Play names no account, so a Play purchase counts to its network alone; the hashes, a payer's first purchase day and its day's sums are kept apart from any network (compute-2) | limits that follow the money's source, not only the network a fraudster made |
| searches a day | whatever its policy's `day_max` says, at most 200 for a network until 7 days after its oldest unreversed paid lot, then 2,000; more only by URnetwork's review of its payment history (`sidecarctl compute search-cap`) | search is the one path from a stolen card to USDC (CO-29, §21.9), and a chargeback takes back the USDC and the percentage both, so its cap is the broker's, which a fraudster administering its own network cannot raise |
| enclaves for a new account | 1 CPU enclave until 24 h after its first successful payment; GPU shapes after $50 of lifetime purchases | mining with stolen cards is the expected abuse (§17) |
| promotions | none automatic; codes by campaign (below): each lot at most $10, lapsing 30 days after redemption, one a network a code and one a network in 30 days, within its code's cap and last day; counted as a load toward the daily load and the balance cap; never paying for a search | free compute draws abuse, and a search may pay a member's own address (CO-29) |
| chargeback | compute suspended for the network, enclaves stopped, the network's indexer enclave once what of its reserve no reversed lot funded, and its grace, are spent (9.9), the lot reversed | the money is gone |
| a direct call serving another model than declared | the served model charged and the network flagged; after review, or a second mismatch in 30 days, its direct calls refused, never its enclaves or TEE calls (§6.6) | the broker cannot read a direct call's body, so the provider's receipt is the check, and an alias the provider maps to the declared model is no mismatch |

Stripe Radar screens every card payment, with 3-D Secure requested on first purchases above $50.

**Promotion codes** (CO-35, D-BAL-12). These are URnetwork's own codes, apart from the stores' offer codes, which arrive as store purchases (9.5). An operator makes each with `sidecarctl compute promo create`, naming its campaign, its value (at most $10), its cap on redemptions and its last day, and whether a network must hold an unreversed paid lot to redeem it, which every code with a cap above one asks; the server keeps a keyed hash of the code, its case folded, with who made it and why (§14.4). A code is 8 to 32 letters and digits; one made for a single network is 16 random characters, about 80 bits. A person who may buy (9.10) redeems one on the compute screen (`Compute().Redeem`, §15.4) or with `ur compute redeem <code>`, which a harness process among its ancestors cannot run (§15.1); no agent, MCP tool, tagged sidecar or enclave reaches `POST api/compute/promo/redeem` (§14.3). In one transaction the route checks the code, known, before its last day and under its cap, and the network: no earlier redemption of this code, none of any code in the last 30 days, a paid lot where the code asks for one, no suspension for a chargeback, and the code's value counted as a load with the day's purchases against the daily load limit and the balance cap above, so purchases and codes together stay under the closed-loop exclusion's daily value (§10.8); it then writes the redemption, a kind-3 lot of market `promotion` whose `market_ref` is the redemption's id and whose `expire_time` is 30 days on, and the code's count. A retry finds the network's redemption and answers its lot, crediting nothing twice. A refusal names its reason (`code_unknown`, `code_ended`, `code_redeemed`, `redeemed_recently`, `paid_lot_required`, `daily_limit`, `balance_cap`), and after five failed codes in a UTC day a network's attempts answer `rate_limited` until the next. A promotional lot has no payer: it counts toward no payer's limits, nor toward the new-account purchase limits, which bound cards, and raises none. It pays for remote inference and enclaves, drawn first (9.4), and never for web search: a search draws only subscription and purchased lots, and its hold is refused where `available` less the unexpired promotional credit would fall below zero (9.7), since a search may pay an address of the member's own (CO-29, §10.8), which would turn free credit into USDC, and no search is free (Q-SRCH-5). At its `expire_time` what is left of the lot lapses (`compute_promo_lapse`, §14.5) and the month's statement shows it (9.13); a chargeback in the network lapses its promotional lots at once, and a refund never returns one (9.12).

### 9.12 Refunds and reversals

- **Stripe purchases:** the unspent part of a lot is refundable for 30 days from purchase on request (`ur compute refund`, the apps, support), never the spent part; promotions never.
- **Store purchases:** refunds are the store's; a refund notification reverses the lot (`reversed_time`), and what it had paid for stays charged, so the account may go negative, to `suspended` if below the floor, until topped up.
- **Closure:** a deleted network's unspent purchased credit is refunded to the card where the market allows within 90 days of purchase, and otherwise forfeited with notice at deletion.

### 9.13 Statements

`ur compute statement --month YYYY-MM` and the apps give a month's charges by kind, model, enclave, member and agent, from `compute_charge_day`, and the lots bought or redeemed, with what of a promotion lapsed; Stripe's and the stores' own receipts are the tax documents. A statement names sidecars and agents by their labels, resolved on the device from the config (§14.6 keeps labels off the server).

**Spend** (CO-22). The spend view says where a network's credits went: for each service, its total since the network's first charge and its last 7 days, and both for all services together. `GET api/compute/spend` serves it (§14.3); `ur compute spend` (§15.1), the sdk's `Compute().Spend()` and the apps' compute screen (§15.4) show it; the person's own bot reads it through `compute_spend` (§7.5).

| Service | Charges (9.6) | Breakdowns (`--by`; agent: the last 7 days only) |
|---|---|---|
| Remote inference | kind 1 | provider; model, by canonical name (§6.3); member; agent |
| Enclaves | kinds 2 (running time) and 4 (host egress), each its own line | enclave; shape (`--by model`); provider; member, the sponsor |
| Web search | kind 6 | member; agent; one provider, Parallel, and no mode, which the broker never learns (§21.5) |
| Adjustments | kind 5, net: support credits negative, debits positive; a refund nets into its charge's service instead (9.6) | the network's own line |
| Web fetch | none | no charge: its bytes count toward the transfer balance (§22.7) |
| Calendar | none | no charge: a calendar call's bytes count toward the transfer balance (§23.7) |
| Connected services | none | no charge: a connection's calls and refreshes are transfer (§25.8) |

Local inference never appears: it writes no charge (R-BAL-5). Recording takes no compute charge (§24.10). Open holds and a running enclave's current 10 minutes are not spend yet; the view shows them apart, as "held", from the balance (9.7).

- **Exact.** Every figure is a sum of settled charges in nano-USD, shown to the cent ("< $0.01" below one), exact as of the last settlement, seconds behind (Q-BAL-9); the route reads the total, the 7 days and `compute_account.update_time`, the settlement time it reports, in one REPEATABLE READ transaction, so the figures are of one moment. A charge is never rewritten: a refund is a negative charge of the kind it returns (9.6), so the figures only ever add rows, and each service's figures are net of its refunds, which the view shows as "after $x refunded" (Q-BAL-12).
- **UTC days.** The last 7 days are today so far and the 6 UTC days before it, each charge counted to the UTC day of its start, `(start_time AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')::date` and never a cast in the session's time zone, as `compute_charge_day`, the charge partitions, which are bounded in UTC, and the statements count; the apps show the window's bounds in the person's local time beside "UTC" (Q-BAL-8).
- **Where the figures come from.** `compute_settle` adds each charge it inserts, in the same transaction, to its `compute_charge_day` row and its `compute_charge_total` row, and sets `compute_account.first_charge_day` to the earliest of its charges' days and the day already there, `LEAST(first_charge_day, day)`, since charges can settle out of start order (a direct call's minutes after it ends, or up to a day while its provider's lookup fails; 9.4, 9.7). A refund adds its negative amount to `amount_nano_usd` and its size to `refunded_nano_usd`, and changes neither `count` nor the units. The total reads `compute_charge_total`, the 7 days read 7 days of `compute_charge_day`, and neither reads the per-request rows; `compute_rollup_day` re-derives each closed day from its charges, grouped by their stored columns, and alarms on a difference; it also checks, for each network and kind, that `compute_charge_total`'s sums equal `compute_charge_day`'s plus `compute_charge_pruned`'s, which holds in every snapshot, since `compute_settle` writes a charge to both rollups in one transaction and the job moves each dropped day row into `compute_charge_pruned` in one, and alarms on a difference (§14.5). Both rollups start with the ledger in M12, so every charge is in them.
- **Who.** A charge counts to the member the broker writes on it (9.4) from the projection it checked at the hold: an untagged device's member, or the sponsor of a tagged sidecar or an enclave (DESIGN §7.7; §11.4); a later SponsorSet, removal or revocation moves no earlier charge. Work another member drives in a sponsor's enclave, by the sponsor's consent (§7.10), counts to the sponsor, whose budget it spends. The route filters by 9.10's roles: an Owner, Billing admin, Admin, Network admin, IT admin or Auditor sees the network's spend; a Member what counts to them; an agent only its person's, through `compute_spend` on that person's consented device (Q-BAL-11). "Held" is the network's for the roles that see the network's spend; a Member's view, and every agent's, shows only the holds of sidecars that count to its member, which each hold records.
- **Labels.** The server answers ids and numbers (I-13); the device names them, as statements do: members from the config; enclaves by the name their incarnations were admitted with (§11.4); agents by their cards (§20.5) where the viewer may read the member's agents repo, else as an agent of that member; models and shapes from the catalog (§6.3). An id the device cannot resolve shows as "unknown". Labels from signed sources reach a model as plain text: members from the config, enclaves from their admissions, TEE models from the signed policy (§5.4), local models from the release's manifest. Any other label reaches a model only between untrusted-data markers and does not taint: a catalog id no signed source names (a direct model's, a shape's, one gone from the policy), labeled as the broker's and shown only within §6.3's grammar and 96 characters, else as "unknown"; and an agent name from any writer other than an untainted run on the member's untagged device, labeled with its writer, as `agent_list`'s stubs do (§20.6). The device takes only the answer's ids and typed numbers (9.4) and drops any other field.

### 9.14 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hold the compute balance in the transfer-balance tables with a new unit | one ledger | CO-3 says separate; bytes and dollars do not mix in one row type | rejected |
| Bill compute post-paid on Stripe meters, as Team overage is | no prepayment | CO-3 asks for credits and auto-renew; post-paid exposes URnetwork to unpaid GPU hours | rejected |
| Hold the balance on chain (gamma the user mints) | no fiat handling | CO-10: users pay fiat; a user's coldkey would be public and linked (mmm/BTCPAY.md §18.8) | rejected |
| Charge inference per day in one line | fewer rows | CO-3 asks for a charge per inference | rejected |
| Count tokens on the server | no device declaration | the server sees no plaintext (directive) | impossible |
| Keep lifetime spend on devices, in EVS, folded from the day rows | the server keeps nothing past 400 days | each viewer's devices keep their own fold, without a gap, a member's unable to read an admin's; the figures derive from charges the server holds anyway | rejected: server totals with no day, sidecar or agent (Q-BAL-10) |
| Roll the day rows up once a day, as statements alone would need | fewer writes at settlement | today's spend unseen until tomorrow, the day a person most often asks about | rejected: rolled up at settlement (Q-BAL-9) |

### 9.15 Decisions proposed

**D-BAL-1 (proposed).** The compute balance is lots and charges in Postgres with a Redis projection and holds, settled every 2 s by `compute_settle`. *Why:* the escrow admission pattern already carries this load shape (DESIGN §20.3), and I-12 keeps Postgres off any per-packet path, which compute's per-request path is not.

**D-BAL-2 (proposed).** A credit is one US dollar; balances, prices and charges are nano-USD. *Why:* gamma is USD-valued (§10.2), so prices and balances need no conversion, and the user carries no exchange-rate risk; URnetwork carries TAO's movement between buying it and minting, which the margin table and the weekly realized margin watch (§10.6, §10.7, Q-GAMMA-4).

**D-BAL-3 (proposed).** The provider's reported usage is what a request is charged; the device checks it and raises `charge_mismatch`. *Why:* the server cannot count tokens it cannot read, and the provider's usage is also what URnetwork pays.

**D-BAL-4 (proposed).** Enclaves are charged per second, written every 10 minutes, with the next 10 minutes held. *Why:* providers price by the hour or finer; 10 minutes bounds both the hold and the write rate.

**D-BAL-5 (proposed).** Holds are each request's worst case, a direct call's its declared model's, against the balance and budgets alike; calls and searches hold down to zero and enclave intervals down to the floor (the smaller of $5 and an hour of the network's enclaves); and URnetwork carries a direct call's gap to its provider's costliest model up to $5 a network, under the exposure rule; so a network owes at most the floor, plus up to 72 hours of its indexer enclave's price in that enclave's grace (§9.9), and $5 more only where a device of its lied about a direct call's model. *Why:* R-BAL-8; the broker cannot see a request's own limits; holding the provider's costliest model on every direct call would strand small balances (Q-BAL-14); a stopped enclave loses nothing that matters, since its work lives in EVS (§11.9).

**D-BAL-6 (proposed).** The spend view gives each service (remote inference, enclaves, web search, adjustments; web fetch and calendar calls at no charge) its total since the network's first charge and its last 7 UTC days, net of refunds, exact to the last settlement, from two rollups `compute_settle` writes with each charge: `compute_charge_day`, kept 400 days, and `compute_charge_total`, kept for the account's life with no day, sidecar or agent; the server answers ids and numbers, and the device names them. *Why:* CO-22; R-BAL-9; no view reads the per-request rows, and past 400 days nothing but the network's first charge day says when, and nothing says on which device (Q-BAL-8 to Q-BAL-10, Q-BAL-12).

**D-BAL-7 (proposed).** The person's own bot reads the spend view through `compute_spend` (R), in the Harness and over MCP, only on the person's consented device (untagged, neither ephemeral nor Delegation-admitted) and within the person's role, a label no signed source vouches for reaching the model only between untrusted-data markers (9.13); agents on tagged sidecars and in enclaves read none, and no agent reads charge rows, lots or payment methods. *Why:* CO-22, asked of the bot tab (CO-19); I-7; I-9; R-BAL-6 (Q-BAL-11).

**D-BAL-8 (proposed).** The apps report store purchases through `api`'s existing verify routes (`Compute().StorePurchase`), each bound to its network by the purchase's account token, or as Pro's are where it names none, and credited once by its transaction or order id, whichever of the app's report and the store's notification comes first, a plan change granting only the difference (9.5); `insufficient_quota` names whether the balance or a budget ran out, and the Harness offers "add credit" to a person who may buy and "raise the budget" as kind 21 (the `compute_budget_raise` tool, `ur compute budget raise`, `Compute().RaiseBudget`); credits go on sale once something the network may use can spend them (Q-BAL-13). *Why:* CO-3; CO-19's "add credit and select a remote model"; CO-35's per-agent budgets; Pro's store purchases already report this way.

**D-BAL-9 (proposed).** Auto-renew and 9.9's states read the balance, settled less unsettled charges and running enclaves' accrued time, holds left out; admission alone reads `available`; a direct call has one hold per authorization, settled by the provider's three-state lookup, and a hold the lookup cannot answer stays pending and is never charged; a refused enclave interval is cut to what is left and its enclave stopped when it runs out. *Why:* a hold is a worst case, not spend, so a call costing a cent must not charge a card or move a state, nor a provider's outage settle a balance to zero and stop enclaves; R-BAL-8.

**D-BAL-10 (proposed).** Purchase limits follow the payer as well as the network: a new payer, like a new network, buys at most $100 a day and $200 in its first 7 days, and every payer and network at most $1,500 a UTC day; and the broker caps a network's searches by the age of its paid credit, a cap no policy raises. *Why:* networks are free, so limits per network alone reset with each one a fraudster makes; search is the one path from a stolen card to USDC (CO-29), where a chargeback takes back the USDC and the percentage both; §10.8's closed loop rests on a daily limit under $2,000 (Q-BAL-15, Q-SRCH-15).

**D-BAL-11 (proposed).** Disputes count by network, at most 10 a network a day, and page a person, never changing the catalog by themselves; an hourly canary of known token counts checks each provider's usage and bill. *Why:* a dispute is a claim only the device can check, so a few modified clients must not remove a provider; comparing two of the provider's own numbers catches an inflating broker, not an overcounting provider (§6.7).

**D-BAL-12 (proposed).** Promotion codes are URnetwork's, made by an operator with a value of at most $10, a cap on redemptions and a last day, a code with a cap above one asking for an unreversed paid lot; only a person who may buy redeems one, on the compute screen or with `ur compute redeem`, never an agent, MCP, a tagged sidecar or an enclave; a network redeems a code once and one code in 30 days; its value counts as a load with the day's purchases against the daily load limit and the balance cap; and its lot, drawn first, pays for inference and enclaves, never web search, and lapses 30 days after redemption. *Why:* CO-35's 30-day promotions; networks are free, so only a code's cap and its paid-lot rule bound what a campaign gives; a search may pay a member's own address (CO-29), which would turn free credit into USDC, and Q-SRCH-5 gives no free searches; and counting codes with purchases keeps a day's loads under the closed-loop exclusion's daily value (§10.8).

### 9.16 Questions

**Q-BAL-1.** What does "auto renew" mean? *Options:* (a) a threshold top-up; (b) a monthly grant; (c) both. *Answer:* (c), with threshold on the web only, since the App Store and Google Play sell no off-session consumable, and the monthly grant on every market as a subscription. *Decider:* owner, confirmed (CO-35).

**Q-BAL-2.** What markup does compute carry over the provider's gamma price? *Options:* (a) none, at cost; (b) 1.20; (c) per model. *Answer:* (b) 1.20 on every model and shape. It covers Stripe's ~3%, the TAO purchase and mint (§10.6, about 1-3%), broker bandwidth, refunds and fraud, and leaves a margin; one number keeps the catalog explainable. The owner sets the number; 1.20 stands until then. *Decider:* owner, confirmed (CO-35).

**Q-BAL-3.** Do store purchases give fewer credits per dollar, or cost more? *Options:* (a) same credits, higher price; (b) same price, fewer credits. *Answer:* (a): a credit is always one dollar of compute, so the balance means one thing everywhere; the store product costs more, at the price tier that nets the web price after the commission URnetwork pays there: 15% in the stores' small-business programs and for a subscription past its first year, else 30%, and where a store's rules allow a link to web checkout (the US App Store since the 2025 ruling), the app offers it. *Decider:* owner, confirmed (CO-35).

**Q-BAL-4.** Do credits expire? *Options:* (a) never; (b) after 12 or 24 months. *Answer:* (a) for purchased and subscription credits; promotions expire in 30 days. Expiry rules for prepaid value vary by state and invite disputes, and a dollar balance that never expires is the simplest promise. *Decider:* owner, confirmed (CO-35).

**Q-BAL-5.** Who may buy credits in a Team network? *Options:* (a) Owner and Billing admin only; (b) any member. *Answer:* (a), with `compute:buy` in the policy (§16.2) to let members buy for the network. *Decider:* owner, confirmed (CO-42).

**Q-BAL-6.** May the crypto rails (Gamma on SN25, TAO, the coins, x402) fund the compute balance? *Options:* (a) no; (b) yes. *Answer:* (a) at launch, as CO-10 says fiat; x402, which lets an agent pay for itself, is the first candidate later because it keeps the rail where agents already are. *Decider:* owner, confirmed (CO-42).

**Q-BAL-7.** What happens to a running enclave when the balance runs out? *Options:* (a) stop at once; (b) grace to a floor, then stop; (c) keep running and bill later. *Answer:* (b), 9.9's floor and one hour, then stop; its work is in EVS, and it starts again as a new incarnation once the balance allows. *Decider:* owner.

**Q-BAL-8.** Which days are the spend view's "last 7 days", and in which time zone? *Options:* (a) 7 UTC days, today so far included; (b) days in a time zone the network sets; (c) the last 168 hours, rolling. *Answer:* (a). `compute_charge_day`, the statements and DESIGN's daily quotas (DESIGN §20.4) all count UTC days, so the view and a statement agree; a network's zone would be one more fact on the server that hints where its people are, and a Team's members span zones; (c) would read the per-request rows on every view. The view says "UTC", and the apps show the window's bounds in the person's local time beside it. *Decider:* owner.

**Q-BAL-9.** Are the spend view's figures exact or estimates? *Options:* (a) exact: settled charges, as of the last settlement; (b) estimates that add open holds and a running enclave's current interval; (c) exact as of a daily rollup. *Answer:* (a). `compute_settle` adds each charge to its day and lifetime rows in the transaction that writes it, so every figure is the sum of its charges to the nano-USD, seconds behind; a hold is a worst case (9.7), not a cost, so (b) would overstate, and the view shows holds apart; (c) would hide today's spend, the spend a person most often asks about. *Decider:* peer review.

**Q-BAL-10.** Where are lifetime totals kept, for how long, and at what grain? *Options:* (a) on the server for the account's life, by kind, member, model or shape, provider and enclave, with no day, sidecar or agent; (b) 400 days, as the day rows, so the "total" is the last 400 days; (c) the account's life at the day rows' grain; (d) on devices, in EVS, folded from the day rows. *Answer:* (a), deleted with the network. CO-22 asks for a total, which (b) cannot give past 400 days; (c) would keep for the account's life when each sidecar used which model, which 9.4 bounds at 400 days on purpose; (d) would have each viewer's devices keep their own fold without a gap, a member's unable to read an admin's, for figures the server derives from charges it holds anyway; (a) keeps only how much each member spent on each model or shape, and one date, the network's first charge, which is all the view shows. It keeps no agent: an agent's id names one device's agent (DESIGN §5.5), so a lifetime row by agent would be a device's lifetime spend, and agent ids churn with every sub-agent and enclave incarnation, so such rows would grow without end; by agent, the view covers the last 7 days and statements their months. *Decider:* owner.

**Q-BAL-11.** May the person's own bot read the spend view? *Options:* (a) no, as agents see no charges today; (b) yes, through `compute_spend` on the person's consented device, within the person's role; (c) yes, for every agent of the network. *Answer:* (b). "Where did my credits go?" is a question for the bot tab (CO-19); the view holds figures and the device's labels, never content (R-BAL-6), less than the mail and vault the same agent may already read, and the sidecar calls the route, so no credential enters the agent's context (I-7). (c) would give agents on tagged sidecars, which act for no one person, and in enclaves, which run on machines others hold (§2.6), a view no role of theirs grants; an untagged CI runner or server, enrolled by an auth key that acts as its creator (DESIGN §7.8), is such a machine too, so (b) asks for the person's consented device, untagged and neither ephemeral nor Delegation-admitted, not merely an untagged one. Charge rows, lots and payment methods stay out of every agent's reach. *Decider:* owner.

**Q-BAL-12.** Where does a refunded charge show in the spend view? *Options:* (a) under Adjustments, as the negative `adjustment` that refunds it, naming the refunded charge and its member, agent and model; (b) netted into the service it refunds; (c) nowhere, the refund a credit lot outside spend. *Answer:* (b), each service's line saying "after $x refunded" where it has refunds. A refund is a negative charge of the kind it returns, carrying that charge's member, agent, model, provider and enclave (9.6), so each service's figure is what its credits bought, every figure is still a plain sum of its kinds' rows, as statements and reconciliation (§10.7) count them, and Adjustments keeps support credits and debits, which name no charge. (a) would show a charge an upheld dispute refunds as remote inference spent, its refund on another line and perhaps another day; (c) would leave a refunded charge counted as spent. *Decider:* peer review.

**Q-BAL-13.** Are credits sold before anything can spend them, as at an M12 exit where no inference provider has passed its gate (Chutes without gamma, CO-32; engy or SayGM without the features their gates name)? *Options:* (a) yes, from M12, whatever the catalog holds; (b) no: the stores' products, `ur compute buy` and the apps' purchase sheets open once a service the network may use can spend credit, a remote model, web search or an enclave shape, and the bot tab offers credit only beside a remote model the person may pick, otherwise local models alone. *Answer:* (b). Credit that nothing can spend brings refunds and support work, and an app store expects what an app sells to be usable in it; local inference is free (CO-9), so the bot tab is useful before any credit. The ledger and the store products still ship and pass review in M12, closed, and open the day a gate passes. *Decider:* owner, confirmed (CO-41).

**Q-BAL-14.** While no provider without a TEE enforces a bound the broker signs, what does a direct call hold? *Options:* (a) its provider's costliest model's worst case, about $2.60 to $3 at launch whatever the call costs, so a $5 balance runs one Codex call at a time and strands up to half of itself; (b) the declared model's worst case, URnetwork carrying the gap to the provider's costliest model up to $5 a network, with $10 the smallest pack offered beside a remote model. *Answer:* (b). Under CO-32 the direct path is the only remote path at launch, and (a) would refuse a session's second call for balance while it had cost cents; (b) risks at most $5 a network, and only from a device that lies about its model, which is charged in full, flagged and, at a second mismatch in 30 days, loses its direct calls (9.11); the packs start at 10 credits (9.5). *Decider:* owner, confirmed (CO-42).

**Q-BAL-15.** Do purchases have a daily limit after a network's first week, and do limits follow the payer as well as the network? *Options:* (a) no: after day 7 only the $10,000 cap bounds a day, and limits are per network; (b) yes: $1,500 a UTC day per network and per payer, a new payer limited as a new network is. *Answer:* (b). §10.8's closed-loop argument cites a daily limit under $2,000, which only (b) designs; networks are free, so limits per network alone reset with each one a fraudster makes, while a card's fingerprint or an App Store account follows the money. *Decider:* owner, confirmed (CO-42).

### 9.17 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| A provider reports more usage than it served | low | overcharge | the device's check (9.7), disputes counted by network (§6.7) and the canary's known counts; §10.7's reconciliation; a provider found overcounting on review is dropped from the catalog |
| Stolen cards buy GPU hours for mining | high | chargebacks, provider complaints | 9.11's limits per network and per payer, Radar, 3-D Secure, the enclave gates |
| Redis loss over-admits | low | holds lost for seconds | bounded by open holds; settlement reads Postgres |
| A provider changes a price without notice | medium | URnetwork pays more than it charges until the catalog's next read | hourly provider price reads; a cost above the price raises an alarm and pulls the model at a 0% margin |
| Unspent credit as a liability | certain | a balance sheet item; in some states, unclaimed property after a dormancy period | the $10,000 cap; deferred revenue until spent, as prepaid service is booked; counsel's reading of unclaimed-property rules (§10.8) |
| A spend rollup drifts from the charges (a bug, a hand edit) | low | the spend view disagrees with statements | written in the charges' own transaction; `compute_rollup_day` re-derives each closed day, checks the totals against the day rows and the pruned sums, and alarms on either difference; reconciliation (§10.7) sums the charges, not the rollups |

### 9.18 Phasing

M12 builds the ledger, Stripe purchases, promotion codes (9.11), self-serve refunds (9.12), both auto-renew modes on Stripe (threshold and the monthly plan), inference charges, and the store products and their subscriptions, which the apps' bot tab needs to sell credit (CO-19); M14 adds the enclave kinds. The spend view (9.13) ships with the ledger, each service joining it with its charges: web search in M13, enclaves in M14. §19 gives the milestones.

## 10. Paying providers in Gamma

### 10.1 Purpose and scope

CO-10: "people pay us fiat for compute balance, and we pay the providers in gamma." This section designs the second half: the treasury that turns fiat into TAO and TAO into gamma, how gamma reaches a provider, the keys and caps that bound a mistake, reconciliation, accounting and the rules that keep the compute balance a closed loop. The first half, users' fiat, is §9.

### 10.2 What Gamma is, at runtime 493

From URnetwork's own chain reader (server/controller/gamma_chain.go, which follows runtime 493 since server commit 5ca596d12), mmm/BTCPAY.md §18, and [Rpt:bt] (gamma_payments_treasury.md, chain reads at block 9,567,893 on 2026-11-23):

| Fact | Detail |
|---|---|
| What | a Subtensor runtime feature (PR #3300, first in runtime 488, mmm/BTCPAY.md §18.1): a per-subnet, US-dollar-valued, non-transferable, non-redeemable service credit, 10^9 units a gamma |
| Mint | `mint_gamma` (call 166) by a coldkey: buys the subnet's alpha with TAO and burns it in one call, crediting a deposit keyed by a hotkey; `mint_gamma_with_stake` (167) burns staked alpha; gamma = alpha × min(gamma price, spot) × TAO/USD; needs the root-fed TAO/USD price no older than 300 blocks; at least 0.1 gamma |
| Spend (since 2026-11-20) | `spend_gamma(service, netuid, amount)` (call 168), signed by the deposit's own hotkey, fee-free; the amount is burned and added to `GammaSpent(netuid, service, hotkey)`; the provider reads that total at finalized blocks and credits the hotkey's account in dollars. The spender account, the `GammaSpend` proxy and the 32-byte references of runtimes 488-492 are gone |
| Caps | per deposit, set by the coldkey; refill linearly over 7,200 blocks (about a day); 0 pauses the deposit |
| Value | a spend pays the provider nothing on chain: the burned alpha's value accrues to the subnet's alpha holders, and the provider bills against its own off-chain balance |
| Who takes it (2026-11-23) | subnets 25, 28, 37, 51, 53, 58, 75, 76, 80, 81, 94, 103 and 117; **not 64 (Chutes) nor 4 (Targon)** |
| The price feed | one root-appointed feed; after a ~17-hour outage on 2026-11-10/11, a median age of 11 blocks in 160 samples; the accepted price falls at once and rises at most ~2% an hour |
| Runtime 494 (2026-11-23) | no change to gamma; signed extrinsics move to transaction version 2, so the treasury's minting and spending tools regenerate their metadata ([Rpt:bt] saygm_tee_verification.md, saygm_gamma_terms.md) |

For URnetwork, gamma is a way to prepay a provider, not a token anyone holds: URnetwork mints it from its own TAO into deposits under hotkeys it controls, and spends it at the provider's service, which credits URnetwork's account there.

### 10.3 Requirements

| Id | Requirement | Source |
|---|---|---|
| R-GAMMA-1 | Every Bittensor provider in the catalog is paid in its subnet's gamma; Parallel, which is not one, per search in USDC (§21.8) | CO-10, CO-16, CO-28 |
| R-GAMMA-2 | Users pay fiat; the design gives no user gamma, TAO, alpha or USDC to hold, see or move, and a device carries at most a one-search authorization URnetwork signed, of at most the policy's ceiling, to the payee it named, which a member's modified client may make its own (§21.5) | CO-10; CO-29; FinCEN closed loop (10.8) |
| R-GAMMA-3 | A leaked key, a wrong spend or a dissolved subnet costs at most a bounded, small amount | derived |
| R-GAMMA-4 | What URnetwork pays each provider reconciles daily with what it charged users | derived |

### 10.4 The flow

```text
users ──fiat──▶ Stripe / App Store / Play ──▶ URnetwork's bank account          (§9.5)
treasury  weekly, or when the TAO float is under 3 days of forecast spend:
          buy TAO for USD on Coinbase Prime or Kraken; withdraw to the compute treasury coldkey
per provider P on subnet N, with service hotkey S_P (from its published service document):
  deposit   D_P = (N, K_P): K_P an API-key hotkey URnetwork made for P (one per environment); the coldkey owns D_P
  mint      compute_gamma_mint, a taskworker job: when D_P holds under 1 day of P's forecast cost, mint_gamma(N,
            K_P, tao, min_gamma) from the mint coldkey's float, raising D_P to 2 days; refused when the feed is
            stale or price impact would pass 1%
  spend     compute_gamma_spend: when P's account balance is under 1.5 days, spend_gamma(S_P, N, amount) signed by
            K_P, with amount the lesser of (3 days - the account balance) and D_P; P credits it within minutes
            (Lium: "usually within a few minutes")
  use       the broker calls P's API under URnetwork's account (Chutes: its API key; gamma-native providers: btauth/1
            requests signed by K_P, the orchestrator's own and, for inference without a TEE, those devices send on
            the direct path, §6.6), and P bills that account per request or per second
```

Two buffers, for two failures: the deposit holds 1 to 2 days of gamma not yet spent, so a stale price feed, which blocks mints but not spends, stops nothing for at least a day; the provider account holds 1.5 to 3 days, so a slow chain stops nothing either. Both are small on purpose (10.9).

**Forecast.** A provider P's forecast daily cost is the largest of: P's trailing 7-day mean daily cost; the daily cost of the enclaves running at P (their hourly rates × 24) plus P's trailing mean of inference; and P's floor in `compute_gamma.yml`, set at its gate to at least a day of its largest shape for one enclave, or of a busy network's inference, so a new provider, and a GPU enclave bigger than P's history, start covered. Mints, spends, deposit caps and the treasury's weekly buy all size from it. The broker refuses a new call or a new enclave whose hold P's account, as last read less the cost of what P served and the holds open there since, cannot cover: `capacity`, with a retry time, and the spend job runs at once. A running enclave's interval is never refused for this; a shortfall then pages.

### 10.5 Keys and caps

| Key | Holds | Where | Can do | Bounded by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Treasury reserve coldkey | the TAO reserve | a multisig on the owners' Ledgers, as SN25's `ur-owner` is (mmm/BTCPAY.md §18.6) | anything with the reserve | 2 of 3 signers; used weekly at most |
| Compute mint coldkey | a TAO float of at most 7 days of spend; owns every D_P | vault, delivered only to the taskworker hosts that run `compute_gamma_mint` | mint into D_P, set caps, move or pause deposits | the float; mints only to the (N, K_P, S_P) triples `compute_gamma.yml` lists |
| API-key hotkey K_P | its deposit D_P, and, at a gamma-native provider, URnetwork's whole account there, since the provider's balance belongs to the hotkey that spent and every request is a btauth/1 signature by it | a signer service on the `computeservice` hosts, which signs only `spend_gamma` extrinsics the spend job asks for and btauth/1 requests the broker makes, at a capped rate; never on a device | spend D_P at any service on subnet N up to its daily cap; spend URnetwork's provider balance; create, stop or delete any VM URnetwork holds at P | D_P (2 days at most) and its cap (twice the forecast daily cost); the provider balance (3 days at most); the signer's rate |

So a leaked K_P is a full provider credential at a gamma-native provider: it can spend up to two days of deposit and three of provider balance, and act on every enclave VM URnetwork runs there. Three checks catch it: `compute_gamma_watch` keeps the hash of every extrinsic the spend job submits and treats any other extrinsic from K_P as a leak, setting D_P's cap to 0 within a block (runtime 493 has no spend references to match, so the extrinsic hash is the key); the orchestrator reconciles the provider's VM list against `compute_enclave` on every poll and pages on a VM it did not create or a change it did not make; and the provider balance is read hourly against the charges. The mint key then moves what is left to a new hotkey, and the provider is asked to bind the account to it. A leaked mint key spends at most the float. For Chutes, which takes no gamma, the credential is its API key, held the same way.

### 10.6 Cost

| Cost | Size (2026-11-23) | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Exchange | ~0.1-0.6% plus spread | Coinbase Prime or Kraken |
| Mint price impact | for a $10,000 mint: ~0.03% on SN51 (Lium); ~0.12% on SN53 (engy); ~0.14% on SN75 (Hippius); ~0.18% on SN28 (SayGM); ~2.2% on SN94 (Cathedral); ~0.03% on SN64 should Chutes take gamma ([Rpt:bt] gamma_payments_treasury.md, pools on 2026-11-23) | a mint into a thin pool is split or refused (10.4's 1%) |
| Feed asymmetry | the accepted TAO/USD price lags a rise by up to ~2% an hour and follows a fall at once | the minter waits up to 6 hours after a rise over 2% before a non-urgent mint |
| Transaction fees | mints pay an ordinary fee; spends are free | negligible |
| Provider premium | engy credits $1.05 a gamma; Lium, Cathedral and Hippius $1.00 | the adapter records each provider's rate |

**Margins.** At full spend a pack's margin is its price less the market's fees, less the provider cost of its credits, which is their face value over the 1.20 markup (§9.6); the costs above and TAO's movement come out of what is left. US cards and storefronts, before tax; Stripe at 2.9% plus $0.30 and Stripe Tax's 0.5%; a store at the commission URnetwork pays there (Q-BAL-3):

| Pack | Market | Price | Fees | Net | Provider cost | Margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 credits | Stripe | $10.00 | $0.64 | $9.36 | $8.33 | $1.03 (10.3%) |
| 25 credits | Stripe | $25.00 | $1.15 | $23.85 | $20.83 | $3.02 (12.1%) |
| 100 credits | Stripe | $100.00 | $3.70 | $96.30 | $83.33 | $12.97 (13.0%) |
| 10 credits | a store at 15% | $11.99 | $1.80 | $10.19 | $8.33 | $1.86 (15.5%) |
| 10 credits | a store at 30% | $14.99 | $4.50 | $10.49 | $8.33 | $2.16 (14.4%) |
| 5 credits, not sold | Stripe | $5.00 | $0.47 | $4.53 | $4.17 | $0.36 (7.3%) |
| 5 credits, not sold | a store at 30%, priced for 15% | $5.99 | $1.80 | $4.19 | $4.17 | $0.03 (0.4%) |

Cards from abroad add Stripe's 1.5% and its conversion fee; engy's $1.05 a gamma lowers its cost by about 5%. The last two rows are why the packs start at 10 credits and a store's price follows the commission it actually charges (§9.5). TAO's movement is the larger swing: the treasury buys weekly (CO-35), and TAO bought for a week and a 7-day float is minted about ten days later on average; the accepted TAO/USD price read about $218.76 on 2026-11-10/11 and $191.77 on 2026-11-23 ([Rpt:bt] gamma_payments_treasury.md), a 12.3% fall in under two weeks, which on that week's spend would turn the 1.20 markup into about 1.05. `compute_reconcile` reports each provider's realized margin weekly and pages under 5% (10.7); Q-GAMMA-4 asks the owner to move the conversion just in time.

### 10.7 Reconciliation

A daily job, `compute_reconcile`, compares three ledgers per provider:

| Ledger | Source | What it says |
|---|---|---|
| What URnetwork charged users at cost | `compute_charge.cost_nano_usd` (§9.4) | what the broker metered at the provider's prices |
| What the provider billed URnetwork | the provider's usage API (Chutes: `/invocations/exports`, `/users/me` usage; Lium, Hippius: their billing APIs) | what the provider says it served |
| What URnetwork paid | `GammaSpent(N, S_P, K_P)` and the mints, read from finalized blocks by the chain reader the server already runs | what left the treasury |

A gap over 1% between the first two opens a review; held disputes (§6.7) and the canary's gaps settle there. Weekly the job also reports each provider's realized margin, its charges less the USD cost of the gamma it spent, at the price of the TAO that minted it, over its charges, and pages when a provider's week falls under 5% (10.6). A gap between the provider's credited balance and the gamma spent is raised with the provider. The `compute_provider_ledger` table (§14.4) keeps the provider's balance as last read, each spend and each credit.

### 10.8 Accounting, tax and regulation

Background for the owner and counsel, not advice ([Rpt:bt]):

- **The compute balance** is a customer prepayment, a contract liability recognized as revenue as charges are made; with no expiry (Q-BAL-4) there is no breakage.
- **TAO** is held at fair value (ASU 2023-08); each mint disposes of TAO, a taxable event at the difference between the services' value and the TAO's basis. How gamma itself is carried, non-transferable and non-redeemable, needs an accountant's reading; the design treats provider prepayments as prepaid expenses consumed as the provider bills.
- **Closed loop.** FinCEN's prepaid-access rule excludes closed-loop prepaid access sold up to $2,000 per device per day, and the money-transmitter rules exclude funds integral to selling one's own goods or services. The balance buys only URnetwork's compute, moves between no users, and pays out only a refund to the original payment method (§9.12), but for one exception the owner accepts (CO-29): a web search's authorization pays whatever address the device names from Parallel's challenge, since the gateway's payee changes per request (§21.5), so a member's modified client can direct each authorization, at most the policy's ceiling, to an address of its own, within the network's budgets, daily cap and rate. Two risks follow: the exclusion may not survive a balance a user can turn into USDC at an address of their choosing; and a stolen card can buy balance that searches cash out. The mitigations are the ceiling per authorization; the payee screen (below); the network's budgets, daily search cap and per-network rate (§21.9), and the broker's search cap, which no policy raises (§9.11); §9.11's purchase limits per network and per payer, $1,500 a day each, under the exclusion's $2,000, and $100 a day and $200 in a first week for a new network or payer; and §17's monitoring of search volume by network, never content. A chargeback takes back both the percentage CO-29 counts on and the USDC already paid, so for a Stripe card or an App Store account the payer limits bound what one stolen source can cash out: about $167 of USDC in its first week, whatever networks it funds. Counsel reads this bullet under CO-29 before search launches (G-SRCH-parallel, Q-SRCH-13), and, before the store products are submitted (§19.2), whether the exclusion's "maximum value that can be associated with a prepaid access device or vehicle on any day" (31 CFR 1010.100(ff)(4)(iii)(A)) means a day's loads, which the daily limit keeps under $2,000, or the balance held, which §9.5's $10,000 cap would pass. Users never hold gamma (R-GAMMA-2).
- **Sanctions.** Buyers: Stripe's screening at checkout, and compute refused for sanctioned regions by the address the broker sees, which is never logged (I-13) but may be checked. Payees: CO-29 accepts a member's own search payee, not URnetwork's payer paying a sanctioned address, which EIP-3009 would let a modified client do by submitting an authorization to Base itself, past the facilitator's screening; so the search signer screens each payee against the sanctions lists before it signs, and, once G-SRCH-parallel shows the gateway's payees fresh, refuses any address with a past; it signs windows of at most 3 minutes; and an authorization settled by any sender but the facilitator is kept with its network as a sanctions record and flagged (§21.5). Counsel reads the payee side with the closed loop (G-SRCH-parallel): the lists the screen takes, whether a refusal or an out-of-band payment must be reported to OFAC, and how long the records are kept.
- **Unclaimed property.** Credits that never expire (CO-35, Q-BAL-4) leave no breakage, but a balance left untouched may become unclaimed property that some states require be reported and remitted after a dormancy period; counsel reads which states' rules reach a compute balance and what notices they ask, before the store products are submitted (§19.2), and the accountant books what counsel finds.
- **Providers never learn users.** A provider sees URnetwork's account and, at gamma-native providers, URnetwork's hotkeys; no user's identity, wallet or address.

### 10.9 Failure modes

| Failure | Effect | Response |
|---|---|---|
| The price feed is stale | mints fail; spends continue | the deposit's day of gamma; an alarm after 2 hours |
| A provider's subnet is dissolved or pruned | its deposits' gamma is destroyed | at most 2 days' deposit and the provider account's 3 days are lost; the provider leaves the catalog |
| A provider does not credit a spend | URnetwork paid, the provider will not serve | spends pause for that provider; raised under the E6 agreement; the provider leaves the catalog if unresolved in 48 h |
| A runtime upgrade changes a call | mints or spends fail | the chain reader's shape check, as `gamma_chain.go` already does, pauses and alarms rather than guess |
| TAO falls between purchase and mint | fewer gamma per dollar | a float of at most 7 days; the weekly realized-margin page (10.7); Q-GAMMA-4 |

### 10.10 Providers that do not take gamma

Parallel (§21) is not a Bittensor provider and takes no gamma; CO-28 names it, so URnetwork pays it per search in USDC on Base from its payer address, to the payee each challenge names, and `compute_reconcile` matches the month's settlements of the broker's authorizations to the kind-6 charges (§21.8, Q-SRCH-2). CO-10 governs Bittensor providers. A provider whose subnet has not enabled gamma cannot be paid under CO-10, so it is not in the catalog: Chutes, today. The owner decided that case (CO-32, Q-PROV-1): such a provider is dropped from launch, with no payment in card, TAO or alpha in its place, and joins when its subnet takes gamma. The adapter's `Payment()` is configuration, `gamma` for every Bittensor provider, so admitting Chutes when SN64 enables gamma is a configuration change, a new signed policy (§5.4) and the broker's catalog, not a release (§4.7).

### 10.11 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Users mint gamma themselves | no treasury | users would hold crypto (against CO-10's fiat); a coldkey per user, public on chain | rejected |
| One large deposit per provider | fewer mints | a leaked hotkey or a dissolved subnet costs more | rejected: 1 to 2 days' deposit (D-GAMMA-2) |
| Fund the treasury from SN25's owner alpha | uses what URnetwork already earns | a treasury decision with market effects outside this design | allowed as a source of TAO; not designed here |
