CO-19 asks for it always on, and under (a) it stops an hour after the balance reaches zero, which a store buyer with no threshold top-up reaches unawares, and most restarts page a person, since no provider pins machines; the reserve costs a network a week of its price up front, the grace at most 72 hours more owed, and the weekly limit keeps a breached broker from drawing machines at will. *Decider:* owner, confirmed (CO-42).

**Q-ENC-12.** Should an agent's `enclave_stop` and `enclave_start` need the person in a tainted run, with the network's indexer enclave outside agent tools? *Options:* (a) no: both W in any run; (b) yes: a start through a tool is a kind 19, a tainted run's stop waits for the person's confirmation, and no tool stops, starts or removes the indexer enclave. *Answer:* (b). A stop destroys the VM and its scratch disk, so under (a) a prompt-injected run, local or through MCP, could stop every enclave the person sponsors, the network's mail with them, and a start would resume per-second charges no budget stops and admit an incarnation by a tool, which 11.4 forbids; a tainted run's `agent_stop` already waits for the person (§7.10). *Decider:* owner.

**Q-ENC-13.** Does CO-43's full access extend to the network's indexer enclave? *Options:* (a) no: it stays a tagged sidecar its Owners and Admins sponsor, receiving the network's mail and reading only the mailboxes members grant it; (b) yes, as a device of the Owner or Admin who set it up, with that member's access. *Answer:* (a). The indexer serves the whole network: it holds every member's incoming mail and the mailboxes members grant it, and its sponsors are the network's Owners and Admins, any of whom may admit its incarnations (11.4), so its access is not one member's; under (b) every member's mail would sit beside one admin's vault, mail and accounts on one machine, a breach exposing them together, and members' grants (CO-20) already give it what it needs. It keeps its measured role, with no Harness, no agents and no login (11.10). *Decider:* owner.

**Q-ENC-14.** How is an agents' enclave given its sponsor's access (CO-43)? *Options:* (a) admitted as an untagged device of the sponsor; (b) a tagged admission that also names its sponsor, capability bit 3: consented for the sponsor, holding none of their authority; (c) an `EvsShare` or grant of each repo, link and connection to its tag, as before CO-43. *Answer:* (b), for the initial version. It rests on DESIGN's own consent (§8.5's `scoped` clause) and key delivery, so the enclave reads what the sponsor's devices read with no share to keep current, and it keeps `tag:enclave-<id>`, on which its claim, its network reach, its egress default and its listeners rest (§11.8, §16.5, §26); (a) would drop the tag and give a machine a miner holds the sponsor's authority to admit devices, consent and share, which would outlast the incarnation's revocation; (c) is what CO-43 replaced: a share per item, which reaches no new repo by itself. The bit also keeps the enclave from the sponsor's authority and from writing their settings (11.4). *Decider:* peer review.

### 11.17 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| No provider adopts EPC-1 | medium | no user-facing enclaves | the reference provider keeps the stack ready; the three CO-28 chose asked in parallel, Hippius and Cathedral for the launch-data binding first; meanwhile no user gets an enclave and mail indexers stay members' always-on devices (11.3) |
| A miner's physical attack on an enclave | low | that enclave's keys and data: for an agents' enclave, everything its sponsor's devices hold (CO-43) | §2.6; removal and new keys; no authority in it, so nothing it signs outlasts its revocation; the indexer holds only its grants |
| A breached broker aims a new incarnation, the indexer above all, at a rigged machine | low | that incarnation's keys and what it holds, for the indexer the network's incoming mail | one VM per authorization, the device starting each retry; the indexer only where the broker does not choose the machine; its keeper's new machines capped (11.6, 11.10) |
| A kernel escape from the agents' container, whose root holds `CAP_NET_ADMIN` in its user namespace | medium | the incarnation's keys, its rules and all it holds, in an agents' enclave everything its sponsor's devices hold | 11.10's hardening; EPC-9's kernel cadence; incarnations replaced at their profile's expiry (11.11); gVisor evaluated (11.14) |
| An injected agent in an enclave that reaches out sends the sponsor's mail, accounts or record out with `bash` | medium | that data, past every gate | the `private` mark: a run that reads them uses no container tool, and the crossing is the person's kind 24 (§7.8) |
| Each stop of an agents' enclave removes one of its sponsor's devices | high | every repo the sponsor reads, Team repos included, takes a REMOVE rotation and a path epoch within 24 hours (DESIGN §10.5), its other readers fetching the new generation | the rotation is the next writer's and the path epoch due within a day, so several stops in a day cost each repo one; enclaves run for days, a planned restart at most at their profile's expiry (11.11); §18 measures the load; a narrower enclave, Later, shrinks the set (§19.5) |
| The indexer enclave stops: the balance runs out, a loss, an outage | medium | members' mail waits on senders' retries | its reserve and grace; unattended restarts on allowed machines; make before break when planned; silence alone fails nothing (11.10, 11.11) |
| Agents in enclaves misused for abuse | medium | provider complaints, URnetwork's network reputation | §17 |

## 12. The bundled SSH

### 12.1 Purpose and scope

CO-5: "Sidecar should have a built in minimal version of ssh that allows remotely accessing the secure enclaves." This section designs it: a server in every enclave, a client in every sidecar, authentication by sidecar identity, authorization by policy, host keys known in advance, recording, the agent's `ssh_exec`, and OpenSSH interoperability. It also carries the Harness's attach link (§7.10).

### 12.2 Requirements

| Id | Requirement | Source |
|---|---|---|
| R-SSH-1 | A client in `ur`, the sdk and the Harness; a server in every enclave | CO-5, CO-6 |
| R-SSH-2 | No `~/.ssh` key management: identity is the sidecar's | derived |
| R-SSH-3 | No trust on first use: the client knows the enclave's host key before it connects | R-ENC-6 |
| R-SSH-4 | Who may log in, and as which user, is policy (DESIGN §8) | derived |
| R-SSH-5 | Standard SSH, so OpenSSH, VS Code and sftp work | derived |
| R-SSH-6 | Listens only on the overlay | I-10, I-17 |

### 12.3 What exists

| Fact | Citation |
|---|---|
| The local tier's git front already serves SSH with `golang.org/x/crypto/ssh`: one Ed25519 host key per network kept sealed, public-key auth mapped to a sidecar through the host's lookup of §7.9's `KeyRegister`, and only `git-upload-pack` or `git-receive-pack` exec'd; "no shell, no pty, no forwarding, no subsystem" | sidecar/evs_local_ssh.go:1-17, :38-60 |
| The config's projection already carries registered SSH public keys with member and purpose | DESIGN §2.8 api-7 |
| `golang.org/x/crypto` is v0.58.0 in the module | sidecar/go.mod:25 |
| x/crypto/ssh v0.59.0 (2026-11-11) puts `mlkem768x25519-sha256` first; 22 CVEs since 2023, 13 announced 2026-05-22 and fixed in v0.52.0, CVE-2026-56854 (the no-client-auth path) fixed in v0.55.0 | [Rpt:bb] ssh_git_minimal.md |
| gliderlabs/ssh has had no commit since 2025-01; Charm and Tailscale keep forks; Tailscale SSH identifies the caller from the overlay peer and accepts "none" auth; Coder turns SSH auth off | [Rpt:bb] |

### 12.4 The server

`ssh_server.go`, built only for the enclave leg (Linux):

| Feature | Served |
|---|---|
| Listener | the enclave's overlay address, TCP 22, never the host interface (11.8's firewall also drops it) |
| Key exchange | x/crypto/ssh defaults, `mlkem768x25519-sha256` first; the module moves to x/crypto v0.59.0 or later |
| Host key | the incarnation's SSH host key (Ed25519), made in its VM, bound in its evidence and registered (§11.7, 12.6) |
| Session | `exec`, `shell` with a pty (`creack/pty`), `env` for `LANG`, `LC_*` and `TERM` only, `window-change`, `signal`; `origin@ur.io` before an `exec`, the caller's signed origin (12.5, §7.10); `effect@ur.io`, a use's effect key, which the server records before it starts the command and answers to the client's Lookup (§16.3); an `agent` session's `exec` and `shell` run in the agents' container, but an `exec` of `ur harness rpc`, which the server joins to the Harness outside it (§11.10), and an `edit` session's in the edit container (12.9) |
| Subsystem | `sftp` (`github.com/pkg/sftp` server), so scp, sftp and editors copy files; it runs in the session's own namespaces and as its user: the agents' container's for `agent`, the edit container's for `edit`, the enclave's own for `root` |
| Forwarding | for a person's session only, local forwarding (`direct-tcpip`, and `direct-streamlocal@openssh.com`) to the session's own loopback, which VS Code Remote-SSH and port previews need, the server entering the session's network and mount namespaces before it connects: the agents' container's for `agent`, the edit container's for `edit`, the enclave's own for `root`; never for an agent's session; remote forwarding, agent forwarding and X11 refused everywhere |
| Global requests | `evidence@ur.io` with a nonce, which the server answers itself, outside the agents' container, with fresh evidence binding this session (12.6) |
| Users | `agent`, `root` and `edit` (12.9); a session runs as the user the rule allowed (12.5) |
| Limits | 16 sessions a client, 64 an enclave; idle sessions closed after 12 hours |

### 12.5 Who may log in

Authentication is public key only, and the key must be a sidecar's:

```text
client key   each sidecar has an Ed25519 SSH key in its keychain, separate from its identity key, registered once
             with KeyRegister (purpose ssh), signed by its identity key (DESIGN §7.9); the daemon signs with it and
             never exports it
server check 1 the offered key is a live KeyRegister of an admitted sidecar S, not revoked, parked or suspended
             2 the TCP session's overlay source resolves, through the bridge's verified flow principal (DESIGN
               §17.9), to the same S; a key presented over another sidecar's flow is refused
             3 the policy allows ssh from S to this enclave as the requested user (§16.2), another member's
               S only by a requested grant the enclave's sponsor approved (Q-HARN-9), and root, which
               reaches all the daemon holds for the sponsor (CO-43, §11.4), only from an untagged device
               of the sponsor, whatever a rule or grant says; a rule with check
               needs a decision from an approval-capable device or a presence key within its check period
               (default 12 h), asked for at login as an outward-style approval and recorded
             4 the session is accepted and recorded (12.7)
origin       5 before an exec of ur harness rpc, the origin@ur.io request: a §6.9 Signed of purpose
               attach-origin (SIGNED_ATTACH_ORIGIN = 0x1808, §6.11) by S's identity key, its public key from
               the config, over {network, S, the enclave and incarnation, this session's exchange hash, its
               mode: carried, with its one origin, or stamped}; the server verifies it outside the agents'
               container and hands the Harness the verified header; a session without one is an unknown
               run's (§7.10)
```

The server takes keys through `VerifiedPublicKeyCallback`, which runs only after the client has proved it holds the key, and does checks 1 to 3 there, never in `PublicKeyCallback` (CVE-2024-45337: that callback's key may not be the one that authenticates). x/crypto/ssh's advisories cluster in every authentication callback, `VerifiedPublicKeyCallback`'s source-address handling included (CVE-2026-46595), so the module pins v0.59.0 or later and §18 fuzzes the server. Public keys are used, rather than a Tailscale-style "none" login on the overlay's identity alone, because the server must tie a login to a registered key and its flow both, and because OpenSSH, sftp and editors present keys.

### 12.6 Host keys

The client never trusts on first use (R-SSH-3). It resolves the enclave's name to its running incarnation, takes that incarnation's host key from the config's `KeyRegister`, signed by the incarnation's identity key, and checks it against the key the incarnation's evidence bound (§11.7 steps 5 and 9). A host key that does not match is refused, naming the enclave. Because a host key could still be extracted from its machine by a physical attack, an attach also binds the session itself: the client sends an `evidence@ur.io` global request with a nonce, which `ur ssh-server` answers itself, outside the agents' container, with fresh evidence whose report data carries the SSH exchange hash and the nonce, and refuses a session that cannot produce it (§5.5).

### 12.7 Recording

Each session is a reach receipt (DESIGN §16.8): who, which sidecar, which user, when it opened and closed, bytes each way; in a Team, in the team record. Commands are not recorded by the server: an agent's `ssh_exec` is already a tool call in its own run (§7.7), and a person's shell is the person's. Recording a person's whole session, as some regulated teams want, is Later, and would go to that person's vault, never a server.

### 12.8 The client and the agent's tool

- **CLI.** `ur ssh <name>[.<net>] [--user agent|root] [command]` dials the enclave's overlay address through the daemon's bridge (DESIGN §17.5), so it works with or without `ur tun`. A `root` login asks the person on `/dev/tty` or for a presence key first, as `ur ssh agent`'s does (12.9), and is refused to a caller with a harness process among its ancestors; `ur enclave ssh` likewise, and the sdk's `OpenSsh` logs in as `root` only from the app's own UI, which asks the person.
- **Apps.** The sdk's `SidecarSshSession` (open, write, resize, close, an output listener) feeds a terminal component (xterm.js, SwiftTerm, Termux's view); the app process dials through the sidecar's userspace stack.
- **Harness.** `ssh_exec(host, command, stdin?, timeout?, cwd?)` returns `{stdout, stderr, exit_code, truncated}`, each stream capped at 256 KiB, with progress events while it runs; the output taints the run (§7.8). Agents get no interactive shell.
- **Browser.** Later, with the extension's Worker: Go's x/crypto client builds for wasm (about 1.9 MB gzipped), and would ride a sidecar subprotocol stream instead of a socket.

### 12.9 OpenSSH and editors

`ur ssh config` writes a block to `~/.ssh/config` for each enclave the person may reach:

```text
Host build1.<net>
  ProxyCommand /absolute/path/to/ur ssh --stdio %h %p
  KnownHostsCommand /absolute/path/to/ur ssh known-hosts %H
  IdentityAgent ~/.local/state/ur/ssh-agent.sock
  User agent
```

`ur ssh agent` serves the sidecar's SSH key over the ssh-agent protocol on that socket, signing without exporting it. It signs a login as `root` only after the person confirms it on `/dev/tty` or with a presence key, reading the user from the signed `SSH_MSG_USERAUTH_REQUEST`, since any same-user process, an agent's shell included, can use the socket, and an enclave's real root could rewrite its Harness (Q-HARN-6). OpenSSH 8.5 or later reads `KnownHostsCommand`, so VS Code Remote-SSH, scp and git over SSH work with no key or known_hosts file to manage.

**Editors.** An editor's remote server (VS Code Remote-SSH, JetBrains Gateway, Zed's remote mode) trusts the machine it runs on: whoever holds root where it runs can run commands on the person's computer through the editor, as VS Code's publisher warns, and agents hold root in the agents' container, where `User agent` lands. So `ur ssh config` prints that warning and writes a second block, `Host build1-edit.<net>` with `User edit`, as the editors' target: an `edit` session lands in a person-only container with its own namespaces and root file system, where no agent process runs and which none can write, the agents' container's file system mounted at `/agents`, so an editor's server runs where no agent reaches it, and the person opens `/agents` in the editor's restricted mode (VS Code's Workspace Trust), since agents wrote it. `edit` is refused to every agent's session, `ssh_exec` included, and to `ur ssh` with a harness process among its ancestors, as `root` is (12.8); unlike a `root` login it needs no confirmation, since nothing in it reaches the enclave's keys or the agents' processes.

### 12.10 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| A custom exec and shell protocol over sidecar streams (Kubernetes exec's shape) | simplest; one less crypto layer | no OpenSSH, VS Code or sftp | rejected: R-SSH-5 |
| OpenSSH's server in the image | standard | a second identity system and a larger surface; keys in files | rejected |
| SSH certificates with an attestation extension | standard host-key distribution | no prior art; the config already distributes keys | Later |
| Tailscale-style "none" auth on the overlay's identity | no client keys; OpenSSH still connects | ties a login to the flow but not to a registered key; the advisories hit every callback alike | rejected: keys checked in `VerifiedPublicKeyCallback` against KeyRegister and the flow |

### 12.11 Decisions proposed

**D-SSH-1 (proposed).** The SSH protocol, on x/crypto/ssh v0.59.0 or later, with sidecar-registered keys, flow-principal cross-check and policy rules. *Why:* 12.5; R-SSH-5.

**D-SSH-2 (proposed).** Host keys from the config and the attestation; no trust on first use. *Why:* R-SSH-3.

**D-SSH-3 (proposed).** Local forwarding to the enclave's loopback for people only; no remote or agent forwarding; sftp on. *Why:* VS Code Remote-SSH needs it; agents do not; file copy is needed.

**D-SSH-4 (proposed).** The server, outside the agents' container, verifies each attach link's signed origin (`origin@ur.io`, `SIGNED_ATTACH_ORIGIN`), records a use's effect key before it runs a command (`effect@ur.io`) and answers evidence requests as a global request; a session's sftp and forwards run in its own namespaces and as its user. *Why:* I-9; IC-12; agents have root in their container.

**D-SSH-5 (proposed).** A `root` login, by `ur ssh`, `ur enclave ssh`, `ur ssh agent` or the sdk's `OpenSsh`, is signed only after the person's confirmation on `/dev/tty`, in the app's UI or with a presence key, and `ur ssh` and `ur enclave ssh` refuse it to a caller with a harness process among its ancestors. *Why:* any same-user process can use the agent socket or run `ur`, and an enclave's root can rewrite what runs in it.

**D-SSH-6 (proposed).** `ur ssh config` warns that an editor's remote server trusts its machine and writes an `edit` target: a person-only container with the agents' files at `/agents`, which no agent process enters or writes, `edit` refused to agents' sessions and to a harness's `ur ssh`. *Why:* an agent with root where an editor's server runs could run commands on the person's computer.

### 12.12 Questions

**Q-SSH-1.** Should desktops and other sidecars run the SSH server too? *Answer:* not at launch; CO-5 is about enclaves. `ur ssh serve` for a person's own machines is Later, behind the same rule. *Decider:* owner.

**Q-SSH-2.** Should person sessions be recorded? *Answer:* receipts only (12.7); full recordings Later, to the person's vault, by a Team policy. *Decider:* owner.

### 12.13 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| A new x/crypto/ssh CVE | high | a server bug in every enclave | pin the newest release each `ur` release; fuzz the server (§18); overlay-only listener |
| A person's laptop key misused | low | shell on an enclave | the key never leaves the daemon; check rules for root |
| An editor's remote server in the agents' container | medium | an agent runs commands on the person's computer | `ur ssh config`'s warning and the `edit` target (12.9) |

### 12.14 Phasing

M14: the client, tested against OpenSSH servers in CI, beside the server it reaches; the server in enclaves, `ssh_exec` to them, attach and its session binding, OpenSSH config. §19.

## 13. The bundled git

### 13.1 Purpose and scope

CO-8: "a minimal version of git for the harness to use with our EVS." This section designs it: what it supports, how it is built on sidecar's existing git code, how it reads and writes EVS without a system git or a network remote, and how an agent calls it.

### 13.2 Requirements

| Id | Requirement | Source |
|---|---|---|
| R-GIT-1 | Works where no system git exists: phones, the browser later, and the local Harness everywhere, since CO-6 forbids host processes | CO-6, CO-8 |
| R-GIT-2 | Reads and writes EVS git-mode repos, keeping EVS's rules: the committer rule ([owner decision 81](DESIGN.md#od-81)), the tip CAS ([owner decision 141](DESIGN.md#od-141)), SHA-1 only ([owner decision 249](DESIGN.md#od-249)) | DESIGN §11.11 |
| R-GIT-3 | Covers what coding agents use | derived; [Rpt:bb] |
| R-GIT-4 | Small: no cgo, fits the sdk's size budgets | DESIGN §18.10 |

### 13.3 What exists

| Fact | Citation |
|---|---|
| Strict and lenient codecs for git's blobs, trees, commits and tags on every leg, held equal to go-git and stock git in tests; SHA-1 oids | sidecar/evs_git_object.go:1-24 |
| A pack writer (undeltified, version 2), delta and pkt-line code | sidecar/evs_git_pack.go, evs_git_delta.go, evs_git_pktline.go |
| The local tier runs the system git, desktop legs only; a daemon without it answers `EVS_GIT_REF` to a write on a git-mode ref | sidecar/evs_local_git.go:1-12; DESIGN §16.5's `evs_write` |
| Export "rebuilds plain git with no git binary" | sidecar/evs_git_object.go:1-3 |
| go-git: in-memory clones used ~20× the packed size (324 MB for a 14 MB repo), merges are fast-forward only, no rebase or stash, 11 advisories in 2026; v6 beta builds for wasip1 | [Rpt:bb] ssh_git_minimal.md |
| What agents' own prompts use: status, diff (`HEAD`, `--staged`), `log -n`, show, `add <paths>`, `commit -m`, branch and switch, restore and reset, and gated push; they warn against `reset --hard` | [Rpt:bb] |

### 13.4 Design

`git_*.go` in the sidecar root, on every leg but the VPN component: a small porcelain over the existing codecs, never go-git (which stays the tests' oracle) and never a process.

```text
workspace   a worktree in the agent's workspace (§7.5) with git's own on-disk layout: .git/HEAD, refs, loose
            objects, index version 2; stock git can open a full clone on a desktop for debugging, never a sparse
            or lazily fetched one, whose unfetched paths and objects it would read as deleted or missing; packs
            appear only in transfer
remote      exactly one kind: ur://<net>/<repo> (DESIGN §11.11's names); no http, ssh or file remotes, so the local
            Harness reaches nothing but EVS
clone       reads the ref's head through the evs client (DESIGN §11.9), fetches the commit and tree records it needs,
            and fetches blobs only for the paths checked out: --sparse <prefix> limits a checkout to a prefix, and a
            blob outside it is fetched when a command first reads it, as a promisor remote is
fetch/pull  the same, from the last pin; pull is fetch then merge
commit      builds objects with the strict codecs; committer per owner decision 81 (<client_id>@ur.invalid, the
            agent's name as committer name)
push        writes to the git-mode ref through the evs client's push path, the one the local tier's publish feeds,
            under the tip CAS: a stale tip is refused, and the agent fetches and merges, as with any remote
ignore      .gitignore files and .git/info/exclude, by gitignore(5)'s patterns, for status and add -A; no
            global excludes file, since config is not read beyond user.*
renames     status, diff, log --stat and merge find renames as stock git does by default: exact, then at
            least 50% similar, within its default limits (1,000 files in diff, 7,000 in merge)
modes       100644, 100755 and 120000 as git stores them; the executable bit read from the file system on
            desktops that keep one, else kept from the index (phones, the browser, Windows), so a checkout
            never flips a mode; a gitlink (160000) kept, never checked out
collisions  where two paths fold to one name (case on macOS and Windows, Unicode normalization on macOS), a
            checkout writes the first, leaves the other unwritten and marked, and names both, as stock git
            warns; status does not report the unwritten one as deleted
```

### 13.5 Commands

| Command | Supported |
|---|---|
| `init`, `clone` | `clone ur://<net>/<repo> [dir] [--branch b] [--sparse <prefix>]`; `init` only for a repo `evs_repos` lists or a new one the policy lets this agent create |
| `status` | short and long forms, `--porcelain` (v1), `-s`, `-b` |
| `diff` | worktree, `--staged`/`--cached`, `<rev>`, `<rev>..<rev>`, paths; `--stat`, `--name-only`, `--name-status`, `-U<n>`; Myers diff, git's unified format |
| `add`, `rm`, `mv` | paths, `-A` (within the worktree), `-u` |
| `commit` | `-m` (repeatable), `-a`, `--amend` (unpushed commits only), `--allow-empty` |
| `log` | `-n`, `--oneline`, `--stat`, `--format` with `%H %h %s %an %ad %cr`, `<rev>`, `-- <path>` |
| `show` | a commit, `<rev>:<path>` |
| `branch`, `switch`, `checkout`, `restore` | create, list, delete; `switch -c`; `checkout <branch>`, `checkout -- <path>`; `restore [--staged] <path>` |
| `reset` | `--soft`, `--mixed`, `--hard` (the worktree is a temp workspace, so `--hard` loses only unpushed work, and says so first) |
| `merge` | fast-forward and three-way, with diff3 conflict markers in text files; a binary conflict keeps both versions as `<path>.ours` and `<path>.theirs` for the agent to choose; `--abort` |
| `stash` | `push`, `pop`, `list`, `drop` |
| `fetch`, `pull`, `push` | to and from `ur://` only |
| `tag` | lightweight and annotated |
| `grep` | fixed strings and RE2 regular expressions, `-n`, `-i`, `-l`, paths |
| Not supported | `rebase`, `cherry-pick`, `revert`, `bisect`, `blame`, `submodule`, `worktree`, `lfs`, hooks, filters, `config` beyond `user.*` reads; each answers "not supported by ur git; supported: …" so the agent changes approach instead of retrying |

### 13.6 The agent's tool

One tool, `git(args: string[])`, so models use the syntax they were trained on ([Rpt:bb] found one argv-style command beats many typed tools for agents). It parses only the flags in 13.5's table, runs with no pager and no color, caps output at 256 KiB, and returns git's text plus `details` for the UI: a structured diff for `diff`, `show` and `merge` conflicts, a file list for `status`. Its writes are W-tier (DESIGN §16.5); a push to a repo the agent's grants do not cover is refused by EVS as any write is. Its reads taint as `evs_read`'s do (§7.8): `clone`, `fetch` and `pull`, and any command that fetches an object lazily, check the sealed provenance of each push they take objects from, and where one shows a tainted run, a tagged sidecar other than the member's own enclave or another member, or none they can read, taint the run before they write the worktree or answer, so nothing they bring in is read in an untainted run; `ur git`, run from a harness, taints each run its process ancestry binds (DESIGN §16.6). In an enclave every result is untrusted (§11.10).

### 13.7 Safety

No hooks, attributes-driven filters, smudge or clean drivers, config includes or submodules run, since there is nothing to run them with, and none is left for a person's own git: the porcelain writes a worktree's `.git/config` with the repository format, the remote and the branches alone, never a `core.*` command (`fsmonitor`, `hooksPath`, `sshCommand`, `pager`, `editor`), an alias, an include, a filter or a hook, and in the local profile the file tools refuse every `.git` path (§7.5), so a shell prompt's or an editor's git that opens a worktree on the person's computer finds nothing an agent planted to run (IC-7). Paths are checked as stock git's fsck does after its 2025-2026 advisories: no `..`, no `.git` component in any case or Unicode-folded spelling, no absolute paths, no path through a symlink. Symlinks are stored as links but checked out as links only when the target stays inside the worktree; on phones and in the browser they are checked out as small text files naming the target. Limits: a file of 50 MiB, 100,000 files, and the workspace caps of §7.5.

### 13.8 For people

`ur git` runs the same porcelain from the CLI, so a host without a system git, an enclave image being built, or a person on a locked-down machine can still clone and push EVS repos. On desktops with a system git, `ur mount` and the local tier (DESIGN §11.11) stay the normal path.

### 13.9 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| go-git | broad features | ~20× memory on clone; fast-forward-only merge; 11 advisories in 2026; v5 does not build for wasip1 | test oracle only |
| isomorphic-git (JS) | merge, stash; runs in browsers | a second implementation in JavaScript; no rebase; CORS | rejected |
| libgit2 | complete | cgo; GPLv2 with exception; its Go binding is abandoned | rejected |
| The system git | complete | absent on phones; a host process, which CO-6 forbids the local Harness | used in enclaves and desktops' local tier only |

### 13.10 Decisions proposed

**D-GIT-1 (proposed).** A porcelain over sidecar's existing git codecs, writing git's on-disk layout with stock git's ignore, rename, mode and folding rules, talking only to EVS; a full clone, not a sparse one, opens in stock git. *Why:* R-GIT-1, R-GIT-4; the codecs already round-trip with stock git.

**D-GIT-2 (proposed).** Lazy blob fetch and sparse checkout by prefix. *Why:* phones; EVS reads by path.

**D-GIT-3 (proposed).** One argv tool with a whitelist and explicit "not supported" answers. *Why:* 13.6.

### 13.11 Questions

**Q-GIT-1.** Rebase? *Options:* (a) no; (b) a simple rebase of linear local commits. *Answer:* (a) at launch; merge covers the agent's need to integrate, and coding agents' own instructions avoid rewriting history. A linear `rebase` of unpushed commits is the first addition if agents trip over its absence. *Decider:* peer review.

**Q-GIT-2.** Other remotes (GitHub) from the local Harness? *Answer:* no: CO-6 gives the local Harness EVS for storage, and a GitHub remote would be network access by another name; enclaves use the system git for GitHub, through their egress. *Decider:* owner.

### 13.12 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Merge bugs corrupt an agent's work | medium | lost edits | conformance against stock git (§18); merges never push by themselves |
| Agents expect commands it lacks | high | wasted turns | the explicit answers of 13.5; telemetry of unsupported commands, counted (no arguments), to choose additions |

### 13.13 Phasing

M13a: clone, status, diff, add, commit, log, show, branch, switch, restore, reset, fetch, pull, push, and merge, fast-forward and three-way, which `pull` and a push refused at a stale tip need (13.4); M14, before any provider: stash, tag, grep. §19.

## 14. Server services, routes, tables and metadata

### 14.1 Purpose and scope

What runs on URnetwork's servers for compute, its routes and tables, its jobs, and what it can see: the compute rows of the published metadata list (I-18). Placement follows DESIGN §4.5 and [owner decision 594](DESIGN.md#od-594).

### 14.2 The compute service

| Part | Design |
|---|---|
| Engine | `computeservice` in the sidecar repo, hosted by `server/cli/compute`, one warp service block `compute`, horizontally scaled and stateless; state in Postgres and Redis |
| Host | `compute.bringyour.com`, TCP 443 behind the load balancer; long streams carry an SSE comment every 15 s under the lb's stall timeouts |
| Auth | a sidecar's service token with its DPoP proof (DESIGN §7.8); the token names the sidecar, the broker reads its network, roles, tags and budgets from the signed id-only projection (DESIGN §8.8) |
| Broker | the evidence tunnel, prepare, infer, disputes (§6.6); holds and settlement through Redis scripts and the settlement stream (§9.7); K_P's signer (§10.5); search admissions, holds and charges, relaying each payee and nonce sealed to the search signer, unread (§21.5) |
| Search signer | `searchsigner`, internal, on hosts of its own with its own credentials, Redis and database, which only the broker reaches, over mTLS: the payer key, the payee screen and its lists, the settlement and transfer watchers over two Base sources, and the float (§21.5); it never learns a network |
| Orchestrator | enclave lifecycles (§11.6), one owner per enclave by a Redis lease renewed every 10 s; provider calls, evidence and provisioning relays; one VM per device authorization, never a retry of its own, and the timeouts of the states before `running` (§11.6) |
| Collateral cache | §5.7, in Redis with each item's own expiry |
| Adapters | Chutes, engy, SayGM, Hippius, Lium, Cathedral and, in development, CI and staging alone, the reference provider (§4.6, §11.3), each with its credentials from vault |
| Logs | request ids, status codes, latencies and the compute rows' ids; never bodies (IC-13); no line per search authorization, whose counts go to metrics (§21.5) |

### 14.3 Routes

| Route | Auth | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET compute/v1/catalog` | sidecar | remote catalog entries and prices, versioned (§6.3) |
| `GET compute/v1/tunnel?host=` | sidecar | a WebSocket byte relay to an allowlisted provider host on 443, inside which the device runs its own TLS (§5.7) |
| `POST compute/v1/infer/prepare` | sidecar | a model's instance E2E keys and one-use nonces, fetched with URnetwork's provider key |
| `POST compute/v1/infer` | sidecar | one remote call: `ComputeInferHeader` and the sealed envelope; streams the provider's chunks and `ur_usage` |
| `POST compute/v1/infer/dispute` | sidecar | a `charge_mismatch` (§6.7) |
| `POST compute/v1/infer/authorize` | sidecar | a direct call's btauth/1 headers, after floor, providers, budget and hold (§6.6) |
| `POST compute/v1/search/authorize` | sidecar | one search's admission, after the asset, the policy's ceiling, the web search clause, grace state, budgets, the daily cap and the search cap (§9.11), rate and hold; it relays the device's payee and nonce, sealed to `searchsigner`, and the signer's sealed authorization back, reading neither; it carries the device's unreported outcome counts (§21.5, §21.8) |
| `POST compute/v1/search/outcomes` | sidecar | a device's search outcome counts by class not yet reported, at most once a day, added to the hourly counts across all networks (§21.8) |
| `POST compute/v1/budget/raise` | sidecar, with the approved `compute_budget_raise` decision | a raise past a default budget (§16.3's kind 21), under `Idempotency-Key: <effect_key>`, the use and the new amount stored in one transaction |
| `GET compute/v1/collateral/{vendor}/{item}` | none | vendor-signed collateral (§5.7) |
| `POST compute/v1/enclaves` | sidecar, with the approved `enclave_create` decision | create (§11.7), under `Idempotency-Key: <effect_key>`, the use kept with the enclave's row (§16.3) |
| `GET compute/v1/enclaves`, `GET …/{id}` | sidecar | the network's enclaves the caller may see |
| `GET …/{id}/evidence?nonce=` | sidecar (a member device of the sponsor) | the VM's evidence for that nonce |
| `POST …/{id}/evidence` | the VM's init, by a per-VM token the orchestrator gave the provider | the VM posts evidence and reads nonces (long poll) |
| `POST …/{id}/provision` | sidecar (sponsor's device) | the sealed bundle, relayed once to the VM, never stored |
| `POST …/{id}/stop`, `/start`, `DELETE …/{id}` | sidecar, per §16.2; a start with its approved kind 19 where a tool asked for it (§7.5) | lifecycle; a stop's cause stays in the record, not here (§11.11) |
| `GET api/compute/balance` | sidecar or network credential | available, holds, state, auto-renew, and whether the caller may buy (§9.10), so the apps offer credit only to one who may |
| `POST api/compute/checkout` | an untagged sidecar of an Owner, a Billing admin or a member the policy grants `compute:buy`; or network credential | a Stripe Checkout session for a pack, captured only once its card passes the payer's limits, a card saved for off-session use only when its payer turns on auto-renew in that act (§9.5, §9.11) |
| `GET`/`POST api/compute/auto-renew` | as checkout | threshold and monthly settings (§9.8); a mode turned on names a card the person turning it on saved for it (§9.5) |
| `GET api/compute/charges`, `/statement` | per §9.10's roles | charges and statements |
| `GET api/compute/spend?by=` | per §9.10's roles; only from a member's consented device (DESIGN §8.5, owner decision 126): refused to tagged sidecars, enclaves included, and to ephemeral and Delegation-admitted ones | §9.13's spend view: each service's total since `first_charge_day` and each of its last 7 UTC days, in nano-USD, net of refunds with the refunds apart, with counts and typed units, broken down by `by` (provider, model, enclave, member; agent for the 7 days only) as opaque ids and catalog ids, with the settlement time the figures are exact to |
| `POST api/compute/refund` | Owner or Billing admin | §9.12 |
| `POST api/compute/promo/redeem` | as checkout: an untagged sidecar of an Owner, a Billing admin or a member the policy grants `compute:buy`; or network credential | redeems one promotion code for the network (§9.11): the code's and the network's checks, the load limits counted with the day's purchases, and the redemption and its lot in one transaction; a retry answers the same lot; five failed codes a network a UTC day, then `rate_limited` |
| `GET`/`POST api/compute/terms` | `GET`: any member device; `POST`: an untagged sidecar of an Owner or Admin, or network credential | the compute terms' version and the clauses the network accepted, by whom and when (`compute_terms`); `POST` accepts the web search clause, which the broker's projection then carries, and a checkout records the same with a first purchase (§21.9) |
| Stripe webhooks, App Store and Play notifications | the markets' own | the existing endpoints, with the `compute.*` product family (§9.5) |
| `POST api/subscription/verify-apple-transaction`, `/verify-play-purchase` | the network's credential, as for Pro's | the apps' purchase reports, which Pro's purchases use today, taking the `compute.*` family too: a StoreKit transaction or Play purchase token from `Compute().StorePurchase` (§15.3), bound to its network by the `appAccountToken` (Play: the obfuscated account id) the app set to the network id at purchase; verified with the store and credited once by `(market, market_ref)`, the transaction or order id, through the webhooks' idempotency gates, whichever of the report and the store's notification arrives first, a Play consumable then consumed and a plan change granting the difference; a purchase that names no network binds as Pro's do, to the network whose app reports it, and one naming a deleted network credits none and is refunded through Play, or answered by support on the App Store (§9.5) |

Every route is classified in `route_authz.go` and documented in `connect/api/bringyour.yml`, and mirrored in sdk, as DESIGN CONVENTIONS §8 requires. No agent reaches `checkout`, `auto-renew`, `refund` or `promo/redeem`: they need an untagged member device, and MCP has no tool for them. An agent reads `spend` only through `compute_spend`, on its person's consented device (§9.10).

### 14.4 Tables and Redis keys

Migration groups, additive and pending under `sidecar_pending` until their milestone's exit (DESIGN §19.7):

| Group | Tables | Milestone |
|---|---|---|
| MG-C1 ledger | `compute_account`, `compute_lot`, `compute_charge` (daily partitions), `compute_charge_lot`, `compute_charge_day`, `compute_charge_total`, `compute_charge_pruned`, `compute_auto_renew`, `compute_dispute`, `compute_budget_raise` (approval id, use, effect key, subject id, period, amount, expiry), `compute_promo_code` (a keyed hash of the code, campaign, value, cap, count, last day, whether a paid lot is asked, the operator and the reason) and `compute_promo_redemption` (code, network, lot, the redeeming sidecar's opaque id, time; unique per code and network) (§9.11), `compute_payer` (a payer's keyed hash and first purchase day, no network, 2 years) and `compute_payer_day` (the hash, a day, its purchases' sum, no network, 30 days) (§9.11), `compute_terms` (network, terms version, clauses accepted, the accepting user and time; the web search clause from M13, §21.9) | M12 |
| MG-C2 providers | `compute_provider` (id, kind, status, gate results; Parallel's gateway as kind `search`), `compute_search_outcome_hour` (hour, outcome class, count, across all networks), `compute_provider_price` (hourly reads), `compute_provider_ledger` (balance reads, spends, credits), `compute_gamma_deposit` (netuid, hotkey, cap, balance read), `compute_gamma_op` (each mint and spend, block, extrinsic), `compute_search_flag` (the sanctions records: network, sidecar, reason `payee_refused` or `out_of_band`, payee, transaction, time; §21.5) | M12 |
| MG-S1 signer, in `searchsigner`'s own database | `search_signer_nonce` (each nonce issued, its value and window, settled or lapsed; no ticket, payee or network; a day past its window), `search_signer_facilitator` (the facilitator's settlement addresses), `search_signer_screen` (the screen's addresses, each list's source and fetch time) | M13 |
| MG-C3 enclaves | `compute_enclave` (id, network, sponsor sidecar, shape, provider, state, incarnation, bootstrap hash, times), `compute_enclave_event` (transitions, 90 days after removal) | M14 |

MG-C1's rollups use `UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT`, which needs PostgreSQL 15 or later; production runs 18 (xops/main/ansible/playbook-dbs.yml:1280), and the local, T3 and canary databases must run 15 or later too.

Redis: `{cmp_<network_id>}` (projection and holds), `{cmp_<network_id>}:b:<subject_id>` (budget counters per day and month), `{cmpq_<shard>}` (the settlement stream), `{cmpc_<sha256>}` (collateral), `{cmpe_<enclave_id>}` (orchestrator lease, nonces in flight), `{cmpr_<network_id>}` (a network's search rate and its searches today, against `day_max`), `{cmps}` (the global search limiter), `{cmpa}` (open search admissions, ticket to network, sidecar, agent, request id and hold, on a Redis instance of its own with persistence off and no backups, dropped at the signer's report or an hour past the window; `searchsigner`'s own Redis, persistence off and no backups, holds the other half, ticket to nonce, payee and value, until settlement or lapse), `{cmpk_<network_id>}` (a network's failed promotion code redemptions this UTC day, §9.11), `{cmpp_<k_p>}` (direct calls pending while their provider's lookup fails: nonce to hold, no hash, at most 24 hours), `{cmpo}` (this hour's search outcome counts by class, across all networks), `{cmpd_<k_p>}` (direct calls in flight: nonce to hash and hold, and the nonces used in the last 15 seconds, dropped at settlement, at most 10 minutes).

A script touches one hash tag, as production's Redis Cluster requires: a network's projection, holds and budget counters share `{cmp_<network_id>}`, so one script holds and checks the floor and the budgets; a network's search rate, the global search limiter, the open searches and a K_P's nonces, each in its own slot, take a second script after the first admits, which undoes the hold when it refuses.

### 14.5 Jobs

| Job (taskworker) | Every | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `compute_settle` | 2 s or 500 charges | stream → Postgres (§9.7), each new charge added to its day and lifetime rollups (§9.13) |
| `compute_rollup_day` | daily, at 02:00 UTC | re-derives the closed day's `compute_charge_day` rows from its charges, grouped by their stored columns, and alarms on any difference, since `compute_settle` writes them; checks each network's totals against its day rows and `compute_charge_pruned` (§9.13); deletes web searches' charge rows past 72 hours, which the day rows already count (§21.5); drops charge partitions past 90 days, and day rows past 400 into `compute_charge_pruned` in the same transaction |
| `compute_auto_renew` | 1 min | threshold top-ups and their retries (§9.8) |
| `compute_enclave_meter` | 10 min | `enclave_run` charges and next holds (§9.6) |
| `compute_provider_prices` | hourly | provider prices into the catalog; margin alarms; each direct provider's costliest worst case for the exposure rule, a rise paging (§6.6) |
| `compute_canary` | hourly | from a sidecar of URnetwork's own, in a network of its own, a call of known token counts to each provider's catalog models, compared with the provider's usage, the charge and its bill; a gap over 2% pages (§6.7) |
| `compute_gamma_mint`, `compute_gamma_spend` | 5 min | §10.4 |
| `compute_gamma_watch` | each finalized block | every extrinsic from our hotkeys, matched by hash against what the spend job submitted; any other pauses its deposit (§10.5) |
| `compute_reconcile` | daily | §10.7 |
| `compute_search_settle` | each finalized Base block, in `searchsigner`, from both Base sources | `AuthorizationUsed` events for the payer address, each matched by nonce to the payee and value the signer signed, its sender checked against the facilitator's addresses, reported to the broker by ticket, which charges them, an out-of-band one kept as a sanctions record; tickets whose window a finalized block has passed, unused, reported lapsed and their holds released; a used nonce the signer did not issue is charged to no one and alarms (§21.5) |
| `compute_search_tickets` | 1 min | releases the hold of an admission no report reached an hour past its window, as after the signer's failover (§21.5) |
| `compute_sanctions_list` | hourly, in `searchsigner` | fetches the screen's lists, OFAC's SDN digital currency addresses first; a fetch failing for 24 hours pages, and at 72 hours signing stops (§21.5) |
| `compute_search_watch` | each Base block, in `searchsigner` | a USDC transfer from the payer that settles no authorization the signer issued, to its payee and value, or a used nonce the signer did not issue, stops signing and refills and pages |
| `compute_direct_settle` | 1 min | direct calls: receipts and usage lookups by nonce or hash, in three states: `unknown` a minute after the window releases the hold at no charge, `in progress` keeps it, `finished` settles it; while a provider's lookup fails, its holds stay pending, uncharged, and the broker signs no new call to it; a hold pending 24 hours is released at no charge (§6.6) |
| `compute_search_float` | hourly, in `searchsigner` | refills the payer address only by what settlements of the signer's own authorizations since the last refill explain, up to two days of searches, from Coinbase, whose withdrawals go only to the payer address; pages below one day |
| `compute_search_outcomes` | hourly | moves `{cmpo}` into `compute_search_outcome_hour` and computes Parallel's failure rate; pages above 5% in an hour of at least 100 searches, and reports each day's rate to the owner monthly (§21.8) |
| `compute_suspend` | 1 min | §9.9's states, the indexer enclave's reserve and grace among them |
| `compute_promo_lapse` | hourly | each promotional lot past its `expire_time`: what is left becomes its `lapsed_nano_usd`, and the account's settled balance and the projection's `available` and promo fall by as much, in one transaction and never as a charge (§9.11) |

### 14.6 Metadata rows

Added to DESIGN §2.8's list (I-18), by a design-records fold:

| Row | What the servers see | Kept |
|---|---|---|
| compute-1 | per remote call: network, sidecar, opaque agent id, model id, provider, instance id, catalog version, declared token maxima, reported usage, request and response sizes (TEE path), start and end times (a direct call's kept to the minute once it settles, since its provider keeps its own), request id, outcome code, the route; a direct call's nonce and hash only until it settles (at most 10 minutes, in Redis, never in a log) | holds in Redis ≤ 1 h, a pending direct hold ≤ 24 h; charge rows 90 days; daily rollups (no request ids, no instance ids) 400 days |
| compute-2 | per lot: network, kind, market, the market's reference, amounts, times, reversal or lapse; per promotion code, a keyed hash of it, its campaign, value, cap, count, last day and who made it; per redemption, the code, the network, the lot, the redeeming sidecar's opaque id and the time; per payer, apart from any network: a keyed hash of a card's fingerprint or an App Store account's `appTransactionId`, its first purchase day and each day's sum (§9.11) | lots, promotion codes and redemptions 7 years (financial records); a payer's first day 2 years, its days 30 days |
| compute-3 | per charge: kind, subject ids, the member it counts to, model or shape, units, amount and cost, times; daily and monthly totals, a day's by sidecar, member, agent, model or shape, provider and enclave; lifetime totals by kind, member, model or shape, provider and enclave, with no day, sidecar or agent; per kind, the sums of day rows dropped past 400 days; and the network's first charge day (§9.13) | as compute-1; lifetime totals, the dropped rows' sums and the first charge day for the account's life, deleted with the network |
| compute-4 | per enclave: id, network, sponsor sidecar, shape, provider, the provider's VM id, states and times, incarnations, the bootstrap hash, egress mode (already api-7's), its create's approval id and use (§16.3); whether it is the network's indexer, for its reserve and grace (§9.9) | life + 90 days |
| compute-5 | in transit only: evidence bytes, nonces, sealed provisioning bundles; for the evidence tunnel, the host, sizes and times (its contents are the device's TLS) | not stored; relayed within 10 minutes; tunnel counts in metrics only |
| compute-6 | auto-renew settings and budget amounts by subject id (from the projection), and each raise kind 21 approved, with its approval id and use (§16.3) | while set; a raise until its expiry |
| compute-7 | URnetwork's provider balances, gamma deposits, mints, spends and hotkeys (public on chain) | 7 years |
| compute-8 | disputes: request id, the device's and the provider's usage numbers | 400 days |
| compute-9 | collateral items by hash (public vendor data); no requester | each item's expiry |
| compute-10 | per search: network, sidecar, opaque agent id, request id, authorization and settlement times to the minute, settled or lapsed, the charge; the broker's ticket for it in memory until the signer reports; the signer, apart, the authorization's nonce, payee and amount in memory until it settles or lapses on Base's finalized head, about 30 minutes, and its issued nonces, with their values and windows, without a network; a sanctions record for a payee the screen refused or an authorization settled by a sender other than the facilitator: network, sidecar, payee, transaction and time (§21.5); never the query, the mode or the results | per-search rows 72 hours, then compute-3's day rows; issued nonces a day past their window; sanctions records for OFAC's recordkeeping period, which counsel confirms |
| compute-11 | per search, its outcome class (`ok`, `provider_error`, `timeout`, `refused`), which a device reports with its next search authorization or in a daily count: seen with the reporting network only in transit, and added at once to an hourly count per class across all networks, never kept by network, sidecar or agent. New with CO-30: before it, the servers saw no search's outcome (§21.8) | the hourly counts 400 days; no report kept |
| api-7 (amended) | repo kinds now include `agents` and `agent` (§20.4), so evs and api see how many agent repos a member has | as api-7 |

Web fetch adds no row: a fetch is traffic, counted as DESIGN §2.8's rows already count any, and the broker never sees one (§22.7).

Mail and calendars (§23.12) add none either: mail is read on the device, a calendar call is traffic through an exit, and a saved link is one more repo of the `secret` kind, which api-7 already counts.
Context history (§24) adds no row: its entries are vault files, which DESIGN §2.8's evs rows already cover, and no server sees a call's context (§24.11).

Listeners (§26) add no row but one kind: api-7's and evs-1's kind lists gain `listeners`, one repo a network, so evs and api see that a network has one; its files' writers, padded sizes and write times are evs-4's and evs-11's, as any repo's, and a live ask is connect traffic (§26.11).

### 14.7 Observability

Metrics: calls, latency and outcome by provider and model; attestation failures by reason; holds, settlement lag; accounts by §9.9 state; auto-renew successes and failures; promotion code redemptions and refusals, by code and reason; provider balance in days; deposits, mints, spends; enclaves by state; dispute rate; search authorizations, settlements, lapses and outcome classes; settlement lag. Pages: a provider failing every call for 5 minutes; attestation failures above 5% for 10 minutes; settlement lag over 60 s; a provider balance under a day; an unknown `GammaSpent` from our hotkeys; the policy within 14 days of `not_after`; the newest signed ticket within 7 days of its horizon (§5.4); a reconciliation gap over 1%; a day's spend rollup differing from its charges, or a network's totals from its day rows and pruned sums; lapsed search authorizations above 5% for 10 minutes; the payer float under one day of searches; Parallel's failure rate above 5% in an hour of at least 100 searches (§21.8); any USDC transfer from the payer that settles no authorization the signer issued; a used nonce the signer did not issue; a payee the screen refused, or an authorization settled outside the facilitator; the screen's lists unfetched for 24 hours; Base's two sources disagreeing; disputes from at least 3 networks past 0.5% of a provider's requests in a day; a canary gap over 2%; a provider's realized margin under 5% for a week; a direct provider's costliest worst case rising.

### 14.8 Capacity

A remote call is small: a few to tens of KiB in, a stream out; at 1,000 calls a second the broker carries tens of MB/s and writes 1,000 charge rows a second in 2-second batches (a few transactions a second), each also upserting its charges' day and lifetime rollup rows in key order, at most two a charge and usually far fewer (§9.13). Enclaves are hundreds to thousands, each a few rows an hour. A search costs the broker one Redis script and a relay, and the signer one signature, one read of Base and one Redis write; its bytes go from the device to Parallel's gateway, never through the broker. None approaches the load the escrow and evs paths already carry (DESIGN §19.9). Context history adds bytes to evs and few pushes: session entries ride in the pushes a run's calls already make, and an enclave's ride its calls' pushes as a desktop's do (§24.5, §24.10's pushes).

### 14.9 Decisions proposed

**D-CSRV-1 (proposed).** One new service, `compute`, for the broker and orchestrator, and an internal one, `searchsigner`, for the search payer key; billing on api; jobs on taskworker. *Why:* DESIGN §4.5's pattern; streaming needs its own block; the payer key apart from the broker, so no one system joins a search's payment to its network (§21.5).

**D-CSRV-2 (proposed).** compute-1 to compute-11 are the whole of what the servers keep. *Why:* I-18; IC-13.

### 14.10 Operations

Compute adds standing work for URnetwork's operators beside the services above, carried by a compute rota of named operators. Each line has a runbook in xops before its milestone's exit, and its page-class alerts join DESIGN's two-person out-of-hours rota ([owner decision 143](DESIGN.md#od-143)):

| Work | Cadence | Who | When it fails |
|---|---|---|---|
| The compute policy (§5.4): a profile as a provider rolls an image, a model id, a disclosure text, a `direct`, `search` or `services` line, a revocation | about weekly, by inference; a revocation the same day | two of the compute-policy key's four holders | a holder away: any other two sign; a provider's new image not yet signed: TEE calls to it fail closed until it is, so the rota follows providers' release notes; a token lost: the release key certifies a new compute-policy key |
| Freshness tickets, 14 days ahead (§5.4) | a weekly sitting, with the policy's | the same holders; the ticket host posts one a day | a missed sitting leaves 7 days of slack, paged from its start; past it, remote model calls, enclave creates and searches stop |
| The staging policy (§5.4) | weekly; it expires after 7 days | the staging key's holder | staging and CI stop; no user is touched |
| The treasury (§10): TAO buys, the reserve, mints and spends, reconciliation | weekly buys; jobs every few minutes; daily reconciliation | two of three owners' Ledgers for the reserve; the jobs; the rota on a page | a deposit or provider balance under a day pages; a stale price feed blocks mints, never spends, for at least a day (§10.4) |
| The search payer (§21.5) | hourly refills, by its job | the job; the rota on a page | a stopped payer key: searches answer a named error until the rota rotates the key and tells Parallel the new payer address |
| The provider adapters (Chutes, engy, SayGM, Hippius, Lium, Cathedral); each provider's gate and disclosure re-read every 90 days (G-PROV-any) | each provider release; each 90 days | the compute rota | a provider suspends URnetwork's account: its models and shapes leave the catalog, running enclaves are told to move (§11.11), calls fail with a named error, and E6's notice clause is invoked |
| Codex and Claude Code against the gateway (§18) | each of their releases | the compute rota | a failing harness release: the gateway's fix ships with the next `ur` release, whose notes name the harness versions that pass |
| URnetwork's OAuth clients and their verification (G-CONN-<service>, §19.2) | each scope change, and as each provider asks | the compute rota | a client suspended: that service's connections fail with a named error and the apps say why, until the provider restores it |

By inference, this is about one person's full time from M12 and one and a half from M14, beside the holders' weekly sitting, counted apart from §19.4's engineering.

## 15. CLI, MCP, sdk and app surfaces

### 15.1 The `ur` commands

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `ur harness [--agent <name>] [--model <name>] [--enclave <name>] [--json]` | a Harness in the terminal, or attached to an enclave's (§7.11) |
| `ur harness rpc [--session <id>\|--new] [--harness ur\|pig]` | Pi's RPC on stdio; what attach runs over SSH (§7.10) |
| `ur harness rpc --manage` | the whole Harness on stdio: Pi's prompt, steer, follow_up, abort, get_state and get_messages, each naming its agent, and `ur_list_agents`, `ur_launch_agent`, `ur_subscribe`, `ui_response` and `ur_continue`; what management runs over SSH, which the enclave's SSH server joins to the Harness outside the agents' container (§7.10) |
| `ur harness ls [--enclave <name>] [--live] [--json]` | the person's Harnesses, this device's and each enclave's, with each agent's model, state and newest summary (`harness_list`, §7.10); summaries printed as `ur agents` prints prose (DESIGN §16.11) |
| `ur harness export <run>` | the run as Pi JSONL v3, every node and part: `ur record export --run <id> --bodies` under RECORD.md section 9's rules, confirmed on /dev/tty or in an app and recorded as a `disclosure` entry first (§24.6) |
| `ur harness runs [--agent <a>] [--size]` | a member's runs with their sizes, per agent and per enclave, blobs apart (§24.10) |
| `ur harness show <run> [--call <n>]` | a run's tree, or one call's rebuilt context, printed only to a terminal and otherwise as stubs, first tainting each run its process ancestry binds (§24.6) |
| `ur harness continue <run> [--at <node>] [--model <name>] [--enclave <name>]` | continue or fork a run here, or in the person's enclave, which reads it from the vault, on its old model unless `--model` names another; with `--enclave`, refused to a caller with a harness process among its ancestors, and sent only once the person confirms on /dev/tty or in an app (§24.7) |
| `ur models [--local\|--tee\|--provider <p>]` | the catalog for this device and policy, by canonical name, with each model's label, efforts and disclosure line (§2.8) |
| `ur models pull <id>` | download a local model and its engine |
| `ur models settings`, `ur models set [--default <name>] [--tee-only on\|off] [--sign-in-mail withhold\|allow] [--allow <glob>…] [--harness <h> --tier <t> <name>]` | the person's `models` key (§16.4): the default model, TEE-only, sign-in mail's withholding (§23.4), the models and providers allowed and each harness's tiers; `set` confirmed on /dev/tty and refused to a caller with a harness process among its ancestors (DESIGN §5.8), as `ur disclosures ack` is |
| `ur infer --model <name> "<prompt>"` | one prompt, streamed |
| `ur disclosures [--json]`, `ur disclosures ack <id>` | every disclosure (§2.8): its version, summary, whether it asks before first use, the version the person acknowledged and the network's, with who gave it; `ack <id> --network`, on an Owner's or Admin's device, acknowledges for the network's tagged and cloud sidecars (CO-41), signing the statement and saving it into the `compute` block as a policy change; `ack` prints the whole text and takes the person's answer on /dev/tty, refused without a terminal or with a harness process among its ancestors (DESIGN §5.8). `ur infer`, `ur harness` and `ur search` ask the same way before a first use that needs it, and otherwise answer `disclosure_required` |
| `ur gateway status`, `token --harness <h>`, `grants`, `config <h>`, `run <h> -- <command>` | §8; `run` for a harness with no credential command (Q-GW-6) |
| `ur install-harness <h> --gateway` | writes §8.8's settings beside DESIGN §16.7's entries |
| `ur compute status`, `buy <pack>`, `redeem <code>`, `auto-renew threshold\|monthly\|off …`, `charges`, `statement --month`, `refund <lot>`, `budget …` | §9 (buy, redeem and auto-renew on devices of an Owner, a Billing admin or a member granted `compute:buy`, `redeem` refused with a harness process among its ancestors, as `terms accept` is (§9.11); refund for Owner and Billing admin) |
| `ur compute budget [ls]`, `ur compute budget raise <agent\|grant> --day <usd>\|--month <usd>\|--run <usd>` | budgets and what is left of them (§16.4); `raise` files `compute_budget_raise` (kind 21, §16.3) and waits for its approval |
| `ur compute spend [--by <dim>] [--json]` | where credits went (§9.13): each service's total and last 7 UTC days, net of refunds, `<dim>` one of provider, model (a shape for enclaves), enclave, member, or agent for the last 7 days only, within the caller's role |
| `ur compute terms [--json]`, `ur compute terms accept` | the compute terms' version and the clauses the network accepted; `accept` prints the web search clause and takes an Owner's or Admin's answer on /dev/tty, refused with a harness process among its ancestors (§21.9) |
| `ur enclave create <name> --shape <s> [--egress auto\|<exit>\|tag:<t>\|none]` | §11.7; asks for the provider's disclosure where the person has not acknowledged it (§2.8), then prints the approval prompt and waits |
| `ur enclave create <name> --role indexer`, `ur mail indexer grant`, `ur mail indexer revoke` | the network's indexer enclave and a member's grant of their mailbox (§11.10) |
| `ur enclave ls`, `show <name>`, `stop`, `start`, `rm`, `egress <mode>`, `keeper <device>`, `held <name>`, `release <name> [<ref>…]` | §11; `held` lists the versions §7.8's hold keeps from the enclave's container, and `release` files kind 24 for them |
| `ur enclave attach <name>`, `ur enclave ssh <name> [cmd]` | §7.10, §12 |
| `ur ssh <host> [cmd]`, `ur ssh config`, `ur ssh agent`, `ur ssh known-hosts <host>` | §12 |
| `ur git …` | §13 |
| `ur agents [ls]`, `ur agents send <name> "<text>"`, `ur agents broadcast "<text>"`, `ur agents inbox [--thread <id>]`, `ur agents reply <thread> "<text>"` | §20 |
| `ur search "<query>"… [--objective <text>] [--mode <m>] [--json]` | one web search on Parallel, from the device through `auto` egress, charged as any; at a terminal no run binds, a first search shows the `search:parallel` disclosure on /dev/tty, and elsewhere it answers `disclosure_required` (§21.6) |
| `ur fetch <url> [--json]` | one web fetch, as an agent's (§22) |
| `ur listeners [--json] [--all] [--device <name>]` | the network's listeners grouped by device, each `ip:port (description)` with its private name, kind, list age and this device's badge (§26.7); `--all` adds this device's own view and, asked live, the person's other devices' own-view and hidden entries (§26.8); its first run shows `listeners:publish` on `/dev/tty`, then this device's own first list for the person to confirm, before a desktop publishes (§26.6) |
| `ur listeners label <port>[/udp] "<text>"` or `--clear`; `ur listeners hide <port>[/udp]` or `--device`; `ur listeners unhide …`; `ur listeners refresh [<device>]` | this device's labels and hides (§26.6), `label` and `unhide` confirmed on `/dev/tty` and refused to a caller with a harness process among its ancestors, since a label is the person's word to the network and `unhide` opens an entry to the listeners rule; a live ask (§26.8) |
| `ur calendar link set <label>` with `--caldav <url> --user <name>`, `--ics`, `--google` or `--microsoft`, each with `--connection <label>` or making one (§25.13), and `--egress direct` for a `caldav` or `ics` link (§23.7); `ur calendar link ls`, `rm <label>`, `default <label>` | a calendar link, its secret read on `/dev/tty` or taken from the provider's consent page, never from argv; `set`, `rm` and `default` each confirmed on `/dev/tty` or in an app's UI (§23.6) |
| `ur calendar [--from <date>] [--to <date>] [--calendar <label>] [--json]` | the person's events, as `calendar_list` reads them (§23.8); before printing one anywhere, it taints each run its process ancestry binds, as `ur search` does (DESIGN D-MCP-23) |
| `ur connect <service> [--feature <f>…] [--label <l>]`; `ur connect <label> --add <feature>`; `ur connect <label> --here`; `ur connect --issuer <url> --client-id <id> --api-host <h>… --scope <s>… [--label <l>]` | a connection by §25.5's flow, confirmed on `/dev/tty`, through the system browser; the last form a person's own definition, on desktops (§25.4); `--here` makes a connection another platform made usable on this desktop (§25.7); `ur connect <label> --egress direct\|auto` sets its route, confirmed on `/dev/tty` (§25.8, Q-CONN-16) |
| `ur connections ls [--json]`, `ur connections show <label>` | the member's connections: label, service, account, features and scopes, state, last refresh; never a token (§25.6) |
| `ur disconnect <label>` | revokes at the provider where it can, deletes the connection's repo and the calendar links that name it, confirmed on `/dev/tty` (§25.7) |
| `ur approve <id> --events <i>,…` | approves only the listed events of a kind-25 batch, the rest answered `declined` (§23.9) |
| `ur approvals [--json]`, `ur approvals mode auto\|ask [--kind <kind>]`, `ur approvals digest [--day <date>] [--json]` | the person's automatic-approval setting per kind, the network's limit, `approvals:auto`'s state and today's count; `mode` confirmed on `/dev/tty` and refused to a caller with a harness process among its ancestors; the day's automatic approvals with their verdicts (§27.9, §27.10) |

### 15.2 MCP tools

Added to DESIGN §16.5's catalog, with its tiers:

| Tool | Tier | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `compute_balance` | R | the session agent's budget left and whether the network can pay (§9.9's state); never the network's balance |
| `compute_spend` | R; labels per §9.13, unsigned ones between untrusted-data markers | §9.13's spend view within the person's role (§9.10), as the Harness's (§7.5); only in a session on the person's consented device (untagged, neither ephemeral nor Delegation-admitted): a tagged sidecar's, an enclave's included, and a CI runner's or server's get none |
| `enclave_list`, `enclave_status` | R | |
| `enclave_create` | O | `enclave_create` action (§16.3) |
| `enclave_stop`, `enclave_start` | `enclave_stop` W in an untainted session and refused in a tainted one, the error naming the app and `ur enclave stop`; `enclave_start` O, a kind 19 (§16.3) | a stop revokes only the running incarnation, by its own `SidecarRevoke` (§11.4); a start's admission runs on the approving device; neither reaches the network's indexer enclave (§11.11) |
| `enclave_delete` | O | `enclave_delete` action (§16.3), its removal run on the approving device |
| `enclave_exec` | W; O (kind 24) in a tainted run when the enclave's egress is not `none` or it is another member's (§7.8) | `ssh_exec` to an enclave the session's sidecar may reach |
| `agent_register`, `agent_summary`, `agent_list`, `agent_find`, `agent_send`, `agent_broadcast`, `agent_inbox`, `agent_close` | per §20.10 | in an enclave, through the container socket, every call a tainted run's (§11.10) |
| `web_search` | R; untrusted result | §21.6's tool, charged to the MCP session's agent under its budget; the only web search for external harnesses, since the gateway serves none (§21.7, Q-SRCH-7); `disclosure_required` until the person acknowledges `search:parallel` |
| `listeners_list` | R; other devices' words as capped tokens between untrusted-data markers, free text only with `untrusted: include`, which taints first | §26.9's tool; in an enclave, through its container socket, only what the enclave may reach |
| `calendar_list` | R; untrusted result | §23.8's tool over the member's links; no link in any result (IC-18) |
| `calendar_add`, `calendar_update`, `calendar_delete` | O, `calendar_write` (§16.3): an MCP session's run counts as tainted for calendar writes, its taint missing what its harness reads by itself (§23.9, Q-CONN-14) | up to 20 events a call, one approval for the batch (§23.9) |
| `connections_list` | R | §25.9's tool; no token in any result (IC-20) |
| `service_call` | R for reads, untrusted result; O, `service_write` (§16.3), for every write and send, an MCP session's run counting as tainted for them (§25.10, Q-CONN-14), decided as a tainted run's under §27 | §25.9's tool under §25.10's classes; no `connection_request`, which only a person in the apps or at the terminal can answer (Q-CONN-12) |

External harnesses get models through the gateway, not MCP; there is no MCP inference tool, and no MCP `web_fetch` (Q-FETCH-5). In an enclave, the harnesses that run in the agents' container reach these tools through its container socket, whose every call is a tainted run's (§11.10).

Every tool whose service needs a disclosure the person has not acknowledged answers `disclosure_required`, naming the id, its summary line and the fix, `ur disclosures ack <id>` or the app's settings (on a tagged or cloud sidecar `--network`, for an Owner or Admin, §2.8): `web_search` (above); `service_call`, and the calendar tools on a `google` or `microsoft` link, at a new version of their service's text (§25.12); and `enclave_create` or a start that is a kind 19 (§11.7); MCP never prompts, and no MCP tool acknowledges (§2.8).
