Store purchases are the app's (StoreKit, Play Billing); the sdk only reports the store's transaction to `api` for verification (`Compute().StorePurchase`, §14.3), as Pro's do today, the app setting the purchase's `appAccountToken` (Play: its obfuscated account id) to the network id so the credit lands in that network, and offering the products only where `Balance()` says the person may buy and Q-BAL-13 has opened sales.

### 15.4 The apps and the browser

The apps render §7.6's events as components and own their screens (owner rule 6). **The bot tab** (CO-19) is the Harness's home in the apps, and the sdk gives it what it needs: on first open, the local model this device fits (`Models().Recommended()`, then `Pull` with progress), or adding credit (§9.5; the store purchases ship in M12 for this), only where the network's balance cannot pay (§9.9), a member who may not buy (§9.10) being told who can, and picking a remote model by canonical name and label (§6.3), with the TEE-only switch and the providers allowed beside the picker (`Models().SetSettings`, §16.4, Q-CACL-3) and a chat's model changed by `SetModel`; a harness selector between the local Harness, with only the bundled tools (CO-6), and an enclave's, with Debian's (§11.10), which the app attaches with `SidecarHarness.Attach` (§7.10) and whose agents have root in their own container (Q-ENC-3), the selector opening the enclave screen's create sheet (§11.7) where there is none and, with an enclave chosen, a model picker of what it may run under its sponsor's settings (§11.4), set over the link (`set_model`); switching back to this device forks the enclave's run here from the vault (§24.7), tainted where its nodes carry the bit, as those of a run that touched the agents' container do (D-CTXH-9), while the enclave's agent keeps its own; and the recURd view, which opens the agent graph (§20.8). **The compute screen** (CO-22), beside the balance, credits and auto-renew (§9.5, §9.8), a field to redeem a promotion code, shown to one who may buy and answering with the credit and the day it lapses or why the code was refused (`Compute().Redeem`, §9.11), and the web search clause, which an Owner or Admin accepts there (`Compute().AcceptTerms`, §21.9), shows where credits went: a row per service with its total and its last 7 days, net of refunds and saying "after $x refunded" where it has any, each opening its breakdowns as far as the person's role reaches (§9.10), and web fetch, calendar and connected-service calls at no charge, from `Compute().Spend()`; the bot tab answers the same question in words, through `compute_spend` (§7.5). The browser's page Worker gets no compute surface at launch; with the extension's Worker (Later), the Harness runs remote-only there, its evidence collateral through the broker's cache (§5.7).

**Mail and calendar** (CO-24). The apps' calendar settings save a link (`Calendar().SetLink`, or `Connect` for Google and Microsoft) from a secure field, showing what it reads and writes, and what else its credential opens, before it is saved (§23.6); the bot tab renders `mail_summary` and `calendar_event` cards (§23.11), whose "Mark these read", Undo and "Add with my phone's calendar" are the person's own acts, and kind 25's approval as one card of events, each with a switch (§23.9).

**Connected services** (CO-36, CO-37). The apps' settings gain a Connected services screen, from `Connections()`: each connection's label, service, account, features and state, with Add feature, Replace, Disconnect and, for a connection another platform made, Use on this device (`UseHere`, §25.7); and Connect, which lists the policy's services and their features in words, shows the disclosure `connect:<service>` before a service's first connection (§25.12), and runs §25.5's flow through the app's browser seam (`SetConnectHost`): `ASWebAuthenticationSession` on iOS, `AuthorizationClient` or Chrome's Auth Tab on Android, the loopback port on desktops. An agent's `connection_request` shows in the bot tab as a card whose Connect starts the same flow; only the person's tap answers it (§25.5).

**Listeners** (CO-38, CO-39). The apps gain a Listeners section, from `Listeners()`: every device's entries as `ip:port (description)`, the private name beside each, grouped by device, the person's own first; a search box; each list's age and Refresh; each entry's badge, which says when a narrowed policy blocks this device and names the rule that would open it; Copy; and Open, in the system browser, for an entry that a port or label marks as a web service (§26.10). On the person's own devices each entry offers Label and Hide, and each device Hide device; Unhide asks for confirmation, since it opens an entry to the listeners rule; an enclave's container sockets offer "map it" to its sponsor. The section's first open raises `listeners:publish` (§26.6), and until the person acknowledges it their devices publish nothing; a desktop then shows its own first list, publishing once the person confirms it there, and an Owner or Admin may acknowledge the text for the network too, for its tagged sidecars (§26.6). An admin who writes the network's policy, where its document lacks the listeners rule, is offered it, previewed and saved as any policy. Phones list their own forwards and every other device's lists (§26.4).

**Enclaves** (CO-5, CO-7). The apps' enclave screen, from `Enclaves()`, shows each enclave as a card drawn from its `enclave_status` events (§7.6): its state and why it stopped, role, address and private name, shape, provider, label, price, egress mode, keeper and the provider's disclosure line. It offers Create, whose sheet shows the provider's disclosure before kind 19's approval (§11.7); Stop, Start and Remove (§11.11); Egress, a `BridgeEgress` the sponsor files, `direct` only by kind 20 (§11.8); Keeper (§11.7); a terminal from `OpenSsh` as `agent`, or as `root` once the person confirms (§12.8); and Attach, through the bot tab's harness selector (above). With no enclave shape in the catalog, it says that enclaves await a provider (§11.3).

**The indexer enclave** (CO-19, CO-20). The apps' mail setup, where the network has no mail indexer, and its mail settings at any time offer an Owner or Admin an indexer enclave beside DESIGN's always-on device (DESIGN §15.6), only where §11.10's Where row allows: a sheet with its shape, provider, label, monthly price, what it will hold, its reserve and when it could still stop (§11.10), and the provider's disclosure, with the person's own grant switch beside it, on by default in a personal network; credit first if the balance cannot fund its reserve (§9.5, §9.9); then `Enclaves().Create` with `role: "indexer"` and kind 19's approval, whose device signs the `IndexerSet` (§11.10). Each member's mail settings then show the network's indexer enclave with its disclosure line and who set it up and how, under setup over SSH that their devices take that person's word for what it installed (§11.10); say that it reads their incoming mail as it arrives, in a Team from a day after every member was told; and carry the grant switch (`GrantMailbox`), which shows the provider's disclosure before a first grant and after a move (§11.10).

**Disclosures** (CO-31, CO-33, CO-34). The bot tab's model picker shows each model's disclosure line beside its label, and picking a model whose provider is labeled `none` opens the full text first, the pick made only once the person acknowledges it there (`AckDisclosure`); the local model's download shows `inference:local`'s line, and each assistant message's badge carries its model's (§7.6). The enclave screen's create sheet and each enclave's card show the provider's line, kind 19's card shows it again (§11.7), and the indexer's mailbox grant opens it for each member (§11.10). Search asks before the first search (§21). Settings list every disclosure from `Disclosures()`, with its full text, its version, whether it asks and the version the person acknowledged, and acknowledge any not yet acknowledged; at a new version, one that changes a fact, every line of the disclosure shows "changed" until opened, while a revision of its words changes the text with no mark (§2.8). An Owner's or Admin's network settings list the disclosures the network's tagged and cloud sidecars may need, each with the version the network acknowledged and who acknowledged it, and acknowledge one for the network after showing its whole text (`AckNetworkDisclosure`, CO-41); each such sidecar's card in the device list names who acknowledged each disclosure it relies on.

**History** (CO-25). The apps' run view, from `SidecarHarness.Runs`, lists each agent's runs with their sizes, blobs apart, and opens a run's tree and any call's rebuilt context, marked where it differs from what was sent or can no longer be checked (§24.6); at 80% of the network's storage a warning names the largest runs and offers pruning and the `bulk` class's life, and history stops at its caps before it can stop mail (§24.10). A run and its continuations show as one conversation (§24.7). Moving a run into the person's enclave, from the run view or the bot tab's harness selector, calls `SidecarHarness.Continue`, which sends it only after a confirmation that names the run, the node, the enclave and its egress, whether any node it continues is flagged, and whether the run holds the person's mail, calendars, accounts or vault, so starting there with the `private` mark (§7.8, §24.7).

**Automatic approvals** (CO-40). Settings gain Approvals, from `AutoApprovals()`: the mode, `auto` or `ask`, for every kind and per kind, the network's limit beside each, `approvals:auto`'s text and today's count. The bot tab shows each automatic approval in its run as a note, "approved automatically by this device's check", with the disclosure's line, never with the person's name, and a card the check sent to the person says so; a notification on each day with automatic approvals opens the digest, each entry opening the action, its verdict and the inputs it read, with Undo where the action has one and "Ask me for these" (§27.9). The apps run the classifier behind `SetSafetyClassifierHost`, on a reduced ONNX Runtime (§27.5).

### 15.5 Decisions proposed

**D-CSURF-1 (proposed).** Disclosures are read and acknowledged on the person's own surfaces: `ur disclosures` and `ur disclosures ack <id>` on /dev/tty, the sdk's `Disclosures()` and `AckDisclosure(id)` from the app's UI, the bot tab's model picker, the enclave screen and settings; MCP and the gateway only refuse with `disclosure_required`, naming the fix. *Why:* CO-33, CO-34; an acknowledgment is the person's act, which no tool, run or harness takes for them.

## 16. Policy, budgets and approvals

### 16.1 Purpose and scope

Who may run which model, spend how much, create which enclaves, and log in where; the outward actions compute adds; and the harness config's `models` key, which [owner decision 452](DESIGN.md#od-452) left for a later design.

### 16.2 Resources and actions

Added to DESIGN §8.4's table (acl.proto numbers new atoms and actions after the existing ones):

```text
resource                 actions; notes
model:<canonical name>   infer: run a remote model; a glob within the name (model:chutes-*), never read as a label, since a
                         name's words promise nothing: a rule meaning TEE only sets assurance_floor (§16.4);
                         local models need no grant (CO-9: free, on the device)
compute:enclave          create, admin (stop or delete another subject's enclave; a start is its sponsor's,
                         or for the indexer enclave any Owner's or Admin's, §11.4); a rule may name shapes
compute:buy              buy credits, redeem promotion codes and set auto-renew, beside the Owner and Billing admin roles
compute:search           query: run a web search (§21); every member device and its agents by default
a subject (an enclave)   ssh, with users ["agent", "root", "edit"] and an optional check period; the dst is usually
                         tag:enclave or tag:enclave-<id>, which ur and the apps fill in from the name
listener:<selector>      dial: each listed socket and map entry of the subjects the selector names (*, tag:,
                         group:, user:, sidecar:, autogroup:), at their overlay addresses; an ip field narrows the
                         ports (§26.7)
```

### 16.4 Budgets, models and the floor

In the ACL document (DESIGN §8.5), a `compute` block the config's writers sign:

```json
{"compute": {
  "assurance_floor": "none",
  "providers": ["*"],
  "enclave_assurance_floor": "AP",
  "budgets": [
    {"subjects": ["autogroup:tagged"], "per": "subject", "day_usd": 5, "month_usd": 50},
    {"subjects": ["group:interns"], "per": "member", "month_usd": 100}],
  "enclave_shapes": ["cpu-2", "cpu-4", "cpu-8"],
  "search": {"enabled": true, "modes": ["fast", "turbo", "basic", "advanced"], "day_max": 2000},
  "fetch": {"enabled": true, "egress": "auto"},
  "calendar": {"enabled": true, "egress": "auto"},
  "connect": {"enabled": true, "services": ["*"], "generic": true, "custom": true, "egress": "auto"},
  "approvals": {"auto": ["fetch_unlisted_url", "tainted_send", "calendar_write", "service_write"]}
}}
```

`assurance_floor` is the lowest label remote inference may use: `none` (every model, CO-18's default), `AP`, `A1` or `A2`; `providers` names the remote inference providers allowed, `*` for all; a local model passes both, and the person's `tee_only`, since nothing leaves the device (CO-9, §6.3). Both go into the projection, so the broker refuses below them as the device does. Budget amounts and subjects go into the signed id-only projection, so the broker enforces them (compute-6); a budget is per subject, per agent, per member or per network, per day or month. Whatever the document says, the broker applies defaults (16.5) per untagged device and per agent id, the agent id riding every call's header (§6.6), and a ceiling per untagged device across all its agents and calls, $50 a day by default (CO-41, Q-CACL-4), counted by the calls' sidecar in the broker's budget counters (§14.4), since an agent id is the device's own word and a process that mints new ones would otherwise pass each agent's $5 again and again; so no local grant, harness or process spends past them without a `compute_budget_raise` a person approves, or a policy that raises them. The device also enforces budgets before it asks (the router, the gateway's grants), so most refusals never reach the server. `calendar` turns §23's calendar tools on or off for the network's agents, and with them the calendar's paths in `service_call` (§25.10), and sets their egress, `auto`, `exits` or `direct` (§23.7, Q-CONN-16). `connect` turns §25's connections on or off for the network's agents, names the services members may connect (`*` for every one the policy lists), and says whether `service_call` is offered (`generic`), whether members may add their own definitions on desktops (`custom`), and the egress, `auto`, `exits` or `direct` (§25.8, Q-CONN-16); it only narrows, and never lets an admin read a member's connection. No admin or Team audit reader opens a member's tokens or calendar secrets, which are sealed to the member's own devices (§25.6). `disclosures` holds the network's acknowledgments for its tagged and cloud sidecars, each an Owner's or Admin's signed `disclosure-ack` statement by id (§2.8, CO-41); it stays out of the projection, since the broker checks no acknowledgment (Q-CTRUST-2). A network with no document keeps its `compute` block alone, a config record its writers sign as they sign a document, which sets no reach, so the network stays under the implicit document (DESIGN §8.5). `approvals` names the kinds the safety classifier may decide in the network's tainted runs (§27.10), all four by default, `[]` sending every such approval to a person; it only narrows.

In the member's harness config (`harness/config.json`, DESIGN §16.7), the `models` key, which acts from M11:

```json
{"models": {
  "default": "local-gemma-4-e4b-off",
  "allow": ["local-*", "chutes-*"],
  "tee_only": false,
  "sign_in_mail": "withhold",
  "harness": {"codex": {"model": "chutes-<model>-tee-high"},
              "claude-code": {"opus": "chutes-<model>-tee-high", "sonnet": "chutes-<model>-tee-medium", "haiku": "local-gemma-4-e4b-off"}},
  "agents": {"<label>": {"default": "…"}}
}}
```

`tee_only` is the person's own floor of AP. It narrows, never widens, what the policy grants; the gateway renders it into each harness's settings (§8.8). `sign_in_mail`, `withhold` by default, keeps sign-in mail's codes and links from every model outside the device and A1 or A2 TEEs, and `allow` lets them go where the run's model goes (§23.4). The person writes the `models` key only by their own act, `ur models set` on /dev/tty or `Models().SetSettings` in an app's UI, such as the TEE-only switch beside the picker (Q-CACL-3); no tool or MCP call writes it (DESIGN §16.6). Beside `models`, the key `compute.disclosures`, `{"<id>": <version>}`, holds the disclosures the person has acknowledged (§2.8), which only their own act writes, never MCP (DESIGN §16.6 refuses its writes to the vault's `harness/` path); a model labeled `none` is called only once its provider's disclosure is acknowledged there, or on a tagged or cloud sidecar in the network's `disclosures` above, mail read or not (§23.5). Beside them, the key `approvals`, `{"mode": "auto", "kinds": {"<kind>": "ask"}}`, holds the person's automatic-approval setting, `auto` when absent (CO-40), which only their own act writes (§27.10).

### 16.5 Defaults

The implicit document (DESIGN §8.5) gains:

| Rule | Personal networks | Team networks |
|---|---|---|
| `model:*` infer | every member device and its agents | the same, under the Team's budgets |
| Budgets the broker enforces by default | per agent id (in-daemon agents, gateway harnesses, Harness agents) and per tagged subject: $5 a day, $50 a month; per untagged device, for calls naming no agent: $20 a day, $200 a month; per untagged device across all its agents and calls: $50 a day (CO-41) | the same unless the policy says otherwise |
| `compute:enclave` create | the owner's untagged devices, each create an outward action | members' untagged devices, each create an outward action |
| `ssh` | the sponsor's untagged devices to its enclaves as `agent`, `edit` and `root`, `root` only after the person's confirmation and `edit` refused to agents and to a harness's process (§12.9), by `ur ssh`, `ur enclave ssh` or `ur ssh agent` alike (§12.8, §12.9); the sponsor's agents as `agent`, which lands in the agents' container as its root (§11.10); no one to the indexer enclave (§11.10) | the same; another member only by a requested grant the sponsor's consented device approves (`autogroup:dst-owner`, DESIGN §8.8), never by an admin's rule alone and never as `root` (CO-43, §12.5), that member's prompts, steers and stops spending the sponsor's budget (Q-HARN-9) |
| `compute:buy` | the owner | Owner and Billing admin |
| `compute:search` query | every member device and its agents, under their budgets (Q-SRCH-4) | the same |
| Web fetch | every member device and its agents, through `auto` egress (Q-FETCH-2) | the same |
| Listeners (§26) | the person's devices already reach every listed entry (DESIGN's allow-all, owner decision 120); the listeners rule, `autogroup:tagged` to `listener:*`, adds their tagged sidecars and enclaves once the Owner has acknowledged `listeners:publish` for the network (§26.6) | the starting document's listeners rule, every client to `listener:*`; an existing document only by an admin's save (Q-LSTN-8); tagged sidecars' entries once an Owner or Admin has acknowledged it for the network (§26.6) |
| Calendar links and tools | each member's own links, read by their consented devices, their agents' enclaves among them (CO-43); the tools for their devices' local agents, their enclaves' agents and MCP sessions, through `auto` egress (§23) | the same; a Team's policy may turn the tools off or set `exits` |
| Connections and their tools | each member's own connections, made by their consented devices and read by them and their agents' enclaves (CO-42, CO-43); the tools for their devices' local agents, their enclaves' agents and MCP sessions, `service_call` included; their own definitions on desktops; through `auto` egress (§25) | the same; a Team's policy may narrow the services, turn off `service_call` or members' own definitions, or set `exits` |
| Automatic approvals (§27) | `auto` for kinds 23-26 in their tainted cases, acting once the person has acknowledged `approvals:auto` (CO-40) | the same; a Team's policy may narrow the kinds or force `ask` |
| `deposit` into `agent` repos (§20.4) | every admitted sidecar | `autogroup:member`, members' devices and the agents on them, a member's agents' enclave among their devices (CO-43); another tagged subject (a server, a CI runner, a cloud agent) only where a rule names it (Q-HARN-9); a policy may narrow it per agent; another member's message wakes no agent unasked (§20.7) |
| `tag:enclave`, `tag:enclave-*` owners (tagOwners) | `autogroup:member`, so a member's consented device admits the enclaves it sponsors, each `tag:enclave-<id>` claimed by the first admission under it, for its sponsor or, for the indexer enclave, the Owners and Admins, readers refusing anyone else's (§11.4) | the same |
| Assurance floors | inference: `none`, every label and provider (CO-18), which a network or a person may raise to AP, A1 or A2 or narrow to named providers; enclaves: AP (Q-PROV-2), a network may raise it | the same |

### 16.6 Enforcement points

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| The router and the gateway (device) | model allowed, budget left, assurance floor, attestation (§5) |
| `Sidecar.Authorize` (device) | 16.3's kinds |
| The safety classifier (device; an enclave's daemon) | `auto_ok` and the verdict for taint-driven approvals of kinds 23-26 (§27.9) |
| The connection client (device) | a connection's hosts, scopes and typed paths, and `service_call`'s classes (§25.8, §25.10) |
| The broker (server) | the projection's model and search rules, budgets and floors; holds; search rates |
| The enclave's SSH server | the `ssh` rule (§12.5) |
| The enclave daemon | the `private` mark and its crossings (§7.8); the sponsor's settings and harness config, taken only from their devices that are no enclave (§11.4) |
| The receiving Harness | attach-link origins (§7.10), outside the agents' container |
| An enclave's daemon | the container socket's calls as a tainted run's; the inbox refusal; the hold on a tainted run's EVS versions from its container until their release (§11.10, §20.4, §7.8) |
| EVS | inbox deposits and agent repo writes, as any write (§20.4) |
| The member's devices, reading | each card, status and summary path held to its agent's sidecar, and a tagged sidecar's version outside its own agents' paths ignored and alarmed (§20.4); an enclave's version of its sponsor's harness config or `enclaves/` settings ignored and alarmed (§11.4) |
| The Harness (device and enclave) | taint, the bundled git's fetches and every enclave-profile tool that touches the agents' container among its triggers, and the `private` mark (§7.8); wakes per agent and per sender, another member's message waiting for a person's turn (§20.7) |
| The host's hook (device) | the listeners rule against the host's listed set, less what discovery removed; `Deliver` through `ur tun` or a non-loopback address, never `127.0.0.1`; the implicit document's rule only while the network's acknowledgment of `listeners:publish` stands (§26.7) |

### 16.7 Decisions proposed

**D-CACL-1 (proposed).** `model:`, `compute:enclave`, `compute:buy`, `compute:search` and the `ssh` action, as 16.2. *Why:* §16's questions need resources to name.

**D-CACL-2 (proposed).** Outward kinds 19-26. *Why:* creating and removing machines (whose admission and removal no tool may do alone, DESIGN §16.6), leaving through a miner, passing a budget, fetching a URL a tainted run composed, a tainted run's sending into an enclave that reaches the internet or to another member, and a calendar write from a tainted run or to an event with attendees, whom its provider mails, and a connected service's write or send from a tainted run (CO-40), are outward; ordinary spending is budgeted, not approved per call.

**D-CACL-3 (proposed).** The `models` key acts from M11 and only narrows. *Why:* [owner decision 452](DESIGN.md#od-452) left it for this design; a config key that widened a policy would be an admin path.

**D-CACL-4 (proposed).** A network's `assurance_floor` (default `none`) and `providers`, and a person's `tee_only` and `allow`, choose which inference may run; the device enforces all four, and the broker the network's two, which the projection carries, since a person's live in their sealed harness config; an enclave enforces its sponsor's, which it reads from the vault as their other devices do (§11.4). *Why:* CO-18; CO-43.

**D-CACL-5 (proposed).** Kinds 19-24 are built at `CanonicalAction` version 5, with fields 42-49 beside DESIGN's, what a gate does not see sealed, and an effect lookup each (16.3); kind 24 binds the whole of what it sends by `body_sha256` and shows it as untrusted text. *Why:* DESIGN §16.8 refuses a kind until its fields are named and §5.4 one without a lookup; an approval must bind what leaves.

**D-CACL-6 (proposed).** Beside each agent's budget, the broker enforces a ceiling per untagged device across all its agents and calls, $50 a day by default, counted by the calls' sidecar, which the policy or `compute_budget_raise` raises. *Why:* CO-41 (Q-CACL-4); an agent id is the device's own word, so per-agent budgets alone do not bound a process that mints new ones, and §16.4's promise that no local process spends past the defaults needs it.

### 16.8 Questions

**Q-CACL-1.** Is each remote inference call an outward action? *Options:* (a) yes; (b) no, budgets bound it. *Answer:* (b). A call per approval would make agents unusable; budgets, model rules and taint bound the risk, and the record holds every call. *Decider:* owner.

**Q-CACL-2.** Default budgets? *Answer:* $5 a day and $50 a month per agent and per tagged subject, $20 a day and $200 a month per untagged device for calls naming no agent, enforced by the broker and raised by policy or by `compute_budget_raise`. *Decider:* owner, confirmed (CO-35).

**Q-CACL-3.** What may a new network use? *Options:* (a) every provider and label, with TEE-only one setting away; (b) TEE-only until a person widens it. *Answer:* (a), as CO-18 says. Every model carries its label in the catalog and on every message, and the apps put the TEE-only switch beside the model picker. *Decider:* owner.

**Q-CACL-4.** Should an untagged device's spending have a daily ceiling across all its agents? Q-CACL-2's budgets bind each agent id, and its $20 a day only the calls that name no agent, so a same-user process that mints new agent ids can spend past $5 a day each, bounded only by the balance and auto-renew's limits. *Options:* (a) no, budgets per agent only, as CO-35 confirmed; (b) yes, $50 a day per untagged device across all its agents and calls by default, which the broker enforces by the calls' sidecar and policy or `compute_budget_raise` raises. *Answer:* (b). It keeps CO-35's per-agent figures and bounds what a prompt-injected or modified local process can spend in a day, which per-agent figures cannot, since an agent id is the device's own word. *Decider:* owner, confirmed (CO-41).

## 17. Abuse, safety and legal process

### 17.1 Purpose and scope

Compute adds two kinds of abuse DESIGN §21 does not cover: misuse of inference URnetwork cannot see, and misuse of machines URnetwork rents. This section says what URnetwork can and cannot do about each, under end-to-end encryption.

### 17.2 What URnetwork can see and do

URnetwork sees compute-1 to compute-11 (§14.6): who used which model or enclave, when, how much, and paid how. It cannot see prompts, outputs, enclave files or commands, and builds no way to (the directive). So its controls work on accounts, volumes, payments and network behavior, never content:

| Vector | Control | Residual |
|---|---|---|
| Stolen cards buying compute, or cashing it out through searches (CO-29) | §9.11's limits per network and per payer, Radar, 3-D Secure, the enclave gates; for searches, the policy's ceiling, the network's budgets, daily cap and rate, the broker's search cap, which no policy raises, and search volume by network, a new network spending its search cap day after day flagged for review (§21.10) | chargebacks within the limits, about $167 of USDC per stolen card in its first week (§10.8) |
| Mining in enclaves | prohibited by the terms; new-account and GPU gates (§9.11); provider complaints act on the enclave | until a complaint |
| Creating enclaves that never run, so URnetwork pays the provider for their start | the first 10 minutes held at `requested`; a timeout for each state before `running`; VMs on their way counted against the enclave limits, and failed tries capped per network per day (§11.6, §11.13) | a few failed VMs a day per network |
| Scanning, attacks or spam from enclaves | port 25 refused (§11.8); `auto` egress leaves through URnetwork's network, so DESIGN §21.7's network reputation and probation apply; `exits` through the customer's own exits; `direct` only by an outward action, and provider complaints about a miner's address stop that enclave | traffic within the limits until reported |
| Harmful content from inference | the providers' acceptable-use terms, which bind URnetwork for its users (Chutes makes the integrator liable); per-network rate limits; report intake (DESIGN §21.8) acting on accounts | content URnetwork cannot read |
| Abuse that a provider without a TEE sees in content | that provider's own terms; per-network limits; a report naming a time and token counts leads to the network and agent that made the call, since compute-1 keeps each direct call's minute and usage (§14.6) | content URnetwork cannot read |
| A device naming one model and buying another on the direct path | the receipt's model checked against the declared entry, the served model charged, and a second mismatch in 30 days refusing the network's direct calls (§6.6, §9.11) | one round of lies, charged in full, leaving the network at most $5 below its floor (§9.7) |
| One user's abuse suspending URnetwork's provider account | E6's notice clause (§4.3); per-network limits; fast suspension of the offending network's compute | a provider acting without notice |
| Sanctioned users | Stripe's screening; compute refused by region at the broker from the request's address, checked and never logged (I-13); search payees screened before signing, and authorizations settled outside the facilitator recorded (§21.5) | VPN users, as anywhere; a fresh payee's later dealings |
| Scraping or reselling Parallel through URnetwork, harmful searches, or authorizations cashed out | no Parallel-shaped API: the tool, `ur search` and MCP only, each budgeted, capped and rate-limited per network (§21.9); the compute terms' web search clause carries Parallel's terms and forbids using an authorization outside URnetwork's tools (§21.11); a modified client can direct authorizations to an address of its own, never a listed one, which the ceiling, budgets, rates and the broker's search cap bound (CO-29, §21.5, §9.11); report intake acting on accounts | searches within the limits; queries URnetwork cannot read; cash-outs within the budgets (CO-29) |
| Fetches used to scrape or probe through exits | per-agent and per-device rates (§22.4); `ur-fetch`'s `User-Agent` with a contact page; DESIGN §21.7's egress reputation controls | fetches within the rates |

### 17.3 Legal process

A demand for compute content gets what URnetwork has: compute-1 to compute-11 and payment records, under DESIGN §21.9's process. Enclaves hold their own keys and are ephemeral; URnetwork can stop or remove one (a takedown) but cannot image its memory or disk, which the TEE and dm-crypt protect from URnetwork as from the miner. A demand for web searches gets compute-10 and compute-11, never a query, which URnetwork's servers never hold (§21.10). The transparency report counts compute requests apart.

### 17.4 Decisions proposed

**D-CABUSE-1 (proposed).** Compute abuse is handled on accounts, volumes, payments and network behavior, never content. *Why:* the directive.

**D-CABUSE-2 (proposed).** Mining, scanning and spam are prohibited in the compute terms, with suspension of the network's compute. *Why:* the providers' terms make URnetwork answerable.

## 19. Phasing and milestones

Milestones name scope; 19.3 sets the order it is built in, so that what a person can use with no outside party's act comes first and nothing is built for a provider before it commits in writing (D-CPHASE-1, D-CPHASE-2). 19.4 gives the effort and the teams, 19.6 what each use case waits on and whom, 19.7 where each item once proposed for deferral is built (CO-42), and what is kept, and 19.8 how the outside facts are kept current.

### 19.1 Milestones

After M10's exit, on the same `sidecar` branches (DESIGN §23.4), with the same entry and exit reviews, each entry also re-checking the outside facts its scope builds on (19.8). M12 and M13 come in two parts each: part a needs nothing new from another company, part b holds what waits on one, and each part has its own exit, so no exit waits on another company. The rows run in 19.3's build order:

### 19.3 Build order, and what reaches people

The milestones are built in this order (D-CPHASE-1). What a person can use with no outside party's act ships first; no adapter is built for a provider before it commits in writing to its gate's asks (D-CPHASE-2); and each provider's work starts when its commitment arrives, beside the rest. The tracks of 19.4 run the steps side by side where their inputs allow.

1. **Before M11's entry.** URnetwork sends its asks in writing and keeps each date in 19.6: engy's and SayGM's gate features (§4.7); gamma on SN64 and E6's agreement from Chutes; an EPC-1 form, EPC-2 and terms from Hippius, Cathedral and Lium (§11.3); and a notice to Parallel of the payer address and the volume expected, a notice and not an agreement (D-CPHASE-9). Google's verification and Microsoft's publisher verification are filed, since their reviews take weeks (19.2).
2. **From M10's exit: M11, M12a and the listeners track.** M11 is the Harness on local models, free, with the recURd skill and agent threads, and every run's context history kept in EVS, to continue on any of the person's devices. M12a builds §2.8's acknowledgment flow first, since the listeners and the classifier ask through it; then the compute balance, its Stripe and store products built and reviewed but closed until something can spend credit (Q-BAL-13); and the gateway, which puts local models behind one entry for Codex. The listeners track brings every device's listeners and forwarded ports to the apps and `ur listeners` (§26), and needs only the bridge, EVS and the ACL.
3. **From M11's midpoint: M13a.** Git on EVS, three-way merge included (stash, tag and grep follow in M14, §13.13), web fetch, mail summaries and CalDAV and ICS calendars, and tainted runs' fetches and calendar writes approved automatically by the device's safety classifier, on by default once the person has read `approvals:auto` (§27). **The first release** is M11, M13a, the listeners track and Codex on local models through M12a's gateway: everything in it is free and waits on no other company, its calendar links after the credential store's security review (19.2).
4. **M13b, on M12a's broker.** Claude Code through the gateway, Team agents, connected services with CO-40's clean-run calls, and web search, whose signer is built only after G-SRCH-parallel's load test passes (D-CPHASE-9). **Reaches people:** a person's own OIDC services on desktops at once (CO-41); web search after G-SRCH-parallel, and with it the compute balance, whose purchase sheets open with the first service that can spend credit (Q-BAL-13); Google's and Microsoft's calendars and connections after G-CONN-google and G-CONN-microsoft, and every calendar link and connection after the credential store's security review; and service writes approved automatically where §27 allows.
5. **M12b, once engy commits in writing.** A short paid trial against engy's live service first (D-CPHASE-4); then the direct path, engy's adapter, §10's treasury jobs and G-GAMMA-treasury's account and first mint; SayGM's adapter once SayGM commits to its two features. **Reaches people:** engy's models after G-PROV-engy and G-GAMMA-treasury, then SayGM's after G-PROV-saygm; if no inference provider has passed by then, the compute balance has opened with web search alone.
6. **M14's platform, from M11's midpoint, before any provider.** The image, PiG pinned in it, and its measurement pipeline, §5's CPU verifier, the SSH client and server, the orchestrator, the agents' container and the attach link, built and tested on the reference provider, its self-hosted SEV-SNP host included (§11.3; Q-CPHASE-3). **Then, once a provider commits in writing to an EPC-1 form:** its VM lifetimes and restarts measured (D-CPHASE-4), its adapter, the provisioning form it offers, the indexer enclave and attach's management mode. **Reaches people:** after G-PROV-hippius or G-PROV-cathedral, CPU enclaves, the network's indexer enclave among them where §11.10 allows, and the local Harness managing the enclaves' Harnesses (CO-23), its prompts into them approved automatically where §27 allows.
7. **M15, at its gates.** The Chutes path once SN64 takes gamma and Chutes signs E6's agreement (D-CPHASE-3); GPU enclaves once Lium commits; beacon nonces, the local GPU verifier, custody lists and A2. **Reaches people:** TEE inference after G-PROV-chutes; GPU enclaves after G-PROV-lium.
8. **M16,** the follow-up audit, once what it audits has shipped.

A provider that declines in writing, or has not answered when its work would start, gets no adapter, and the owner hears, since CO-28 names the providers and only the owner replaces one (Q-CPHASE-1).

Beside the tracks: one person for provider relations, who sends the asks, keeps their dates in 19.6 and brings back written commitments and terms; a security lead, who commissions 19.2's external audits and the reviews of G-SRCH-parallel, G-CONN and the credential store; counsel and an accountant, for 19.2's readings; the apps' engineers on each platform, for §15.4's seams (owner rule 6); and, from M12a's exit, an operations rota for policy signing, the treasury's runs, the 90-day re-checks, each harness release's conformance run and the provider canary. At its peak the build needs 13 to 14 engineers, about four times DESIGN's M10 team. The items of 19.7 add no track and no engineer: their 3 to 4.5 engineer-months fall across the five tracks, at most about one and a half on any one, so the critical paths below keep their ranges, each moving by a week or two at most. With fewer, 19.3's order holds, the tracks run one after another in it, and every date moves, the owner hearing at each entry review, as DESIGN §23.5 has it.

**Critical paths**, by inference with the tracks above:

- **The first release**, everything free: M11's loop and tool plumbing, then M13a's tools and classifier, the listeners track beside them; about 6 to 8 months after M10's exit.
- **The first paid service, web search**: M12a's ledger, broker and store products, then M13b's `searchsigner` after G-SRCH-parallel's load test, then the gate's counsel and outside review; about 8 to 10 months, and it opens the compute balance (Q-BAL-13).
- **Remote models**: engy's written commitment, then the paid trial, M12b, the direct path's audit and G-GAMMA-treasury; about 3 to 4 months after engy commits.
- **Enclaves**: a provider's written commitment to an EPC-1 form, then its adapter and that form's provisioning on M14's platform, then the external audit; about 3 to 5 months after the commitment, the platform ready by then.

### 19.5 Later

Anonymous metering for remote calls; a credential-injecting egress proxy in enclaves; the browser Harness; embeddings; Gemini's API in the gateway; stored responses; persistent enclave volumes; a narrower agents' enclave, per-repo or per-connection shares in place of its sponsor's whole access, which CO-43 gives it for the initial version (§11.4); an SSH server on desktops; recorded person sessions; cross-network agent messages; a Team-wide agents repo; x402 or other rails funding compute; GPU enclaves serving models to their network; SSH host certificates carrying attestation; SEAT-style attested TLS where providers offer it; web search's batched payments, per-device tokens and zero data retention, when Parallel offers them; web fetch's PDFs and a headless browser in enclaves; for mail and calendars, attachments an agent opens, a `mail_flag` tool, scheduled digests, replies to invitations and tasks (§23); for connected services, typed tools beyond the calendar, a person's own definitions in the apps, a Team's definitions, an OAuth grant of an enclave's own (Q-CONN-17) and providers' remote MCP servers as services (§25); for listeners, eBPF-driven discovery on Linux, the hosts behind a subnet route, and the names a host's services announce over DNS-SD (§26); for automatic approvals, an alignment stage and DESIGN's own kinds (§27); a verbatim relay that carries the person's own last message into an enclave under the person's origin, so a bot that has read a report need not ask again (§7.10).

So the first release gives a person every use case that costs nothing and none that spends credit. The first paid service, web search, waits only on URnetwork's own gate. Every remote model, TEE inference and every enclave wait on a company that has not yet built what its gate asks.

So what this document says of an outside party is informative, as of its date, and what URnetwork requires of a party (E1-E7, N1-N5, EPC-1 to EPC-9, §21.3's open items) is normative.
