| D-HARN-11 | §7 | The bundled `git`'s `clone`, `fetch` and `pull`, and any command that fetches an object lazily, taint the run before the worktree is written or the command answers when a push they take objects from shows a tainted run, a tagged sidecar other than the member's own enclave or another member, or no provenance they can read; in the enclave profile every tool that reads or runs in the agents' container taints its run as it starts, the file tools included, so every push from the container is a tainted run's. |
| D-HARN-12 | §7 | An enclave whose egress is not `none` keeps from its agents' container, and from every run there without the `private` mark, every EVS version whose provenance shows a tainted run, or none its daemon can read, other than pushes from the containers of the member's enclaves that reach out by runs without that mark, until its sponsor releases it by kind 24, built on the sponsor's device from the versions it reads; an enclave whose egress is `none` counts as reaching out where a rule lets it dial another device's services. |
| D-HARN-13 | §7 | In the local profile the file tools refuse every `.git` path component, in every spelling git itself refuses, and the bundled git writes a worktree's config with no command, alias, include, filter or hook. |
| D-HARN-14 | §7 | In an enclave that reaches out, a run holds the sponsor's private data or the agents' container, not both: reading mail, calendars, connected services, the mailbox, a vault file or a marked node gives a run the `private` mark, which it never loses, which follows the work as taint does and which its session entries carry; a marked run calls no tool that runs in or reads the container, and a run that has called one makes no such read and takes in no marked run's work, each crossing waiting for the person's kind 24, never the classifier's; a marked run works under the local profile's rules. |
| D-GW-1 | §8 | Three API fronts (Responses, Chat Completions, Messages) over one router; Gemini later. |
| D-GW-2 | §8 | Stateless to its callers: no response is served from storage beyond D-GW-5's ten minutes, `store: true` and `previous_response_id` stay refused, and reasoning round-trips in a sealed blob the gateway alone opens; each call's request and response are recorded in the caller's run, sealed and deduplicated, and never read back to answer a call (§24.8). |
| D-GW-3 | §8 | Per-harness grants, hour-long tokens minted by the harness's own credential command, budgets per grant under server-enforced defaults per device and agent; while a grant exists the daemon's unit holds the port, and a token goes only to a port whose listener proves it is the daemon (8.4). |
| D-GW-4 | §8 | An empty balance is `insufficient_quota` (Responses, Chat Completions) and a 402 `billing_error` (Messages); a TEE that cannot be verified is a 503 `tee_unverified` naming the model, and nothing is retried elsewhere. |
| D-GW-5 | §8 | Every stream ends with a terminal event; an identical request joins the call in flight or, within 10 minutes of its end, is answered from its kept response, which is sealed in the daemon's state and outlives a restart, and a planned restart waits for calls in flight; requests take 32 MiB, overflow errors keep each API's words, and Claude Code's attribution block reaches no provider. |
| D-GW-6 | §8 | A gateway call that needs a disclosure the person has not acknowledged answers 403 `disclosure_required` before any provider is called, naming the id, its summary line and the fix, which the harness shows; the gateway never prompts, and `ur install-harness --gateway` asks on /dev/tty for the disclosures of the models it writes, or, on a tagged or cloud sidecar, names those the network has not acknowledged, an Owner's or Admin's acknowledgment for the network standing for the person's there. |
| D-BAL-1 | §9 | The compute balance is lots and charges in Postgres with a Redis projection and holds, settled every 2 s by `compute_settle`. |
| D-BAL-2 | §9 | A credit is one US dollar; balances, prices and charges are nano-USD. |
| D-BAL-3 | §9 | The provider's reported usage is what a request is charged; the device checks it and raises `charge_mismatch`. |
| D-BAL-4 | §9 | Enclaves are charged per second, written every 10 minutes, with the next 10 minutes held. |
| D-BAL-5 | §9 | Holds are each request's worst case, a direct call's its declared model's, against the balance and budgets alike; calls and searches hold down to zero and enclave intervals down to the floor (the smaller of $5 and an hour of the network's enclaves); and URnetwork carries a direct call's gap to its provider's costliest model up to $5 a network, under the exposure rule; so a network owes at most the floor, plus up to 72 hours of its indexer enclave's price in that enclave's grace (§9.9), and $5 more only where a device of its lied about a direct call's model. |
| D-BAL-6 | §9 | The spend view gives each service (remote inference, enclaves, web search, adjustments; web fetch and calendar calls at no charge) its total since the network's first charge and its last 7 UTC days, net of refunds, exact to the last settlement, from two rollups `compute_settle` writes with each charge: `compute_charge_day`, kept 400 days, and `compute_charge_total`, kept for the account's life with no day, sidecar or agent; the server answers ids and numbers, and the device names them. |
| D-BAL-7 | §9 | The person's own bot reads the spend view through `compute_spend` (R), in the Harness and over MCP, only on the person's consented device (untagged, neither ephemeral nor Delegation-admitted) and within the person's role, a label no signed source vouches for reaching the model only between untrusted-data markers (9.13); agents on tagged sidecars and in enclaves read none, and no agent reads charge rows, lots or payment methods. |
| D-BAL-8 | §9 | The apps report store purchases through `api`'s existing verify routes (`Compute().StorePurchase`), each bound to its network by the purchase's account token, or as Pro's are where it names none, and credited once by its transaction or order id, whichever of the app's report and the store's notification comes first, a plan change granting only the difference (9.5); `insufficient_quota` names whether the balance or a budget ran out, and the Harness offers "add credit" to a person who may buy and "raise the budget" as kind 21 (the `compute_budget_raise` tool, `ur compute budget raise`, `Compute().RaiseBudget`); credits go on sale once something the network may use can spend them (Q-BAL-13). |
| D-BAL-9 | §9 | Auto-renew and 9.9's states read the balance, settled less unsettled charges and running enclaves' accrued time, holds left out; admission alone reads `available`; a direct call has one hold per authorization, settled by the provider's three-state lookup, and a hold the lookup cannot answer stays pending and is never charged; a refused enclave interval is cut to what is left and its enclave stopped when it runs out. |
| D-BAL-10 | §9 | Purchase limits follow the payer as well as the network: a new payer, like a new network, buys at most $100 a day and $200 in its first 7 days, and every payer and network at most $1,500 a UTC day; and the broker caps a network's searches by the age of its paid credit, a cap no policy raises. |
| D-BAL-11 | §9 | Disputes count by network, at most 10 a network a day, and page a person, never changing the catalog by themselves; an hourly canary of known token counts checks each provider's usage and bill. |
| D-BAL-12 | §9 | Promotion codes are URnetwork's, made by an operator with a value of at most $10, a cap on redemptions and a last day, a code with a cap above one asking for an unreversed paid lot; only a person who may buy redeems one, on the compute screen or with `ur compute redeem`, never an agent, MCP, a tagged sidecar or an enclave; a network redeems a code once and one code in 30 days; its value counts as a load with the day's purchases against the daily load limit and the balance cap; and its lot, drawn first, pays for inference and enclaves, never web search, and lapses 30 days after redemption. |
| D-GAMMA-1 | §10 | One API-key hotkey and deposit per provider and environment, the hotkey in a rate-limited signer on the broker's hosts, the deposit owned by a compute mint coldkey with a float of at most 7 days, behind a multisig reserve. |
| D-GAMMA-2 | §10 | Mint and spend just in time: 1 to 2 days of gamma in each deposit, 1.5 to 3 days at each provider. |
| D-GAMMA-3 | §10 | Reconcile charges, provider bills and on-chain spends daily per provider. |
| D-GAMMA-4 | §10 | Users never touch gamma; the balance stays a closed loop. |
| D-GAMMA-5 | §10 | A provider's forecast is the largest of its trailing mean, the committed rate of the enclaves running on it plus its inference, and a floor set at its gate; the broker refuses a new call or enclave the provider's account cannot cover (`capacity`); reconciliation reports each provider's realized margin weekly. |
| D-ENC-1 | §11 | An enclave is a named line of incarnations; each is a tagged, sponsored sidecar whose keys are made in its VM and bound in its evidence, admitted by the verifying person's device, an agents' enclave's as one of its sponsor's devices (D-ENC-16), and revoked at its stop. |
| D-ENC-2 | §11 | The enclave platform contract, EPC-1 above all, gates every enclave provider; the reference provider serves development, CI and staging only, the production policy and catalog listing none of its profiles or shapes, and until a provider passes no user is offered an enclave. |
| D-ENC-3 | §11 | Default egress on, mode `auto` unless the network's policy for `tag:enclave` says otherwise; `direct` only by an outward action. |
| D-ENC-4 | §11 | Scratch disk under dm-crypt and dm-integrity, work in EVS. |
| D-ENC-5 | §11 | A network may make one enclave its indexer, named by its enclave identity and followed across incarnations, in a role B and its evidence bind, set up by any of EPC-1's forms (CO-41), which runs no agents and admits no login; it takes the network's mail without reading mailboxes, and indexes a member's mailbox only by that member's grant, which its devices carry to each new incarnation. |
| D-ENC-6 | §11 | The agents' container holds only the agents' tool processes and the harnesses they run, no credential but hour-long gateway tokens, `ur` read-only and no API socket; its one container socket's every call is a tainted run's, and nothing in the enclave's namespaces accepts input from its veth but DNS. |
| D-ENC-7 | §11 | Each kind 19 shows its provider's disclosure line and waits for the sponsor's acknowledgment of that disclosure's current version, and step 6 accepts only the named provider's evidence; a member's mailbox grant waits for that member's own; a new version leaves running enclaves running. |
| D-ENC-8 | §11 | Each incarnation of the indexer enclave makes its own mail-host key and receives under a listen grant its enclave's tag holds, and each member's grant is the key `compute.indexer_grant` of their harness config, so a keeper restarts it with no key to hand over and the member's devices seat each new incarnation; at most one indexer enclave stands at network scope. |
| D-ENC-9 | §11 | Any network's indexer enclave may be set up over SSH: its sponsor's device signs a setup statement binding the incarnation's setup evidence, its keys, B and the payload's hash, and a member's device seats the incarnation as a mailbox reader only on that statement, after checking the provider image's evidence and the binding itself, and only from the member its grant accepted. |
| D-ENC-10 | §11 | Each create or start authorizes one VM, the device itself starting each retry under the same approval, at most 3; the states before `running` time out; their VMs count against the limits and their failures against a daily cap; the first 10 minutes are held at `requested`; any consented device of the sponsor resumes steps 2-9. |
| D-ENC-11 | §11 | An enclave's tag is `tag:enclave-<id>`, its name a label; the first admission under the tag claims it for the enclave's sponsor, or for the indexer enclave its Owners and Admins, and readers refuse anyone else's admission under it. |
| D-ENC-12 | §11 | The network's indexer enclave keeps 7 days of its price in a reserve only its own charges draw, then 72 hours of grace; its keeper restarts it alone on any machine its Where row allows, telling the Owners and Admins, at most two new machines a week; planned restarts make before they break; silence alone fails no enclave. |
| D-ENC-13 | §11 | EPC-9 asks every provider for kernel fixes within 14 days, each a new profile, and no incarnation outlives its profile; gVisor is evaluated for the agents' container. |
| D-ENC-14 | §11 | A start through a tool is a kind 19, a tainted run's `enclave_stop` waits for the person, and no tool stops, starts or removes the network's indexer enclave; each stop records its cause, and a keeper restarts only what the balance or a loss stopped. |
| D-ENC-15 | §11 | The indexer enclave is the network's own receiver on Q-ENC-10's conditions: every key made in it; no key, console, command or login into it for the provider's customer or URnetwork; the keys a device admits bound to the VM it checked, in every form; a machine the broker did not choose; and in a Team, reception only 24 hours after every member is told. |
| D-ENC-16 | §11 | For the initial version an agents' enclave's incarnation is one of its sponsor's devices: its admission, signed by an untagged consented device of the sponsor that verified its evidence, names the sponsor beside its tags with capability bit 3, so it is consented for the sponsor and reads and writes what their devices reach in EVS, their owner-bound repos, calendar links and connections included, while its network reach stays its tags'; it holds none of their authority (no admission, consent, share, suspension, revocation or key registration but its own, `IndexerSet`, config write or approval but its own runs' automatic decisions, and no version of their settings that another device takes); no `SponsorSet` moves it; its stop, loss or compromise revocation revokes it, every repo it read rotating away from it, as for any removed device; the network's indexer enclave stays a tagged sidecar outside this. |
| D-SSH-1 | §12 | The SSH protocol, on x/crypto/ssh v0.59.0 or later, with sidecar-registered keys, flow-principal cross-check and policy rules. |
| D-SSH-2 | §12 | Host keys from the config and the attestation; no trust on first use. |
| D-SSH-3 | §12 | Local forwarding to the enclave's loopback for people only; no remote or agent forwarding; sftp on. |
| D-SSH-4 | §12 | The server, outside the agents' container, verifies each attach link's signed origin (`origin@ur.io`, `SIGNED_ATTACH_ORIGIN`), records a use's effect key before it runs a command (`effect@ur.io`) and answers evidence requests as a global request; a session's sftp and forwards run in its own namespaces and as its user. |
| D-SSH-5 | §12 | A `root` login, by `ur ssh`, `ur enclave ssh`, `ur ssh agent` or the sdk's `OpenSsh`, is signed only after the person's confirmation on `/dev/tty`, in the app's UI or with a presence key, and `ur ssh` and `ur enclave ssh` refuse it to a caller with a harness process among its ancestors. |
| D-SSH-6 | §12 | `ur ssh config` warns that an editor's remote server trusts its machine and writes an `edit` target: a person-only container with the agents' files at `/agents`, which no agent process enters or writes, `edit` refused to agents' sessions and to a harness's `ur ssh`. |
| D-GIT-1 | §13 | A porcelain over sidecar's existing git codecs, writing git's on-disk layout with stock git's ignore, rename, mode and folding rules, talking only to EVS; a full clone, not a sparse one, opens in stock git. |
| D-GIT-2 | §13 | Lazy blob fetch and sparse checkout by prefix. |
| D-GIT-3 | §13 | One argv tool with a whitelist and explicit "not supported" answers. |
| D-CSRV-1 | §14 | One new service, `compute`, for the broker and orchestrator, and an internal one, `searchsigner`, for the search payer key; billing on api; jobs on taskworker. |
| D-CSRV-2 | §14 | compute-1 to compute-11 are the whole of what the servers keep. |
| D-CSURF-1 | §15 | Disclosures are read and acknowledged on the person's own surfaces: `ur disclosures` and `ur disclosures ack <id>` on /dev/tty, the sdk's `Disclosures()` and `AckDisclosure(id)` from the app's UI, the bot tab's model picker, the enclave screen and settings; MCP and the gateway only refuse with `disclosure_required`, naming the fix. |
| D-CACL-1 | §16 | `model:`, `compute:enclave`, `compute:buy`, `compute:search` and the `ssh` action, as 16.2. |
| D-CACL-2 | §16 | Outward kinds 19-26. |
| D-CACL-3 | §16 | The `models` key acts from M11 and only narrows. |
| D-CACL-4 | §16 | A network's `assurance_floor` (default `none`) and `providers`, and a person's `tee_only` and `allow`, choose which inference may run; the device enforces all four, and the broker the network's two, which the projection carries, since a person's live in their sealed harness config; an enclave enforces its sponsor's, which it reads from the vault as their other devices do (§11.4). |
| D-CACL-5 | §16 | Kinds 19-24 are built at `CanonicalAction` version 5, with fields 42-49 beside DESIGN's, what a gate does not see sealed, and an effect lookup each (16.3); kind 24 binds the whole of what it sends by `body_sha256` and shows it as untrusted text. |
| D-CACL-6 | §16 | Beside each agent's budget, the broker enforces a ceiling per untagged device across all its agents and calls, $50 a day by default, counted by the calls' sidecar, which the policy or `compute_budget_raise` raises. |
| D-CABUSE-1 | §17 | Compute abuse is handled on accounts, volumes, payments and network behavior, never content. |
| D-CABUSE-2 | §17 | Mining, scanning and spam are prohibited in the compute terms, with suspension of the network's compute. |
| D-CPHASE-1 | §19 | The milestones are built in 19.3's order: M11, M12a and the listeners track from M10's exit, then M13a, which no outside party holds, then M13b, then M12b, M14's provider work and M15 as their providers commit and their gates pass; M12 and M13 each come in two parts with separate exits, so no exit waits on another company. |
| D-CPHASE-2 | §19 | No provider's adapter is built before that provider commits in writing to its gate's asks; the asks go out before M11's entry, their dates and answers kept in 19.6, and a provider that declines is the owner's to replace (CO-28). |
| D-CPHASE-3 | §19 | The Chutes path, its adapter, the E2E client, §6.6's TEE path and GPU evidence through NRAS, moves to M15 and starts once SN64 takes gamma and Chutes signs E6's agreement; the policy pipeline stays in M12a, and the CPU verifier moves to M14, which needs it first. |
| D-CPHASE-4 | §19 | Before M12b's work, a short paid trial against engy's live service tests signed requests through exits, receipts, the usage lookup's states and its edge's behavior; before an enclave provider's adapter, VM lifetimes and restarts are measured on that provider. |
| D-CPHASE-5 | §19 | Five tracks, each a team, build M11 to M16 (19.4): the Harness, tools and connections, listeners, the compute service, and enclaves, with provider relations, security, counsel, an accountant, the apps' engineers and an operations rota beside them; listeners run as their own track from M10's exit. |
| D-CPHASE-6 | §19 | Nothing is deferred from launch: each item 19.7 lists, once proposed for deferral, is built in the milestone it names and counted in 19.4's effort, and the items 19.7 keeps stay because an owner statement or a use case needs them. |
| D-CPHASE-7 | §19 | 19.6's status table is kept current at each milestone's entry and each gate's check, with the date each outside party was asked and the date it committed. |
| D-CPHASE-8 | §19 | Each milestone's entry re-checks the outside facts its scope builds on (19.8), dated, recording a change in 19.6 and, where a disclosure states the fact, as a new version (§2.8); facts about outside parties are informative and dated, and what URnetwork requires of a party is normative. |
| D-CPHASE-9 | §19 | Web search's signer is built only after G-SRCH-parallel's load test passes; Parallel is told the payer address and the volume expected before users search, a notice and not an agreement; Tavily's keyless search over x402 is the named fallback (§21.15); and Parallel's failure rate comes from devices' outcome reports, kept only as hourly counts across all networks (§21.8). |
| D-SKILL-1 | §20 | Two new owner-bound kinds: `agents` (one per member per network, written only by the member's own devices and agents) and `agent` (one per agent, taking deposits). |
| D-SKILL-2 | §20 | Status is mechanical and versionless; summaries are the agent's, versioned. |
| D-SKILL-3 | §20 | Conversations are thread dirs in the recipient's inbox, replies in the same dir, and by deposit to the sender's own inbox only when the sender cannot read the recipient's repo. |
| D-SKILL-4 | §20 | A message leaves a run untainted only if its provenance shows the member's own person (input path, no run) or an untainted run on the member's untagged device or in their own enclave (CO-43); other members, their enclaves, cloud agents and the Team inbox always taint; readers check provenance against cards and paths. |
| D-SKILL-5 | §20 | In a Team, a Team inbox (`agents-team`, a general repo marked `inbox: team`) carries messages to every agent of the network. |
| D-SKILL-6 | §20 | An agent's summary and status text are trusted only on IC-12's terms; `agent_list` and `agent_find` give a model any other writer's text as stubs of identifier fields, and the text only with `untrusted: include`, which taints the run first. |
| D-SKILL-7 | §20 | Inboxes take messages only through `agent_send`, `agent_broadcast` and `agent_close`, the evs tools and `git` refusing writes under `inbox/`; and a message may name `reply_to`, the person's `me` for work the person asked for, so a report shows to the person without waking the bot. |
| D-SKILL-8 | §20 | An agent takes messages while its run is open in the Harness that hosts it; a desktop daemon keeps runs open past their views and does not idle out while one is; a message that lands while its agent's run is closed or its host is down is taken once when the run reopens, and `agent_send` answers the recipient's state meanwhile. |
| D-SKILL-9 | §20 | The person's `me` is the member's: one card across their devices, each watching the threads that name it. |
| D-SKILL-10 | §20 | An agents' enclave reads and writes its member's agents repo as one of their devices (CO-43), its agents reaching it as the member's other agents do, through the `agent_*` tools, `evs_*` and `git`, a tainted run's versions held from its container in an enclave that reaches out (§7.8); readers hold each card, status and summary path to its agent's sidecar, and ignore and alarm on a tagged sidecar's version anywhere but its own agents' paths and `inbox/`. |
| D-SKILL-11 | §20 | A message from outside the agent's member wakes no agent unless it answers a thread that agent opened, waiting for the next turn its person drives; one sending sidecar wakes an agent at most 5 times an hour; in a Team, deposits into `agent` repos default to members' devices and their agents, a member's agents' enclave among their devices (CO-43), another tagged subject only by a rule. |
| D-SRCH-1 | §21 | Web search is a built-in tool, `web_search`, backed by Parallel's Search through its keyless gateway, on every Harness leg, through MCP and as `ur search`; each search is a kind-6 charge on the compute balance under the inference budgets. |
| D-SRCH-2 | §21 | The device calls the gateway itself, through `auto` egress, and pays each search with an EIP-3009 authorization URnetwork's search signer signs for the device's own nonce, in a fixed window of at most 3 minutes, to the payee the gateway's challenge names, after the broker checks the asset, the policy's ceiling and the network's budgets, caps and rate, and the signer screens the payee; charges follow settlement on Base's finalized head, and the ticket joining broker and signer is dropped then; no URnetwork server reads or intercepts a query. |
| D-SRCH-3 | §21 | sidecar's client calls only the gateway's Search, over its x402 rail, with only its documented fields and fixed headers; never Task, Responses or Extract, nor the MPP rail. |
| D-SRCH-4 | §21 | Results are untrusted and taint the run they reach; the objective and queries are checked for secrets and personal data before they leave; a search is R, not outward. |
| D-SRCH-5 | §21 | The gateway serves no hosted search: `ur install-harness` sets Codex's `web_search = "disabled"` and denies Claude Code's `WebSearch`, and the gateway drops a hosted search tool from a Responses request and answers Claude Code's WebSearch request `unavailable`; harnesses search through the MCP `web_search`. |
| D-SRCH-6 | §21 | A search costs the authorization's value times the compute markup, $0.01 × 1.20 = $0.012 today in every mode, with no free allowance, charged on settlement, failed calls included. |
| D-SRCH-7 | §21 | Results are not stored: stubs in the record, memory only in the apps, no cache across calls or runs, and the skill's rule to cite rather than copy. |
| D-SRCH-8 | §21 | Search is the disclosure `search:parallel` (CO-33), its text in the signed policy saying what could be exposed and what stays private; each person acknowledges each version once, on an approval-capable device, never an agent or an RPC `ui_response`; until then `web_search` answers `disclosure_required` on every surface, and a run with no person attached stops. |
| D-SRCH-9 | §21 | Devices report each search's outcome class without content, with their next authorization or once a day; the broker keeps only hourly counts across all networks, whose failure rate pages and opens the owner's review of alternatives. |
| D-SRCH-10 | §21 | The compute terms gain a web search clause carrying Parallel's Customer Terms and AUP, accepted when a network turns search on; each network is the Customer and one End Customer. |
| D-SRCH-11 | §21 | Before signing, the signer screens each payee against the sanctions lists, and, once the gate shows the gateway's payees fresh, refuses any address with a past; an authorization is valid at most 3 minutes; one settled by any sender but the facilitator is kept with its network as a sanctions record and flagged; and the broker caps each network's searches a day by the age of its paid credit, a cap its policy cannot raise. |
| D-SRCH-12 | §21 | The payer key sits in `searchsigner`, apart from the broker: the broker admits and holds by network and never sees a payee or nonce, which the device seals to the signer; the signer never sees a network; the ticket joining them lives in memory only, with persistence off; per-search rows keep their minute 72 hours; and the signer keeps its issued nonces durably, read from two Base sources. |
| D-FETCH-1 | §22 | `web_fetch` is a core tool on every leg, extracting one page on the device into `FetchedPage` with no model. |
| D-FETCH-2 | §22 | Fetches leave through URnetwork's network (`auto`, or `exits` by policy), never directly from a device, their bytes counted as transfer, with no compute charge. |
| D-FETCH-3 | §22 | Listed URLs are R; a URL the agent composed in a tainted run is outward action 23, `fetch_unlisted_url`; once tainted, the person's own URLs stay listed and uncounted, and other unapproved fetches stop at 10 a turn the person drives. |
| D-FETCH-4 | §22 | Names resolved through the egress; public addresses only, by connect's own list plus the overlay and routed subnets, pinned and rechecked on redirect; ports 80, 443 and 1024 up; `GET` with no cookies or credentials; caps on size and time. |
| D-FETCH-5 | §22 | Results are untrusted and recorded, kept whole up to §24.5's part cap. |
| D-MAILCAL-1 | §23 | The local Harness reads mail with DESIGN's `mail_list` and `mail_read`, in process at R, each read of outside mail tainting the run before any of it reaches the model; `mail_read` gains `start` and `max_chars`, and an invitation's events parsed, never its bytes (Q-MAILCAL-14); no agent's read marks mail seen. |
| D-MAILCAL-2 | §23 | Mail and events go to the model the person picked, under the floors, each label saying who can read them; a model without a TEE reads them only once the person has acknowledged its provider's disclosure, which names them, as for any call to it (§2.8). |
| D-MAILCAL-3 | §23 | A calendar link is a `CalendarLink` record, versionless, one to an owner-bound `secret` repo with no label in the config, set only by a person on their own device and read only by sidecar's calendar tools, never by an agent (IC-18). |
| D-MAILCAL-4 | §23 | Four link forms: `caldav` with an app password, `ics` read-only, and `google` and `microsoft` through a connection (§25), by OAuth on the device: Microsoft's rotating refresh token written back at each refresh; Google's one refresh token per platform client, none kept on Android devices, which take access tokens from `AuthorizationClient`. |
| D-MAILCAL-5 | §23 | Calendar calls leave through the network's egress under §22.4's address rules, `https` only, one exit a link, recorded in it, or `direct` where the person or the policy chose it (Q-CONN-16), discovery kept within the registrable domain the person gave, and a private name the person typed reached over the overlay with a pinned certificate or, to a sidecar, plain `http`, at no compute charge. |
| D-MAILCAL-6 | §23 | `calendar_list` is R with an untrusted result; `calendar_add`, `calendar_update` and `calendar_delete` are W in an untainted Harness run and outward kind 25 in a tainted one, an MCP session's run counting as tainted (Q-CONN-14), and for any event with attendees, one approval to a call, each event shown whole as untrusted text and switchable. |
| D-MAILCAL-7 | §23 | The tools run in the local profile, through MCP, and in the person's own enclave as one of their devices, where a run that uses them takes the `private` mark and, in an enclave that reaches out, uses no tool of the agents' container but by the person's kind 24. |
| D-MAILCAL-8 | §23 | Records keep mail as references to its mailbox, which a rebuild re-renders and checks by hash, calendar reads whole, and every calendar write with its prior version for Undo; nothing records a link's secret. |
| D-MAILCAL-9 | §23 | Kind 25's action is `CanonicalAction` version 5, fields 50-53 with a repeated `CalendarEventAction` carrying each event whole, 54-59 reserved; `ApprovalDecision.selected`, field 14, lists the events approved, an empty list approving none. |
| D-MAILCAL-10 | §23 | Sign-in mail, a message in which the mail component finds a one-time code or a sign-in, password-reset, verification or magic link, reaches a model outside the device and A1 or A2 TEEs only withheld: the renderer keeps its sender, subject and time, puts "(withheld)" in place of its snippet and text and masks any repeat of its code or link, a continuation in an enclave renders it by its own model's label, and MCP returns it so, unless the person's `sign_in_mail` switch allows it. |
| D-CTXH-1 | §24 | Every Harness run keeps its whole context history in the author's vault: one `session_entry` per message of its session tree, large parts as `session_blob` entries referenced by SHA-256, and each `model_call` naming the messages it read and wrote and its request's hash. |
| D-CTXH-2 | §24 | Deduplication is the tree's, on the device and within a run: each message written once, calls naming it, the gateway matching requests by chain hash and repeated items by `same_as`; nothing is shared across runs or deduplicated on a server. |
| D-CTXH-3 | §24 | Parts are kept whole up to 64 MiB in 8 MiB blobs, §22.7's 64 KiB fetch cap lifted, under DESIGN §16.7's run-hour budget. |
| D-CTXH-4 | §24 | A call's context rebuilds from the record by the renderer it names and is checked against a request hash that covers each part by its own hash, so pruning leaves a call checkable; redactions and stubs mark where it differs from what was sent, and an erased node or pruned part reads as unverifiable, never as a fault. |
| D-CTXH-5 | §24 | A run resumes on its own device and continues or forks on any of the member's devices from the vault, their agents' enclaves among them (CO-43); into an enclave only by the person's act, `ur harness continue`, the app, or `harness_continue` after the person's confirmation or kind 24's approval, and on a new incarnation for the runs a lost one held open; a continuation takes its nodes' taint and `private` mark. |
| D-CTXH-6 | §24 | The gateway records every call's request and response whole, deduplicated against the run's earlier calls, and stays stateless to its callers (D-GW-2 as amended). |
| D-CTXH-7 | §24 | Web search results, matches of DESIGN §16.7's secret rules and `keep: false` details stay out in every form the daemon writes, the gateway's entries and ingested transcripts included. |
| D-CTXH-8 | §24 | History is kept until the person erases it; at 90% of the network's storage, or at a member's share of it, by default all of it for one member and 2/n for n, it stops leaving the device, its nodes waiting in the spool and its blobs kept by hash and size, while every call is still journaled first, so mail and repos keep writing; blobs take a retention class of their own, `bulk`, and the person sees and prunes runs by size, the warning offering one tap that expires the oldest blobs. |
| D-CTXH-9 | §24 | A node a tagged sidecar other than the member's own enclave wrote, or that the gateway recorded under a binding it inferred, is untrusted wherever a run takes it into its context or an agent reads it, and taints that run, since such a writer's taint bit is its own word. |
| D-CTXH-10 | §24 | Session entries sit under their own stream prefix, which a reader may defer while still verifying its writers' chains, and from M11 phones lease per-request approval notices and the inbox prefixes rather than the whole vault. |
| D-CTXH-11 | §24 | Kinds 54 and 55 keep DESIGN §16.7's secret rules but not `record.redact.pii`'s hashing, which applies where history leaves the member's devices otherwise: exports hash, and disclosure packets, which prove bodies by commitment, carry addresses and numbers as sealed, their confirmations counting them; a continued run searches again for results it needs. |
| D-CTXH-12 | §24 | Session entries ride in the pushes their calls' `model_call` entries make, or leave at a turn's end or after 60 s, never in a push of their own at each call; an agents' enclave writes them as any of the member's devices does (CO-43). |
| D-CONN-1 | §25 | Service definitions are signed in the compute policy's `services`, Google's and Microsoft's first, each naming its issuer and endpoint hosts, URnetwork's public client and redirect per platform, its features and their scopes, its API hosts and `service_call`'s rules; a service is added or narrowed by a policy update, never a release, and a token goes only to hosts that both the current definition and the connection's record list. |
| D-CONN-2 | §25 | Only a person connects, on their own approval-capable device, in the system browser, with PKCE S256, a single-use `state`, a `nonce` and the ID token's checks, RFC 9207's `iss` where the provider sends it and a redirect path per issuer: loopback on desktops, `ASWebAuthenticationSession` on iOS, `AuthorizationClient` for Google on Android and the Auth Tab's App Link otherwise; the code is redeemed through the egress and never reaches a URnetwork server. |
| D-CONN-3 | §25 | A connection is one `Connection` record in its own owner-bound `secret` repo, with no label in the config and a versionless `connection.json` holding every OAuth credential it has: its refresh tokens, per platform where the provider binds them to a client, and any client secret its client needs, each written before its first use; access tokens live in memory only. |
| D-CONN-4 | §25 | Google's tokens are kept per platform client (Desktop and iOS), and Android devices keep none, taking access tokens from `AuthorizationClient`; Microsoft's one token serves every device and is written back at each refresh; a strict provider's devices refresh under a lease in the repo; no device refreshes an idle connection. |
| D-CONN-5 | §25 | Agents use connections through typed tools, the calendar's first, and three generic tools: `connections_list` (R), `connection_request` (R, answered only by the person) and `service_call`, whose daemon attaches the token for one call to the connection's API hosts and returns no credential. |
| D-CONN-6 | §25 | `service_call`'s reads are R with untrusted results; its writes and sends are W in an untainted Harness run (CO-40), an MCP session's run counting as tainted for them (Q-CONN-14), and outward kind 26 `service_write` in a tainted one, where the safety classifier decides a write first in auto mode and a person every send and every call other than `GET` and `HEAD` the definition does not classify (§27); paths a typed tool owns, for every method and while the network has those tools off, push-notification, subscription and sharing endpoints, batch endpoints, hosts outside the connection and paths that are not canonical are refused, every rule matching the canonical path that is then sent. Kind 26 is `CanonicalAction` version 5 with fields 3, 5, 48 and 60, 61-69 reserved, its body shown whole as untrusted text up to 32 KiB and sent once. |
| D-CONN-7 | §25 | Calls leave through the network's egress under §22.4's rules, `https` only, with one exit per connection, recorded by its provider's client id, country and time, that every device of the member asks for by id, chosen in the device's country and changed only when it fails, each change counted; `direct` from the device's own address where the policy, the definition's gate or the person chose it (Q-CONN-16); the person's sign-in runs in their own browser outside the egress. |
| D-CONN-8 | §25 | Disconnecting revokes each token at the provider where it can (RFC 7009, Android's `revokeAccess()`) and deletes the repo and the calendar links that name it; where a provider cannot revoke one token (Microsoft), the app sends the person to remove the app; after any revocation of a device that could read a connection, the member's devices offer to replace it. |
| D-CONN-9 | §25 | The calendar's `google` and `microsoft` forms are connections with the `calendar` feature, and their gates become G-CONN-google and G-CONN-microsoft, one gate per service. |
| D-CONN-10 | §25 | A connected service's results reach a model without a TEE only after the person has acknowledged that provider's disclosure, as any context does (CO-34); a definition may set `limited_use`, as Google's does, under which a read marks the run, the mark follows its nodes, pushes, messages, children and continuations, and the router, `agent_launch`, `agent_send` and MCP give a marked run's context only to local models and to models of any label whose provider's gate recorded no training on, no keeping past the request and no person reading what they are sent. |
| D-CONN-11 | §25 | No connection, token or `service_call` in tagged sidecars, but in the person's own enclave, one of their devices (CO-42, CO-43), whose daemon reads the connection and attaches its token outside the agents' container, a run that uses it taking the `private` mark (§7.8); MCP gets `connections_list` and `service_call` under the same tiers, its writes and sends as a tainted run's (Q-CONN-14), and no `connection_request`. |
| D-CONN-12 | §25 | A connection another platform made becomes usable on a device through Use on this device: a desktop or an iPhone adds its platform's token to the same record by the person's sign-in with the record's account, once the new ID token's `iss` and `sub` match the record's; an Android phone takes Google's tokens from `AuthorizationClient` for the record's account, showing Google's consent where Google asks, and checks `sub`; until then the connection's tools ask the attached person or answer `connect_on_device`. |
| D-CONN-13 | §25 | Each token in a connection's record, and a calendar link's secret, is sealed again inside its repo to the ReaderKeys of the member's consented untagged devices that use it, a Google token only to its platform's, and kept sealed by the devices themselves, so a Team's audit reader that holds the repo, another tagged sidecar and a device of another platform open none, the member's agents' enclaves opening theirs (CO-43); when a member leaves or is removed, their devices revoke each connection at its provider from their own copies. |
| D-CONN-14 | §25 | URnetwork's Google clients sit in a production project apart from staging's, as Google requires; the Desktop client's secret, should G-CONN-google find the token endpoint needs it, ships in the signed policy from URnetwork's vault, never a repository; the project's Calendar quota is raised ahead of use and watched in its aggregates; a provider's refusal of the client itself suspends that service's connections without asking anyone to reconnect, until a runbook's new client ships by policy. |
| D-LSTN-1 | §26 | A device lists to the network what a client could reach at its overlay address or a name: sockets on every IPv4 interface, maps, forwards, socket names, TLS names and an enclave's SSH server; loopback-only, single-address and IPv6-only binds, the daemon's own listeners and an enclave container's unmapped sockets stay in its person's own view. |
| D-LSTN-2 | §26 | Discovery reads only the OS's socket tables and the device's own bridge state, every 15 s and at a live ask, and never connects to a port; program names and labels are capped at 64 characters and stay their writer's word. |
| D-LSTN-3 | §26 | One `listeners` repo a network, of a kind whose readers are every admitted sidecar and whose writers each write only their own versionless `s/<sidecar_id>`, which no document widens or narrows. |
| D-LSTN-4 | §26 | Every device's list is visible to the whole network; a person's devices publish only once that person has acknowledged `listeners:publish`, again at each new version, and each desktop only once the person has confirmed its own first list on it; tagged sidecars once an Owner or Admin has acknowledged it for the network, by §2.8's `disclosure-ack`, unless the document's `listeners` block leaves them out; a person hides an entry or a device, an opt-out the listeners rule honors. |
| D-LSTN-5 | §26 | The `listener:` resource with `dial` opens each listed `socket` and `map` entry of the subjects named, checked by the host against the set it last published; the implicit document carries it for tagged sources while the network's acknowledgment of `listeners:publish` stands, and Team's starting document and every new document for every client; it never opens a forward, rule 0's listeners, a `shared` port or a share's source. |
| D-LSTN-6 | §26 | Each entry's badge is the viewer's own evaluation of the host's rules with itself as the source, from the rows and the host's list; it changes nothing, and the host's hook decides every flow. |
| D-LSTN-7 | §26 | `LISTENERS` and `LISTENERS_RESULT` (0x1901, 0x1902) ride the control class: any admitted sidecar of the network asks, at most once in 10 s, and own-view and hidden entries go only to the host's person's own devices. |
| D-LSTN-8 | §26 | `listeners_list` is R in the local and enclave profiles and through MCP, other devices' words as capped tokens between untrusted-data markers without taint, their free text only with `untrusted: include`, which taints first, and opening an entry stays an ordinary dial under the ACL, with no new outward kind. |
| D-LSTN-9 | §26 | "Map it" runs `ur bridge expose` on the enclave over its sponsor's own confirmed `root` session, so the enclave signs the map as its host and its `expose` request waits for the sponsor's approval; the map ends with its incarnation. |
| D-LSTN-10 | §26 | A flow the listeners rule admits is delivered through the host's `ur tun` from the source's overlay address where it runs (`Deliver`), else to a non-loopback address of the host, never at `127.0.0.1`; a port a second socket binds on a narrower address admits none; a removal reaches the hook at discovery, before the next publish. |
| D-SAFE-1 | §27 | Once a person has connected a service, every `service_call` from a run that has read nothing untrusted is R or W, sends and calls the definition does not classify included, recorded and rate-limited, with no approval; in a tainted run its writes and sends are kind 26. |
| D-SAFE-2 | §27 | In auto mode, the default, the device's safety classifier decides first the approvals that exist only because a run is tainted: kind 23 on a site the member has used, kind 24 into the member's own enclaves, kind 25's batches without attendees on an unshared calendar, and kind 26's classified writes; it allows when nothing it reads scores at the threshold and no rule of §27.7 holds, and otherwise the person decides; every other approval, and every act that is the person's own, stays with a person. |
| D-SAFE-3 | §27 | The classifier is Llama Prompt Guard 2, the 22M on phones and the 86M on desktops, Macs and enclaves, at int8, run by a reduced ONNX Runtime in the engine process or the app's `SidecarSafetyClassifierHost`, or in an enclave's daemon outside the agents' container; it ships with each release, its files, thresholds and switch pinned in the signed manifest, and a device that cannot run it asks. |
| D-SAFE-4 | §27 | It reads every input that tainted the run and the action's text, each alone in 512-token windows, raw and normalized, the person's own requests serving only to name known destinations and to exempt their own words; it answers allow or ask with a reason and the highest score, allowing under a calibrated threshold whose default is 0.20; hidden characters ask, and so does a run whose tainting inputs the daemon never saw. |
| D-SAFE-5 | §27 | §27.7's rules always ask, a destination becoming known only through the person or an untainted run; at most 10 automatic approvals a run, 3 a minute and 50 a day on a device; one ask or decline ends auto for the run and its continuations; the agent learns no verdict. |
| D-SAFE-6 | §27 | An automatic approval is an `ApprovalDecision` at version 3, channel 4 `auto`, with `auto` (15) set and `auto_verdict` (16), signed by the requesting sidecar's identity key under `auto_ok`, spendable only by it and never at a gate or for a grant, beside `CanonicalAction` version 5's field 70, `AutoFields{basis, rules}`, on kinds 23-26; every verdict in auto mode is a kind-56 `auto_verdict` entry, journaled before the effect, with its inputs' hashes; every surface renders it as automatic, never as the person's, and the apps show a daily digest. |
| D-SAFE-7 | §27 | The person's `approvals` harness config key, `auto` by default and `ask` for every kind or per kind, written only by their own act; the network's `compute.approvals` narrows the kinds, and an evidence list without `auto` forces `ask`. |
| D-SAFE-8 | §27 | The disclosure `approvals:auto` asks before the first automatic approval, says that the check can be wrong and what it may let through, and shows on each automatic approval's note, in the digest and in the settings. |

## Appendix B. Question register

Every Q- item, 185 in all, each answered (CO-14). An answer stands as the design unless its decider overrides it.

| Id | § | Question | Answer | Decider |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q-CCTX-1 | §1 | Does compute ship to personal networks, Team networks, or both? | (a). The compute balance is per network, and a personal network is a network; Team adds budgets per member (§16.4) and billing admins (§9.10). | owner, confirmed (CO-42) |
| Q-CCTX-2 | §1 | Is compute part of a tier? | (a). A prepaid balance carries its own fraud limits (§9.11), local inference is free (CO-9), and gating by tier would push a free user who only wants a TEE model into a subscription they do not need. Only the number of enclaves a network may run at once scales with its tier (§11.13). | owner, confirmed (CO-42) |
| Q-CTRUST-1 | §2 | Is an acknowledgment kept per network or once per person? | (a). The vault and its harness config are per network, and DESIGN keeps no store across a person's networks; CO-26 treats each network as one person or entity, whose policy may allow different providers, so its member reads and acknowledges there. A person in two networks acknowledges in each. | owner |
| Q-CTRUST-2 | §2 | Should the broker refuse a call or a search whose disclosure the person has not acknowledged? | (a). The acknowledgments are sealed in the person's vault, which no server reads, so the broker could check only a flag the device sets, which a modified client sets as easily as it skips the prompt. The check protects the person from surprise, which only the person's own device can do; it does not protect URnetwork from the device. | peer review |
| Q-CTRUST-3 | §2 | May a tagged or cloud sidecar, which reads no vault, use what needs a disclosure, such as a CI runner calling an engy model? | (c), decided by the owner (CO-41): an Owner's or Admin's acknowledgment, kept in the network's `compute` block, covers the network's tagged and cloud sidecars, enclaves keeping their sponsor's; the admin sees the disclosure text before accepting for them. §2.8 carries it: the signed statement, who may make it, where it is checked, what each such sidecar's card shows, and how a new version asks the admin again without stopping work. | owner, decided (CO-41) |
| Q-PROV-1 | §4 | What if SN64 has not enabled gamma by M12's entry? | decided by the owner (CO-32): "Any provider that does not accept gamma at launch will be dropped from launch." So (a): Chutes, and with it every TEE model, is out of the launch unless SN64 takes gamma by then, and joins when it does; (b) and (c) are not taken. (d) is asked of SayGM now, since SayGM is paid in SN28 gamma: the device would verify Chutes' instance evidence and encrypt to it as §6.6 does, SayGM's gateway and miner would carry only ciphertext, and the label would stay Chutes' AP with SayGM outside the boundary; it needs SayGM to build the pass-through and Chutes to consent to the resale in writing. URnetwork asks Chutes for gamma now, with the E6 agreement, since Chutes was reported among the seven initial gamma issuers (2026-09-28). | owner, decided |
| Q-PROV-2 | §4 | Is AP acceptable for enclaves? | (a). A miner, the anonymous party, stays outside the boundary under AP; the provider company inside it is a named business, as a cloud is. The label shows wherever an enclave is shown, a network can require A1 (§16.4), and the provisioning protocol is the A1 one (§11.7), so a provider that meets the contract later moves an enclave to A1 with no change but its label. | owner, confirmed (CO-35) |
| Q-PROV-3 | §4 | May remote inference run at AP, where the provider itself is trusted? | (b). Chutes is AP (its serving code and tenant image are unmeasured and its platform releases disk keys), and no Bittensor provider reaches A1, so (a) means no TEE inference at all. Under (b) the miners, the anonymous parties, stay outside; Chutes, a named company with a DPA, is trusted as a cloud is; the label says so on every message; and a network that will not trust a provider sets its floor to A1 (§16.4) and uses local models. **This is the owner's call: CO-2 says "TEE", and AP is a TEE that excludes the miner but not the provider.** | owner, confirmed (CO-35) |
| Q-PROV-4 | §4 | What would move Chutes to A1? | the chute's image digest and serving code bound into the evidence (its issue #75: a measured RTMR3, or a signed image digest the per-VM certificate carries), single-tenant VMs or a per-tenant key, and a disk key released by measurement rather than by Chutes' platform. G-PROV-any re-checks it every 90 days, and URnetwork asks for it with the E6 agreement. | peer review |
| Q-PROV-5 | §4 | Does the catalog take inference providers off Bittensor (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, OpenRouter)? | (a). CO-1 names Bittensor providers and CO-10 pays them in gamma; frontier models reachable through a Bittensor provider come in under that provider's terms (§4.4). A provider off Bittensor would need the direct path (N1) and USD payment, which is Later. | owner, confirmed (CO-42) |
| Q-PROV-6 | §4 | Should engy's calls always carry its `zdr` flag? | yes. It sends them only to engy's confidential-computing workers or engy's own machines, whose non-retention is more than an operator's promise, at the cost of a 503 when none is free; the policy's `direct` line (§5.4), not the unsigned catalog, marks the one model without ZDR workers (qwen3.6-35b-a3b), which the router sends without the flag, labeled so, and requires zero retention of every other, so a breached broker cannot drop the flag; the device checks each receipt's `served.zdr` (§6.6). | peer review |
| Q-PROV-7 | §4 | CO-18 says "all inference": should Claude, GPT and Gemini through SayGM be in the catalog? | (a). SayGM's miners serve them with their own keys, which Anthropic's, OpenAI's and Google's terms bar reselling, and SayGM's own terms bar circumventing provider policies, so URnetwork would resell a chain each link of which forbids it; frontier models can come in when one of those providers, or a Bittensor provider holding their written approval, offers them. | owner, confirmed (CO-35) |
| Q-PROV-8 | §4 | Should SayGM's `-tee` models be labeled AP, since its gateway is attested? | (a). The device can verify the gateway: its quote passes Intel's checks against current collateral, and a static quote and a CAA pin tie its TLS certificate to it. But the gateway's code is private, so what reads a request inside it is unknown; the miner's CVM and the model's TEE read it too, their evidence never reaches the client, and the client's nonce stops at the gateway; and the gateway alone decides when a `-TEE` request goes to Chutes' plain API. An end-to-end pass-through (Q-PROV-1 (d)) reaches AP without trusting any of them. | peer review |
| Q-PROV-9 | §4 | Until SayGM signs usage per request, should URnetwork use it through one hotkey per network, billing each network from its hotkey's `/balance`? | (a). Every mint and spend is a chain event under its hotkey, so per-network hotkeys would publish each network's spending as a series anyone can read, undoing the pooling behind URnetwork's hotkey (§10); each would cost a mint; and a modified client could still buy models URnetwork excludes (Q-PROV-7), since nothing bounds the model a body names. | owner |
| Q-PROV-10 | §4 | CO-28 chooses SayGM: may it serve users before it signs usage per request, on the usage its device reports, checked against SayGM's public settlement records? | (a). The device would report SayGM's request id, which those records list but bind to no buyer, so a modified client could cite a cheaper request from the same seconds and URnetwork would pay the difference, with nothing to show which network did it; and with no allowlist the same client could buy, on URnetwork's hotkey, the frontier models Q-PROV-7 excludes. engy carries the launch, with Chutes once SN64 takes gamma (CO-32), while SayGM adds the two features G-PROV-saygm names. | owner, confirmed (CO-35) |
| Q-ATTEST-1 | §5 | Per-device nonces or beacon nonces? | (c). Per-device nonces are simplest and enough at launch's volume; the beacon keeps the same freshness bound at any scale, and enclaves, provisioned once each, keep their own nonces. | peer review |
| Q-ATTEST-2 | §5 | NRAS or a local GPU verifier? | (a) when the Chutes path ships, (b) once GPU enclaves need the local verifier, both in M15 (§19.3). NRAS's answer is signed, so the broker cannot forge it; a local verifier removes NVIDIA's view of which GPUs URnetwork uses and a service dependency, but there is no Go implementation to start from. | peer review |
| Q-ATTEST-3 | §5 | How long is a pass trusted? | 10 minutes per instance and key: long enough that a conversation's turns reuse one check, short enough that an instance withdrawn or a key rotated is noticed within the window, and a re-check costs one fetch. | peer review |
| Q-ATTEST-4 | §5 | Who may sign the policy? | (b). The policy changes about weekly, as providers roll images and texts change, and carries a sitting's tickets each week (5.4); DESIGN keeps the offline two-person release key for promotions because its ceremony cannot gate a pipeline that runs that often (owner decision 264), and providers' rolls would otherwise wait on it, TEE calls failing closed meanwhile. Devices still pin the one root and check the certificate's namespace and expiry, and two signers still sign each version, so no one person or server can widen the policy. | owner, confirmed (CO-42) |
| Q-ATTEST-5 | §5 | Who holds the unreleased freshness tickets, and how far ahead are they signed? | (b). The unreleased tickets are the very capability a revocation must defeat: under (a) whoever takes the releasing host holds up to 90 days of them and keeps a revoked profile or chip passing that long; (c) needs two signers every day; (b) bounds the worst case at 14 days, and at 72 hours unless the separate ticket host falls too, for one sitting a week. | owner, confirmed (CO-42) |
| Q-INFER-1 | §6 | Does a local model that fails or lacks memory fall back to a remote one? | (a). Local is free and private; remote costs money and leaves the device. The Harness offers the switch and the person chooses (CO-9, CO-11). | owner |
| Q-INFER-2 | §6 | What if a LiteRT-LM release breaks a platform? | (a), with llama.cpp through yzma as a desktop-only fallback engine behind the same interface if a regression outlasts one release cycle. | peer review |
| Q-INFER-3 | §6 | Is the cache salt per network, per member or per run? | per member on the TEE path: it blocks other customers of the provider and other members of a Team alike, while a member's own runs keep their cache hits; per run on the direct path, whose provider reads the salt in plaintext, where a member's salt would link all of that member's conversations. On the TEE path only Chutes' code inside the boundary reads the salt, and AP already trusts it with the plaintext, so the link it gives Chutes is disclosed (§2.8) rather than paid for in cache misses. | peer review |
| Q-INFER-4 | §6 | Embeddings? | Later. No TEE provider offers embedding models (Chutes' catalog had none on 2026-11-23); DESIGN's search runs without them. | peer review |
| Q-INFER-5 | §6 | When a canonical name carries an effort and the request asks for another, which wins? | the name: it is the person's choice in a harness's settings, so Codex's and Claude Code's own effort settings change nothing for a full name; a request names the alias without the effort to let its own parameter decide (6.3). | peer review |
| Q-INFER-6 | §6 | Should a name let URnetwork pick the provider, as `any-<model>-<effort>` routed to the cheapest allowed one? | not at launch: CO-18 puts the provider in the name, so the person always knows who serves a model; an `any` provider is Later, and would choose only among providers the person's floor and list allow. | owner |
| Q-INFER-7 | §6 | One disclosure per provider, or one per model? | (a). The exposure follows the provider and its label: who reads a request, under which terms; and one acknowledgment per provider keeps the prompts few. Where a model differs, the provider's text says so, as engy's names its one model without zero-retention workers and SayGM's points to the upstream the signed policy names for each model; a provider whose models differ more gets an id per group. | peer review |
| Q-HARN-1 | §7 | Fork PiG or reimplement? | (b), for 7.3's reasons. | owner |
| Q-HARN-2 | §7 | Does the local Harness get web access? | (b): CO-17 asks for a core fetch tool and CO-16 for search, so the local profile gets both (§21, §22), through URnetwork's network, under the listed-URL rule and taint. | owner |
| Q-HARN-3 | §7 | May a local Harness run on the page Worker or the extension? | not at launch: the extension's Worker is Later in DESIGN, and the page Worker has no compute surface; remote-only Harness in the browser follows the Worker. | owner |
| Q-HARN-4 | §7 | What runs by default in an enclave? | (a): it records natively and its tool and approval rules are sidecar's; PiG is one flag away for people who want Pi's extensions and TUI. | owner |
| Q-HARN-5 | §7 | How does a local Harness reach several agents in one enclave? | (b), with threads beside it for work that outlives the link. (a) spends an SSH session per agent against §12.4's 16 a client, and can neither list agents nor launch one; (c) cannot steer, abort or show a run as it happens. One link carries control and the live view, and each prompt's thread carries the answer, which survives a dropped link or a sleeping phone. | owner |
| Q-HARN-6 | §7 | How does the remote side know whether a command on the link is trusted? | (b). (a) lets a tainted run on the person's own device carry injected text into an enclave agent's trusted context, past I-9; (c) taints every run the person drives by hand and costs it its outward actions, though the person typed the prompt. (b) is D-SKILL-4's rule for messages applied to the link, so since CO-43 an untainted run in another of the sponsor's enclaves counts as one on their device (IC-12). Signing over the exchange hash keeps an origin from moving to another session or being chosen by a line's writer, and keeps OpenSSH sessions, which `ur ssh agent` lets any same-user process open, from carrying one; a same-user process that detaches from its harness and drives a pty can still pass as the person, DESIGN's TB1 residual (owner decision 47), which §2.7 discloses. | peer review |
| Q-HARN-7 | §7 | Is a tainted run's prompt into an enclave an outward action? | (b), as kind 24, `tainted_send`, for every tool that carries text there, `agent_send` and `agent_broadcast` included. A receiver's taint stops nothing in an enclave, whose `bash` reaches the internet outside the gate (DESIGN §16.6), so the gate must be the sender's. An enclave whose egress is `none` sends nothing to the internet itself, unless a rule lets it dial another device's services, which can act on the internet for it, so such an enclave counts as reaching out (7.8, §26.7); and it writes into the network (deposits, the agents repo, the repos it syncs): its runs that took the prompt are tainted, so their sends onward pass the same gate, kept by a Harness outside its agents' container (§11.10), and what they write waits behind 7.8's hold before an enclave that reaches the internet reads it, so (c) would cost approvals for nothing the hold does not already cover. One kind for every tool and command that messages, runs a command or moves a context, and no evs or git write into an inbox, leaves a tainted run no messaging door. | owner |
| Q-HARN-8 | §7 | Does a remote agent's answer taint the local run that reads it, even from an untainted run in an enclave whose egress is `none`? | (b) for the member's own enclave, as CO-43 has it, and (a) for another member's. The member's enclave is one of their devices, whose Harness keeps each run's taint in the daemon's namespaces, outside the agents' container, where no agent can clear it (§11.10), so its untainted runs are trusted as a desktop's are; most of its runs are tainted anyway, since every tool that touches the container taints its run (7.8), and their answers taint the reader. Another member's enclave is another member's device, whose runs taint as any other member's (IC-12). A managing agent stays useful because it need not read: `harness_list`'s stubs do not taint, events go to the person's view rather than its context, threads bring the answer when it is needed, and the person's own prompts never wait for approval. | owner |
| Q-HARN-9 | §7 | May an enclave's agent manage another enclave's Harness, and a member another member's? | (b) within a member, and another member's enclave only with its sponsor's consent. Within a member, managing is the `ssh` action (§16.2): the default rule reaches a member's enclaves from that member's untagged devices and the agents on them (§16.5), so one enclave reaches another only by a rule naming both (`tag:enclave-<a>` to `tag:enclave-<b>`). Another member's enclave holds its sponsor's owner-bound agent record, its agents' status, summaries and conversations (owner decision 126), so a rule an admin writes is not enough: the sponsor's consented device approves a requested `ssh` grant naming the other member (`autogroup:dst-owner`, DESIGN §8.8), which the enclave's SSH server checks; with it the other member may list, prompt, steer, wait on and stop the enclave's agents but never launch one, since `ur_launch_agent` takes only the sponsor's origins, and its prompts, steers and stops spend the sponsor's budget. Either way its commands arrive untrusted (Q-HARN-6), from a tainted run into an enclave that reaches the internet they wait for approval (Q-HARN-7), and a report back to another member's agent is kind 24 from the enclave's run, so the skill has such agents report once, at the end. Since CO-43 the enclave holds what its sponsor's devices hold, so such a grant never reaches `root` (§12.5), and what another member's command has a run there read of the sponsor's reaches that member only by the sponsor's kind 24, which the classifier never decides for another member (7.8, §27.7). | owner |
| Q-HARN-10 | §7 | May a tainted run's EVS writes reach an enclave that reaches the internet with no person's act, and should an enclave's agents read every summary of their member's agents? | (b) for the first; for the second, since CO-43 makes the enclave one of its sponsor's devices, its agents read the agents repo, summaries included, as the member's other agents do (§20.4), a summary a tainted run wrote waiting behind the hold like any other version. Kind 24 exists because a receiver's taint stops nothing in an enclave that reaches the internet, and the same holds for what it reads from EVS; the local Harness keeps everything in EVS (CO-6), so a summary a mail-reading run wrote is the common path, not a corner. Holding only tainted runs' versions leaves untainted work flowing, while (c) would break the agent graph and the management of CO-19 and CO-23. | owner |
| Q-HARN-11 | §7 | Once an enclave holds its sponsor's data (CO-43), may one run there both read it and use the agents' container, whose `bash` reaches the internet? | (b). In an enclave that reaches out, a prompt-injected agent's `bash` sends whatever its run holds outside every gate, so under (a) one injected message could send the person's mail, accounts and record anywhere, past every approval; (c) would take from such an enclave the mail, calendars and connections CO-42 shares with it. (b) keeps both: mail and accounts work in runs that never touch the container, under the local profile's gates (7.8), and builds, root and the internet in runs that never read them, as before CO-43; a run that needs both asks the person once, and a crossing's card shows what the run holds. Repos other than the vault and the mailbox stay readable by the container's runs, as CO-43's full access has it for the initial version, which the enclave's disclosure says (§2.8). | owner |
| Q-GW-1 | §8 | CO-4 says "responses api"; is that the only API? | (b), as 8.3 shows: Claude Code speaks only Messages, and most open harnesses speak Chat Completions. | owner |
| Q-GW-2 | §8 | Cursor? | (a): Cursor's custom endpoints are called from Cursor's servers, which would see every prompt, and the gateway would have to be public. | owner |
| Q-GW-3 | §8 | Gemini CLI? | (a); a fourth translation for one harness waits for demand. | owner |
| Q-GW-4 | §8 | May the gateway forward to the person's own API keys for OpenAI, Anthropic or Google? | (a). CO-18 brings every provider URnetwork can reach into its catalog, paid from the compute balance under one namespace; a person's own keys are a separate matter, and a harness that wants them keeps its own provider settings beside the gateway's profile. | owner |
| Q-GW-5 | §8 | Does the gateway run in the apps? | (a): phones run no external harness, and the apps' Harness calls the router in-process. An enclave runs it so Codex, Claude Code or PiG inside the enclave use the catalog (§11.10). | owner |
| Q-GW-6 | §8 | How does a harness that takes its API key from a file or its environment, with no credential command to renew it (most Chat Completions harnesses, [Rpt:bb] gateway_harness_compat.md), keep working past a token's hour? | (b). (a) leaves a long-lived credential on disk, past IC-11's hour; (c) breaks every session at the hour. Under (b) no credential reaches a file, the runner keeps §8.7's loopback, Host and Origin checks, its key ends with the process, and the grant, budget and recording are the harness's own, as for Codex and Claude Code; `ur gateway config <h>` prints this form for such a harness. | owner |
| Q-BAL-1 | §9 | What does "auto renew" mean? | (c), with threshold on the web only, since the App Store and Google Play sell no off-session consumable, and the monthly grant on every market as a subscription. | owner, confirmed (CO-35) |
| Q-BAL-2 | §9 | What markup does compute carry over the provider's gamma price? | (b) 1.20 on every model and shape. It covers Stripe's ~3%, the TAO purchase and mint (§10.6, about 1-3%), broker bandwidth, refunds and fraud, and leaves a margin; one number keeps the catalog explainable. The owner sets the number; 1.20 stands until then. | owner, confirmed (CO-35) |
| Q-BAL-3 | §9 | Do store purchases give fewer credits per dollar, or cost more? | (a): a credit is always one dollar of compute, so the balance means one thing everywhere; the store product costs more, at the price tier that nets the web price after the commission URnetwork pays there: 15% in the stores' small-business programs and for a subscription past its first year, else 30%, and where a store's rules allow a link to web checkout (the US App Store since the 2025 ruling), the app offers it. | owner, confirmed (CO-35) |
| Q-BAL-4 | §9 | Do credits expire? | (a) for purchased and subscription credits; promotions expire in 30 days. Expiry rules for prepaid value vary by state and invite disputes, and a dollar balance that never expires is the simplest promise. | owner, confirmed (CO-35) |
| Q-BAL-5 | §9 | Who may buy credits in a Team network? | (a), with `compute:buy` in the policy (§16.2) to let members buy for the network. | owner, confirmed (CO-42) |
| Q-BAL-6 | §9 | May the crypto rails (Gamma on SN25, TAO, the coins, x402) fund the compute balance? | (a) at launch, as CO-10 says fiat; x402, which lets an agent pay for itself, is the first candidate later because it keeps the rail where agents already are. | owner, confirmed (CO-42) |
| Q-BAL-7 | §9 | What happens to a running enclave when the balance runs out? | (b), 9.9's floor and one hour, then stop; its work is in EVS, and it starts again as a new incarnation once the balance allows. | owner |
| Q-BAL-8 | §9 | Which days are the spend view's "last 7 days", and in which time zone? | (a). `compute_charge_day`, the statements and DESIGN's daily quotas (DESIGN §20.4) all count UTC days, so the view and a statement agree; a network's zone would be one more fact on the server that hints where its people are, and a Team's members span zones; (c) would read the per-request rows on every view. The view says "UTC", and the apps show the window's bounds in the person's local time beside it. | owner |
| Q-BAL-9 | §9 | Are the spend view's figures exact or estimates? | (a). `compute_settle` adds each charge to its day and lifetime rows in the transaction that writes it, so every figure is the sum of its charges to the nano-USD, seconds behind; a hold is a worst case (9.7), not a cost, so (b) would overstate, and the view shows holds apart; (c) would hide today's spend, the spend a person most often asks about. | peer review |
| Q-BAL-10 | §9 | Where are lifetime totals kept, for how long, and at what grain? | (a), deleted with the network. CO-22 asks for a total, which (b) cannot give past 400 days; (c) would keep for the account's life when each sidecar used which model, which 9.4 bounds at 400 days on purpose; (d) would have each viewer's devices keep their own fold without a gap, a member's unable to read an admin's, for figures the server derives from charges it holds anyway; (a) keeps only how much each member spent on each model or shape, and one date, the network's first charge, which is all the view shows. It keeps no agent: an agent's id names one device's agent (DESIGN §5.5), so a lifetime row by agent would be a device's lifetime spend, and agent ids churn with every sub-agent and enclave incarnation, so such rows would grow without end; by agent, the view covers the last 7 days and statements their months. | owner |
| Q-BAL-11 | §9 | May the person's own bot read the spend view? | (b). "Where did my credits go?" is a question for the bot tab (CO-19); the view holds figures and the device's labels, never content (R-BAL-6), less than the mail and vault the same agent may already read, and the sidecar calls the route, so no credential enters the agent's context (I-7). (c) would give agents on tagged sidecars, which act for no one person, and in enclaves, which run on machines others hold (§2.6), a view no role of theirs grants; an untagged CI runner or server, enrolled by an auth key that acts as its creator (DESIGN §7.8), is such a machine too, so (b) asks for the person's consented device, untagged and neither ephemeral nor Delegation-admitted, not merely an untagged one. Charge rows, lots and payment methods stay out of every agent's reach. | owner |
| Q-BAL-12 | §9 | Where does a refunded charge show in the spend view? | (b), each service's line saying "after $x refunded" where it has refunds. A refund is a negative charge of the kind it returns, carrying that charge's member, agent, model, provider and enclave (9.6), so each service's figure is what its credits bought, every figure is still a plain sum of its kinds' rows, as statements and reconciliation (§10.7) count them, and Adjustments keeps support credits and debits, which name no charge. (a) would show a charge an upheld dispute refunds as remote inference spent, its refund on another line and perhaps another day; (c) would leave a refunded charge counted as spent. | peer review |
| Q-BAL-13 | §9 | Are credits sold before anything can spend them, as at an M12 exit where no inference provider has passed its gate (Chutes without gamma, CO-32; engy or SayGM without the features their gates name)? | (b). Credit that nothing can spend brings refunds and support work, and an app store expects what an app sells to be usable in it; local inference is free (CO-9), so the bot tab is useful before any credit. The ledger and the store products still ship and pass review in M12, closed, and open the day a gate passes. | owner, confirmed (CO-41) |
| Q-BAL-14 | §9 | While no provider without a TEE enforces a bound the broker signs, what does a direct call hold? | (b). Under CO-32 the direct path is the only remote path at launch, and (a) would refuse a session's second call for balance while it had cost cents; (b) risks at most $5 a network, and only from a device that lies about its model, which is charged in full, flagged and, at a second mismatch in 30 days, loses its direct calls (9.11); the packs start at 10 credits (9.5). | owner, confirmed (CO-42) |
| Q-BAL-15 | §9 | Do purchases have a daily limit after a network's first week, and do limits follow the payer as well as the network? | (b). §10.8's closed-loop argument cites a daily limit under $2,000, which only (b) designs; networks are free, so limits per network alone reset with each one a fraudster makes, while a card's fingerprint or an App Store account follows the money. | owner, confirmed (CO-42) |

| Q-GAMMA-2 | §10 | Who custodies the reserve? | (a): an exchange or custodian cannot sign `mint_gamma`, and the owners already run a Ledger multisig for SN25. | owner, confirmed (CO-35) |
| Q-GAMMA-3 | §10 | How often does the treasury buy? | weekly, sized to the next week's forecast plus the 7-day float, so price exposure stays near a week of spend. | owner, confirmed (CO-35) |
